systems.name: Orion System
systems.desc: The Orion system is the political and corporate centre of the known galaxy, five worlds across every stage of construction, ruin, and ambition. Home to the Galactic Union and the ghost of OrionWorks, the organisation that built artificial planets and may have started the Tronik War. It is heavily defended, intensely surveilled, and the kind of place where what you know and who you know matters more than what you can do.

planets.name: Orion 1
planets.type: Space Station, Major Spaceport & Trade Hub
planets.atm_note: Maintained throughout commercial sections, outer salvaged ring retains hard vacuum in unrepaired zones
planets.grav_note: Artificial gravity throughout commercial core, patchy in outer salvaged sections
planets.population: ~850,000 permanent staff, transit crews and traders
planets.demographics: Highly mixed, all races, heavy transient population, significant Non-Born labour presence
planets.government: GU Spaceport Authority (civilian) / Alliance Navy Garrison Command (military)
planets.economy: Interstellar trade, cargo transit, warehousing, ship servicing, military logistics
planets.access_note: Open entry with standard Alliance ID check. GU Archive section requires Level 2 clearance. Military substations are restricted.
hazards: Structural mismatch, old salvaged frames next to new construction create unpredictable load stress
Vacuum exposure in outer ring sections not yet repaired
Crowding and crime in the commercial transit zones
Intelligence operations from multiple factions, the volume of trade makes surveillance difficult to avoid

notable_locations.name: Commercial Transit Core
notable_locations.desc: The beating heart of Orion 1's trade operation. Multiple docking arms, warehousing, traders and brokers operating day-cycle around the clock. The busiest single transit point in the Orion system.

notable_locations.name: Military Substations (Network)
notable_locations.desc: The Alliance navy operates a distributed network of substations throughout the station's structure, each positioned to control approach vectors into the system. Well-armed, permanently staffed, and not welcoming to casual visitors.

notable_locations.name: GU Historical Archive
notable_locations.desc: One of the original founding modules, preserved in place amid the commercial sprawl that grew up around it. The Galactic Union charter was signed here. Access Level 2. Some records are restricted with no explanation on file.

notable_locations.name: The Salvaged Ring
notable_locations.desc: The outer sections never rebuilt after materials were stripped for the artificial world projects. Some corridors are hard vacuum. Others have been squatted by traders who prefer not to be registered. The GU Spaceport Authority maintains minimal presence here.

hooks: It is widely known among freight brokers that cargo manifests at Orion 1 routinely list consignees that cannot be verified, a practice so common that customs staff treat it as standard rather than suspicious. Experienced traders say the real consignee is never the registered one.

Scholars studying the original GU charter have long noted that access records for the Historical Archive do not correlate with any documented visitor logs, suggesting routine off-record access by parties whose identities are deliberately excluded from the official register.

Station workers who have served long rotations at Orion 1 say the military substations conduct silent lockdowns periodically with no prior notice and no explanation filed afterward. The practice is so well-established that the civilian staff have developed their own informal warning system to avoid being caught in restricted corridors.
planets.desc: Orion 1 is one of the largest spaceport structures in Alliance Space, and one of the most visibly incomplete. When the GU began construction of the artificial worlds that followed, vast sections of the original station were stripped for materials and never replaced. What grew in their place is a sprawling, partially-rebuilt trade hub handling traffic from across the Orion system and beyond: warehousing, transit facilities, commercial districts, and a dense network of military substations installed by the Alliance navy to defend the system's primary entry point. The station is loud, busy, and structurally mismatched, new construction built directly against stripped-out frames, some corridors unpressurised, others running at full capacity. The GU historical archive sits in one of the original founding modules, carefully preserved amid the commercial noise of everything built around it.

planets.name: Orion 2
planets.atm_note: Core collapsed, no breathable zones remain
planets.grav_note: Fragmented mass, gravitational field unstable and unpredictable
planets.access_note: Active navigational hazard, approach prohibited within 200km
hazards: Gravitational instability, unpredictable micro-gravity wells
High-velocity debris field
No rescue capability within effective range
Electromagnetic interference from core remnants

notable_locations.name: Construction Core Remnant
notable_locations.desc: The original structural skeleton of the failed planet. Partially accessible by skilled pilots but structurally unpredictable. The GU uses it as a cautionary case study in engineering schools.

hooks: Salvagers who have worked the Orion 2 debris field consistently report instrument readings suggesting a power source somewhere in the core remnant, something that should have died with the structure and apparently has not. The GU has never acknowledged these reports.

It is a persistent story among debris field workers that ships sometimes return from the Orion 2 exclusion zone without all the crew that went in. The story is old enough and consistent enough that most veteran salvagers treat it as established fact rather than rumour.

Engineering academics have noted for decades that the GU's official explanation for the Orion 2 failure is inconsistent with the structural data that has been made public. The leading alternative theory among specialists is deliberate sabotage, possibly internal, that the GU has never been willing to investigate openly.
planets.desc: Orion 2 was the Galactic Union's first attempt to build a planet from scratch, ambitious, technically groundbreaking, and ultimately a failure. Structural instability in the core design made the world uninhabitable and increasingly dangerous. Rather than write off the investment, the Union stripped it completely, salvaged every usable component, and used what they learned to design Orion 3. Nothing remains except navigational hazard markers and the most expensive lesson in the galaxy's history.

planets.name: Orion 3
planets.atm_note: Fully engineered, maintained at precise composition
planets.grav_note: Artificially generated and maintained, highly stable
planets.demographics: Mixed, all playable races, heavily cosmopolitan
planets.economy: Administration, finance, corporate HQ, legal services, high-end manufacturing
planets.access_note: Visitor permits mandatory, background checks standard. Certain districts require additional clearance.
hazards: Pervasive surveillance, assume all public conversations monitored
Corporate espionage operations constant, multiple competing cells active
Political intrigue, wrong associations can end careers or lives
Security forces react fast and with lethal force

notable_locations.name: GU Senate Chambers
notable_locations.desc: The central legislative body of the Galactic Union. Open sessions attended by representatives from every member system. The real decisions are made elsewhere.

notable_locations.name: Central Treasury
notable_locations.desc: The financial heart of the GU. Manages the largest reserve of credits and physical assets in the galaxy. Effectively impregnable.

notable_locations.name: Corporate Quarter
notable_locations.desc: The district where every major corporation maintains its primary GU offices. Heavily policed, intensely political. The density of power here is difficult to overstate.

notable_locations.name: The Understrata
notable_locations.desc: The lower levels of Orion 3, maintenance corridors and service infrastructure housing the city's underclass. Off the tourist maps but very much part of the economy.

hooks: The Central Archive on Orion 3 is believed by investigators and financial analysts to hold records of every major corporate transaction in the past two centuries that the GU officially denies retaining. Anomalies in publicly accessible financial histories can only be explained by the existence of such records, and the GU has never provided an alternative explanation.

It is a well-established pattern among Orion 3 traders and couriers that certain GU senators maintain off-manifest freight operations through the station's commercial core. The contents are never discussed and the destinations are never the same twice, but the practice is consistent enough to have its own informal name in the freight community.

Career diplomats and GU intelligence analysts who have served on Orion 3 for long periods speak privately of colleagues who raised questions about Orion 4 and subsequently disappeared from official personnel records, not transferred, not retired, simply absent from any system that can be checked.
planets.desc: Orion 3 is proof that the Galactic Union learns from its failures. Built using everything salvaged from Orion 2, it was the first fully successful artificial planet ever constructed and has stood for centuries. The GU operates its core functions here, executive councils, primary treasury, largest corporate campus, and the administrative infrastructure that ties together the most powerful organisation in the known galaxy. The planet is clean, efficient, and extraordinarily dense with power. Every major corporation has an office here. Security is absolute.

planets.name: Orion 4
planets.atm_note: Partial atmosphere remains, most pressurised sections breached. Respirator advised in unpowered zones.
planets.grav_note: Gravity generators still functional in some districts, fails without warning in others
planets.demographics: Mostly human and Non-Born, transient, no reliable census data
planets.government: None, zone-by-zone control by various groups
planets.tech_level: Variable (Cutting-Edge remnants in ruins / Primitive survival conditions in inhabited zones)
planets.economy: Salvage, black market research, off-books operations
planets.access_note: No official entry restrictions but GU patrols question anyone approaching classified research districts.
hazards: Structural collapse, entire districts can depressurise without warning
Gravity field failure zones
Hostile squatter gangs in unstable zones
Unknown activated technology in unsecured OrionWorks facilities
Vacuum exposure in breached sections
Radiation from unshielded power cores

notable_locations.name: OrionWorks Research Campus (Ruins)
notable_locations.desc: The former home of the most technologically advanced research organisation in the galaxy. Most is destroyed. Some is not. What remained in the labs when everyone left is an open question.

notable_locations.name: The Pressurised Zones
notable_locations.desc: Six districts that still maintain atmosphere and gravity. Populated by salvagers, squatters, and people with very good reasons not to be anywhere that has a census.

notable_locations.name: Sector 7 (Classified)
notable_locations.desc: A GU-marked restricted zone in the heart of the former research campus. No public documentation exists on what is there. GU patrols actively redirect anyone approaching it.

hooks: Among salvagers who work Orion 4, it is common knowledge that certain sections of the OrionWorks campus were not destroyed in the Tronik War but were deliberately sealed, and that the GU has quietly maintained that sealing ever since while officially claiming the ruins are simply too dangerous to clear.

The GU maintains an unlisted team on Orion 4 that does not appear in any accessible personnel database. This is known among veteran salvagers and squatter communities who have observed their movements and learned to avoid the districts where they operate.

It is reported by multiple independent sources across decades that something in the ruins of OrionWorks continues to broadcast on communication frequencies that only OrionWorks used, frequencies that have been officially retired and should have no active transmitters. The GU has consistently declined to comment on the reports.
planets.desc: Orion 4 was once the most technologically advanced world in the known galaxy. Home to OrionWorks, it was a world where the future was being built in real time, gleaming infrastructure, cutting-edge research, and the galaxy's brightest minds. Then the Tronik War started. The devastation was near-total. OrionWorks collapsed. Most of its leadership died or disappeared. What remains is a partially demolished world, some districts still pressurised, most open to vacuum, all of it structurally unpredictable. Somewhere in the wreckage, things that were being developed before the war may still be intact. The Union quietly discourages investigation.

planets.name: Orion 5
planets.atm_note: Frame only, no life support infrastructure installed
planets.grav_note: Structural skeleton only, no gravity systems installed
planets.access_note: Construction zone designation, no authorised civilian access. Frame is completely unsecured.
hazards: No life support, full EVA required throughout
Loose construction materials
Structural instability in incomplete sections
Long-term vacuum exposure in all areas

notable_locations.name: Primary Superstructure Hub
notable_locations.desc: The central node of the planetary frame. The engineering work here represents the height of OrionWorks' design capability. Everything connects to this point. Nothing beyond it has ever been installed.

hooks: Among intelligence professionals and certain high-level corporate operatives, Orion 5 has a well-established reputation as the most deniable meeting location in the Orion system, no life support, no surveillance, and total isolation from any observation network. The practice of using it for sensitive meetings is known enough to be considered an open secret in certain circles.

GU procurement analysts have noted that low-volume material orders consistent with Orion 5 construction preparation have appeared in supply chain records intermittently since the project was suspended, never large enough to attract official scrutiny, but consistent enough to suggest someone is maintaining the option to resume.

In the engineering community descended from OrionWorks practitioners, it is widely believed that complete plans for Orion 5 still exist and that the GU has never destroyed them, choosing instead to keep them inaccessible as both an insurance policy and as leverage over anyone who might independently develop the same capability.
planets.desc: Orion 5 exists as a frame. The superstructure is in place, the skeleton of what would have been the most ambitious planetary construction project the GU had ever attempted, designed by OrionWorks at the height of its capability. Then OrionWorks collapsed. The engineers went home or disappeared. The supply chains dried up. That was fifty years ago. Not a single component has been added since. The GU lists it as a suspended project with no scheduled resumption date.

planets.name: Orion Shepherd Belt
planets.grav_note: Aggregate mass negligible, individual bodies range from boulder to 40km diameter
planets.economy: Trace mineral survey activity, no active extraction licensed
planets.access_note: Navigation through the belt is unrestricted but requires piloting clearance. Standard approach corridors are charted and marked.
hazards: High-velocity debris in irregular orbital paths
GU navigation beacons do not cover the inner belt sections
Salvagers operating without licence are periodically encountered
planets.desc: A dense asteroid field occupying the outer orbital band of the Orion system, well beyond the artificial world cluster. Composed primarily of silicate and metallic bodies, it predates OrionWorks construction activity and was left undisturbed when the artificial worlds were built. The GU designates it a navigational caution zone and maintains approach corridor beacons.

planets.name: Orion-G1
planets.atm_note: Hydrogen-helium envelope, no surface, no breathable zones
planets.grav_note: Strong gravitational field, atmospheric drag begins well above visible cloud layer
planets.access_note: Approach unrestricted. No infrastructure.
hazards: Gas giant atmospheric pressure lethal to unshielded vessels below cloud layer
Radiation belts from magnetic field
Strong gravitational gradient
Ring debris field extends several planetary radii from the equatorial plane, approach from the poles recommended
planets.desc: A large banded gas giant in the outer Orion system, designated G1 on GU navigational charts. Distinguished by a prominent ring system of ice and silicate debris, visible from considerable distance and a navigational landmark on approach to the system. The rings are broad but thin, and the amber banding of the planet beneath them makes the combination visually striking. Occasionally used as a gravitational slingshot point by ships on fuel-conserving trajectories. Ring debris fields make equatorial approach inadvisable.

planets.name: Orion-G2
planets.atm_note: Methane-ammonia ice envelope
planets.access_note: Outermost catalogued body. No approach infrastructure.
hazards: Extreme cold, surface equivalent temperatures approach absolute minimum
Methane ice storms in upper atmosphere
Significant distance from any rescue or resupply capability
planets.desc: The outermost body in the Orion system, a dark, methane-blue ice giant sitting at the edge of the star's gravitational influence. GU survey craft have passed it but no permanent observation has been established. Its primary value to navigators is as a distance reference point when plotting inbound approaches.

systems.name: Titania System
systems.desc: The Titania system is defined by morondium, a living crystalline compound found nowhere else in the galaxy that grants metals regenerative properties when infused. Every major corporation wants it. The result is a permanent corporate warzone on Titania 2, overseen by Nova cruisers enforcing a strict ground-combat-only agreement. The phrase "Warrior of Titan" refers to anyone who has served time here, a mark of toughness earned the hard way.

planets.name: Titania Prime
planets.atm_note: Completely destroyed, debris field only
planets.grav_note: Fragmented, residual unstable gravity wells from largest debris masses
planets.access_note: Active navigational hazard, military exclusion zone. Alliance navy enforces standoff.
hazards: High-velocity debris field, extreme navigation hazard
Residual weapons contamination from the corporate war
Unpredictable gravitational micro-wells
Classified: unknown contamination reported in outer debris ring

notable_locations.name: The Graveyard (Inner Ring)
notable_locations.desc: The densest section of the debris field, where the largest planetary fragments cluster. Rich in recoverable materials but extraordinarily dangerous to navigate without specialised equipment.

hooks: Salvagers who work near the Titania Prime debris field consistently report finding objects that are clearly manufactured, not ore, not structural wreckage, in sections of the field that should contain nothing but fragmented planetary matter. The reports are old enough and numerous enough that some veteran salvagers treat constructed objects in the debris as an expected find rather than an anomaly.

Three independent historical analyses conducted across different decades have reached the same conclusion: the destruction of Titania Prime was a deliberate choice by one of the corporate factions, a decision that the other planets be denied rather than contested. No corporation has ever acknowledged this. The Alliance's official position is that the cause remains undetermined.

Navigation crews who make regular runs past the Titania debris field have noted for years that a small shuttle type makes consistent runs into the densest section of the field and emerges on a schedule too precise to be salvage work. Who operates it and what it collects has never been publicly established.
planets.desc: Titania Prime was the largest inhabited world in the system before the morondium wars escalated beyond anyone's ability to control. Nobody claims responsibility for what happened to it. The debris field it left behind is a permanent hazard to navigation and a reminder of what happens when corporate warfare operates without limits. The loss of Titania Prime is directly why the current ground-combat-only agreement was reached, everyone looked at what had been done and understood that without rules, the last morondium world would be next.

planets.name: Titania 2
planets.atm_note: Breathable but heavily polluted in warzone sectors, respirators recommended in combat zones
planets.demographics: Predominantly human, mixed corporate deployments from across known space
planets.government: None, contested control, multi-corporate military administration
planets.economy: Morondium extraction (ongoing despite conflict), military logistics, weapons supply
planets.access_note: Civilian access prohibited. Entry without corporate military credential risks immediate engagement by all parties.
hazards: Active combat operations, all zones contested
Morondium dust inhalation, cumulative neurological toxin
Unexploded ordnance throughout all sectors
Corporate intelligence ops, assume surveillance by multiple parties
Supply interdiction, food and medical resupply are active combat targets

notable_locations.name: The Extraction Zone (Sector 7)
notable_locations.desc: The primary morondium deposit site. Whoever controls this sector controls the only active export point. It changes hands on average twice per week.

notable_locations.name: Forward Operating Bases (Multiple)
notable_locations.desc: Each major corporate faction maintains at least one FOB on Titania 2. Locations shift as territory does. Maps are obsolete within days of issue.

notable_locations.name: The Meatgrinder (Trench Network)
notable_locations.desc: A network of trenches and fortifications in the central plain, established decades ago and never fully abandoned. Some of the oldest sections have become almost permanent infrastructure. Veterans call this place home.

hooks: Cross-faction intelligence leaks are so commonplace on Titania 2 that military analysts consider the information environment effectively transparent, every corporate faction assumes its operational plans are known to at least one rival, and plans accordingly. The result is a war fought less on information advantage than on sheer attrition and willingness to take losses.

The most dangerous regular work available in known space is moving material from forward operating bases to extraction ships on Titania 2, a route that crosses multiple contested sectors and changes weekly as territory shifts. The pay reflects this. So does the casualty rate among contractors who take the work.

It is accepted among morondium researchers as near-certain that secondary deposits exist outside the current warzone boundary, geological surveys support this, but the discovery has never been publicly confirmed because anyone who locates one faces an immediate and non-survivable level of corporate interest.
planets.desc: Titania 2 is the most fought-over piece of ground in the known galaxy. Morondium, a living crystalline compound that grants metals regenerative properties when infused, exists nowhere else. The current state of affairs is a permanent ground war between corporate armies operating under a single enforced rule: no orbital strikes, no bombardment, no weapons of mass destruction. Ground forces only. This rule is enforced by a Yamato-class and a GU Nova cruiser in permanent orbit, each with orders to destroy any fleet that attempts an orbital strike. For players, Titania 2 is hell with a purpose. There is always work here for soldiers, medics, engineers, and people who can get things across active fire zones.

planets.name: Titania 4
planets.atm_note: Clean, distance from the warzone keeps atmospheric contamination minimal
planets.population: ~2 million, rotating military and support personnel
planets.demographics: Highly mixed, all corporate factions represented simultaneously
planets.economy: Medical services, rest and recreation, food production, neutral logistics hub
planets.access_note: Universal truce enforced by mutual agreement and profit motive. Violence is handled quietly and away from public areas.
hazards: Intelligence operations from all sides, assume you are being watched at all times
Corporate-sponsored violence occurs but is kept away from areas that would draw attention
Debt collection, Titania 4 is where financial disputes from the warzone get settled
Information is a commodity and a weapon here

notable_locations.name: The Strip
notable_locations.desc: The main commercial district. Bars, clinics, black market vendors, and recreational facilities catering to every taste and budget. The truce holds here because it is too profitable to break.

notable_locations.name: Neutral Medical (NMed)
notable_locations.desc: The largest independent field hospital in the known galaxy. Treats all patients regardless of corporate affiliation. Technically neutral, in practice, the intelligence value of a fully-staffed trauma facility cannot be overstated.

notable_locations.name: The Counting Houses
notable_locations.desc: Financial services district, where corporate contracts are negotiated, morondium futures traded, and the real decisions about Titania 2 are made, off the battlefield.

hooks: Debt collection on Titania 4 operates in a legal grey area that both corporate factions tolerate because it occasionally works in their favour, soldiers from any side can find themselves held by the other side's financial representatives without it technically constituting a truce violation. This is common enough that experienced fighters carry debt documentation as a matter of personal survival practice.

It has been reported across decades by medical staff who have worked at NMed that the facility is extensively monitored by every major corporate intelligence operation in the system, the patient population makes it the most information-rich location in the Titania theatre. This is treated as an occupational hazard of working there rather than an exceptional situation.

The Counting Houses on Titania 4 are where the real war is conducted, every major territorial shift on Titania 2 below has been preceded by a corresponding shift in the financial instruments traded on Titania 4 above, typically several weeks in advance. Analysts who track both markets simultaneously have predicted engagements before they occurred.
planets.desc: Titania 4 is the eye of the storm. Every corporation with a presence in the system maintains facilities here, and a universal truce holds, enforced not by law but by mutual self-interest and the understanding that if the truce breaks here, the Nova cruisers above Titania 2 become far less predictable. Soldiers from every side come here for medical treatment, rest, food that is not field rations, and a few days of not being actively targeted.

planets.name: Carnath
planets.access_note: Unrestricted access. Several corporate survey teams have landed. None have established permanent presence.
hazards: No atmosphere, full EVA required at all times
Micrometeorite impacts more frequent than average due to proximity to Titania Prime debris field
Corporate survey teams operating here may be armed
planets.desc: A small, airless rocky world sitting between the warzone of Titania 2 and the neutral ground of Titania 4. The name Carnath was assigned by a survey team over a decade ago and has stuck in usage despite no official designation process. Its proximity to the Titania Prime debris field means its surface shows heavier cratering than expected for its size. Several corporations have quietly surveyed it for morondium traces but found nothing commercially significant. Occasionally used as an observation post during periods of intense fighting on Titania 2.

planets.name: Veroth
planets.atm_note: Hydrogen-helium gas envelope
planets.access_note: No infrastructure. Some vessels use its moons as observation stations.
hazards: Gas giant atmosphere, lethal pressure below cloud deck
Radiation belt
Strong gravitational gradient
Sparse ring system creates navigational scatter zone around equatorial approach
planets.desc: A large banded gas giant in the outer Titania system, informally named Veroth by navigators running the approach corridor. A faint but visible ring system circles the equatorial plane, composed of dark material, less visually striking than Orion-G1 but noted on all current navigational charts. Several of its moons have been proposed as observation or staging platforms for corporate military planning. None have been formally developed, though survey teams have mapped them. Veroth itself is useful primarily as a gravitational reference on approach.

planets.name: Sorellis
planets.access_note: Extreme outer system. No navigation infrastructure.
hazards: Extreme cold, cryogenic surface temperatures
No atmosphere
Extreme distance from system centre
planets.desc: The outermost known body in the Titania system, named Sorellis in navigational records, a frozen, airless world of water-ice and silicate rock at the very edge of the star's gravitational influence. So remote that even corporate survey teams with resource extraction interests have decided the transit time does not justify the potential return. It sits in permanent darkness, unchanged by everything that has happened in the system closer to the sun.

systems.name: Sirius System
systems.desc: Sirius is the commercial heartbeat of Alliance Space, a wealthy, densely populated system with some of the busiest spaceports in the galaxy. If you need to buy something, fence something, or find someone, Sirius is the first place to look. Its orbital stations are cities in their own right, and its surface worlds host the headquarters of several major corporations.

planets.name: Sirius Prime
planets.atm_note: Heavily managed air quality in upper tiers, pollution a persistent issue in lower districts
planets.demographics: Highly mixed, all playable races, significant Non-Born community
planets.economy: Interstellar trade, financial services, corporate HQ, black market, entertainment, manufacturing
planets.access_note: Open entry with standard Alliance identity verification. Criminal records flagged on entry, but flags can be managed.
hazards: Organised crime networks throughout lower districts
Corporate espionage, competing intelligence cells active citywide
Trafficking operations in port districts
Police corruption endemic in certain precincts

notable_locations.name: The Grand Spaceports
notable_locations.desc: Three orbital and two surface terminals processing billions of tons of cargo annually. The busiest single transit points in Alliance Space. Every major trading house maintains a presence here.

notable_locations.name: The Exchange
notable_locations.desc: The galaxy's largest commodities market. What gets priced here affects prices everywhere else. A dozen intelligence agencies maintain listening operations in the building at all times.

notable_locations.name: The Warren (Lower Districts)
notable_locations.desc: The underside of Sirius Prime, old city sections not visible from orbit. Crime organisations, independent operators, and people who need to not be found call the Warren home. Also home to some of the best food in the system.

notable_locations.name: Corporate Row
notable_locations.desc: The headquarters district for several of the galaxy's largest corporations. Publicly accessible, intensely surveilled, and the scene of the most aggressive corporate competition in the galaxy.

hooks: It is widely understood among freight professionals in the Sirius system that a significant percentage of cargo arriving under Haven manifests is misrepresented, the Warren district has absorbed this trade for long enough that receiving handlers consider a false manifest from that origin more reliable than an accurate one from anywhere else.

Financial analysts who specialize in commodity markets have documented for decades that morondium futures on the Exchange show patterns consistent with advance knowledge of military outcomes on Titania 2. The pattern is consistent enough that several academic papers have been published on it, all of which the Exchange has formally disputed without successfully refuting.

The practice of corporate executives arranging quiet extraction from their own organisations' facilities on Sirius Prime is well-established enough that several independent security firms maintain dedicated capability for it. The usual reasons are never shared publicly, but experienced operators say the pattern is almost always the same: someone has found out something about the organisation they work for.
planets.desc: Sirius Prime is the commercial heart of Alliance Space, an ecumenopolis where old city districts layer upon each other across centuries of construction. The upper tiers gleam with corporate towers and efficient transit. The lower levels are a different world entirely. The spaceports never sleep. The Exchange sets the price of half the galaxy's goods. And somewhere in the Warren, every deal that cannot be made in daylight finds its way to a table.

planets.name: Sirius Orbital Network
planets.atm_note: Maintained station atmosphere across all connected habitats
planets.grav_note: Artificial gravity throughout, rotational backup in older sections
planets.population: ~500 million, permanent residents across all stations
planets.demographics: Mixed, heavy Non-Born and Patriark presence in administrative roles
planets.economy: Shipping logistics, warehousing, passenger transit, ship servicing, corporate office space
planets.access_note: Most stations open with standard ID check. Corporate-owned sections require corporate affiliation.
hazards: Decompression risk in older station sections
Smuggling operations throughout the cargo logistics chain
Corporate security forces with minimal external oversight
Station politics can turn lethal, committee seats are contested violently

notable_locations.name: Central Hub Station
notable_locations.desc: The largest single structure in the Sirius system. Population rivalling small cities. Contains system-wide control, coordination, and the central customs authority.

notable_locations.name: The Free Docks
notable_locations.desc: Unaffiliated docking sections where small operators, independent traders, and people who prefer not to have their cargo logged operate. Alliance administration maintains minimal presence here by convention.

hooks: Station workers across the Sirius orbital network consistently report that cargo flagged by customs inspectors is regularly cleared through administrative override, a pattern so established that it has its own informal name in dock culture. The cold addresses used as cover destinations recur across years of records, suggesting an ongoing and organised operation rather than isolated incidents.

Shell corporation acquisition of station sections in the Sirius orbital network has been documented repeatedly over the decades, always following the same pattern: quiet purchase, displacement of independent operators, and transition to use by parties who are not publicly identifiable. The independent trader communities who have been displaced rarely remain accessible for follow-up questions.
planets.desc: The Sirius orbital station network is, in practical terms, a series of cities in space. Collectively they house half a billion people, process a significant portion of all interstellar cargo moving through the core systems, and host the offices of dozens of corporations and hundreds of independent operators. The Free Docks at the system's edge are where independent operators work without the scrutiny the main terminals carry.

planets.name: Pyreth
planets.grav_note: Unusually dense core for its size, standard surface gravity despite small diameter
planets.demographics: Mostly Non-Born operators, small human technical rotation
planets.economy: Heavy metal extraction, iron, nickel, platinum-group ore processing
planets.access_note: Corporate property. Contractor access by arrangement. The Consortium discourages unscheduled visits.
hazards: Extreme surface temperatures on daylight side, well above equipment operating limits
No atmosphere, full EVA
Automated mining equipment creates surface hazard zones
planets.desc: A small but exceptionally dense rocky world close to Sirius, known as Pyreth to navigators and mining crews, though the Sirius Mining Consortium's official documentation uses the older navigational designation. Pyreth's unusually dense metallic core makes it valuable despite its size. A skeleton crew of mostly Non-Born operators manages the automated extraction network from a pressurised station on the terminator line. The ore is processed on-world and shipped in bulk to Alliance Space manufacturing systems.

planets.name: Calodan
planets.atm_note: Hydrogen-helium envelope
planets.economy: Hydrogen fuel extraction, sells to passing vessels at commercial rates
planets.access_note: Fuel skimming platform open to commercial vessels. Guild-licensed rates apply. Emergency fuel available without prior arrangement.
hazards: Gas giant atmospheric hazards below platform altitude
Radiation belt activity varies
Platform is functional but not designed for extended habitation
planets.desc: Known as Calodan to the navigators and freight crews who fuel here, a large gas giant serving as the primary commercial fuel stop for vessels transiting the Sirius system. A Guild-licensed skimming platform operates in its upper atmosphere, extracting and processing hydrogen at commercial rates. Calodan is one of the busiest non-orbital commercial stops in the system; ships that prefer not to dock at the orbital network, for whatever reason, fuel here instead. The platform crew maintains carefully neutral relationships with everyone.

planets.name: Celendris
planets.atm_note: Methane-water ice envelope
planets.economy: None, theoretical ice mining interest, no active operations
planets.access_note: Outer system, no infrastructure. Alliance survey completed.
hazards: Extreme cold
No infrastructure
Far from system emergency response
planets.desc: An ice giant in the outer Sirius system, named Celendris in navigational records, blue-green in colouration due to methane ice in its upper atmosphere. Alliance survey teams have catalogued it as a candidate for future water-ice extraction but no commercial operation has been established. It sits at the outer edge of the system's charted routes, a pale reference point for ships approaching from the deep system.

systems.name: Aderan System
systems.desc: The Aderan system was the site of the first corporate war in galactic history, a conflict that ended with Aderan Prime destroyed and everyone finally understanding that there was no upper limit to what corporate warfare could do. The surviving world found a highly profitable replacement economy.

planets.name: Aderan Prime
planets.grav_note: Fragmented mass, residual unstable gravity wells
planets.access_note: Navigational hazard designation. No official memorial. Alliance discourages unscheduled approaches.
hazards: Active debris field, navigational hazard rated extreme
Residual weapons contamination in dense sections
Gravitational instability from fragmented core

notable_locations.name: Ground Zero (Estimated)
notable_locations.desc: The approximate centre of the event that destroyed the planet. Several independent groups have placed physical markers here. Alliance navy periodically removes them.

hooks: Among historians who study the first corporate war, it is the consensus view, though unpublished as such, that the Alliance's official position attributing the destruction of Aderan Prime to mutual escalation is a deliberate misrepresentation protecting one specific corporate faction whose successor organisation remains politically active today. The evidence exists in archival records that have changed hands multiple times and are never accessible simultaneously.

It is a recurring feature of the Aderan Prime debris field that corporate legal departments periodically file recovery claims for unspecified assets without ever disclosing what they are seeking. Salvagers who have worked the field say these claims arrive in clusters, suggesting that multiple corporations believe the same thing is in the debris and are each hoping to reach it first.
planets.desc: Aderan Prime was the first world ever destroyed in a corporate war. The event, disputed to this day, with multiple corporations claiming the others fired first, marked a turning point in galactic history: the moment everyone understood that corporate conflict had escalated beyond conventional warfare into something with no natural upper limit. No recovery or memorial operation has ever been mounted. The corporate interests that destroyed it moved on to the next calculation.

planets.name: Aderan 3
planets.atm_note: Standard breathable, Consortium manages atmospheric integrity for broadcast quality
planets.demographics: Mixed, global inmate population draws from across Alliance Space
planets.economy: Incarceration services, broadcast rights, entertainment, corporate security contracts
planets.access_note: Access by contract arrangement only, media and staff credentials required. Unauthorised approach treated as hostile intrusion.
hazards: Inmate population, organised criminal networks, gang hierarchy, constant violence
Consortium security forces, well-equipped, loyal to profit not law
Broadcast zones, being filmed has legal and social consequences outside the facility
Blackmail risk, Consortium security records everything

notable_locations.name: The Facility (General Population)
notable_locations.desc: The world's largest incarceration complex. Divided into numbered sectors with varying conditions. Sector 1 is relatively comfortable. Sector 9 is where the broadcast shows are recorded.

notable_locations.name: Ridge Track (Broadcast)
notable_locations.desc: The course used for Ridge Racing, one of the galaxy's most watched programmes. Inmates participate. The degree to which this is voluntary is not discussed publicly.

notable_locations.name: Blood Bowl Arena
notable_locations.desc: Broadcast capacity 80,000. Sellout broadcast audience across Alliance Space every cycle. The Consortium considers this its flagship cultural export. Casualty rates are part of the format.

notable_locations.name: Survivor Zones
notable_locations.desc: A series of terrain environments in the planet's southern continent where Survivor is recorded. The terrain is unmodified. The conditions are unmodified. The casualty rate is part of the format.

hooks: It is broadly known in Alliance political circles that the Aderan Correctional Consortium holds incarceration contracts on individuals from several powerful families, contracts placed through intermediaries that obscure the political connection. The Consortium is believed to use this knowledge as leverage in ways that never become public.

Journalists who have attempted to document conditions in the Facility's Sector 9 have a consistent record of stopping communication shortly after arrival and not being heard from again. The Consortium's explanation is always the same: the journalist chose not to file. The pattern is old enough that media organisations now consider Sector 9 assignments a one-way assignment.

It is known among information brokers in Alliance Space that the Facility on Aderan 3 houses individuals who carry significant knowledge, people who were incarcerated specifically to remove them from circulation rather than to punish a crime. The Consortium monitors all communication, which is why that knowledge has never successfully left.
planets.desc: The only surviving inhabited world in the Aderan system has found a highly profitable purpose. The Aderan Correctional Consortium operates the galaxy's largest for-profit prison facility here, housing criminals from across known space under contracts from the Alliance justice system, corporate security departments, and private clients who do not always specify what the inmate did. What makes Aderan 3 famous beyond the prison industry is the broadcasting. Three of the most watched programmes in the galaxy, Ridge Racing, Survivor, and Blood Bowl, are recorded here, using inmates as participants.

planets.name: Ashvel
planets.atm_note: Trace carbon dioxide, negligible pressure
planets.access_note: Unrestricted, nothing of commercial value confirmed.
hazards: Thin atmosphere provides no radiation shielding
Surface temperature extremes
No infrastructure within recovery range
planets.desc: A small, barren rocky world between the Aderan Prime debris field and the surviving worlds of the system. Called Ashvel in navigational logs, the name predates the corporate war, when it was surveyed and found unremarkable. The Consortium has not expressed interest in it. It orbits in silence, unchanged by everything that has happened in the system around it: the corporate war, the destruction, the prison empire, the broadcasting.

planets.name: Gorthon
planets.atm_note: Dense hydrogen-helium envelope with ammonia cloud bands
planets.economy: None, no fuel licensing in this system
planets.access_note: No commercial infrastructure. Outer system.
hazards: Standard gas giant hazards, pressure, radiation, gravity gradient
planets.desc: A large gas giant in the outer Aderan system, named Gorthon in navigational records. Unlike Sirius, no commercial fuel operation has been established here, the Aderan system's reputation for corporate conflict and the Consortium's tight grip on access have made independent operators reluctant to invest in infrastructure they might not be allowed to use. Gorthon orbits without infrastructure, observed by the Consortium's security network as a matter of routine patrol coverage.

planets.name: Crethis
planets.access_note: Extreme outer system.
hazards: Extreme cold
Isolation
planets.desc: A frozen outer world named Crethis at the edge of the Aderan system's charted territory, primarily ice and rock, far enough from the system's activity to be effectively invisible to the Consortium's monitoring network. Its distance from everything commercial makes it an occasional rendezvous point for vessels that prefer not to appear in Aderan's approach records. Whether the Consortium is aware of this use is a question that experienced operators leave unanswered.

systems.name: Berilia System
systems.desc: Berilia is the Patriark homeworld and the quiet centre of the galaxy's most important dependency: resurrection technology. The Patriarks built no army. Instead they spent centuries making themselves indispensable. The cloning infrastructure on Berilia underpins the Alliance's promise of continuity, and the Patriarks know exactly what it would cost everyone if they renegotiated their terms.

planets.name: Berilia
planets.atm_note: Clean oceanic atmosphere, notably high oxygen, low particulates. Pleasant to most species.
planets.grav_note: Below standard, Patriark physiology adapted. Non-Patriarks find the low gravity pleasant.
planets.demographics: ~85% Patriark, remainder mixed, diplomatic staff and medical tourism
planets.economy: Cloning and resurrection services, biological research, pharmaceutical production, political consultation
planets.access_note: Visitor permits available but processed with comprehensive background checks. The Patriarks are careful about who they let in.
hazards: Patriark political manipulation, every interaction may be an intelligence-gathering exercise
Legal frameworks heavily favour Patriark citizens on home soil
Corporate surveillance targeting cloning research is constant
The dependency economy means the Patriarks hold significant leverage over anyone needing their services

notable_locations.name: The Cloning Spires
notable_locations.desc: The most advanced cloning and resurrection facilities in the galaxy. The actual processes are proprietary and kept from outside observation. The output, reliable resurrection across multiple species, is a dependency the Alliance cannot afford to disrupt.

notable_locations.name: The Archive of Lives
notable_locations.desc: Records of every individual who has passed through Berilia's cloning facilities. The archive is extraordinarily sensitive. The Patriarks maintain it as a private resource. Others have tried to access it. None successfully.

notable_locations.name: Berilia Wet Docks
notable_locations.desc: The main port, built to accommodate the oceanic environment. Ships dock at surface platforms; cargo and passengers are ferried by submersible to the main cities below. An unusual and disorienting entry experience.

notable_locations.name: The Directorate Hall
notable_locations.desc: The seat of Patriark governance. Accessible to invited diplomatic visitors. The real decisions that affect the galaxy are made here by people who have been planning them for decades.

hooks: The Patriark Archive of Lives is believed by intelligence professionals across the galaxy to be the most complete record of individual identities ever assembled, containing not just cloning data but biographical detail accumulated through decades of client interaction. It is widely assumed that the Patriarks use this archive as an active intelligence asset, not merely a service record. No external party has ever successfully accessed it, and the Patriarks have never confirmed or denied its full scope.

Medical researchers and cloning specialists have noted for decades that the published output of Berilia's cloning facilities contains statistical anomalies inconsistent with the biological error rates their own research predicts. The leading explanation among specialists who study the field is that the Patriarks routinely produce results they do not publish, results whose nature is the subject of considerable speculation.

It is an established fact among the galaxy's intelligence community that getting any operative onto Berilia without the Patriark Directorate's awareness is essentially impossible, their background screening process is more thorough than any government security clearance in Alliance Space, and the Patriarks share information about suspicious applicants between themselves in ways that have caught multiple attempts by different agencies to place assets on-world.
planets.desc: Berilia is a predominantly oceanic world and the homeworld of the Patriark, a species whose evolutionary environment shaped them into some of the most capable political operators in the galaxy. The Patriarks have no meaningful military force. They have never needed one. Instead, over centuries, they accumulated something more durable and more difficult to counter: leverage. The Patriark-owned cloning infrastructure on Berilia is the most advanced in existence. Resurrection technology that the rest of the galaxy depends on runs through Berilia in some form. The Patriarks built this dependency deliberately, over generations, as policy.

planets.name: Berilia II
planets.atm_note: Sulphur dioxide and volcanic gas, lethal without full respiratory protection
planets.economy: None, the Patriarks have no interest in industrialising their system
planets.access_note: Unrestricted. No infrastructure. Patriark patrol vessels monitor system traffic.
hazards: Active volcanism throughout
Toxic atmosphere
Extreme surface temperatures
planets.desc: A volcanically active inner world in the Berilia system, frequently illuminated by lava flows visible even from orbit. The Patriarks have never developed it, their philosophy of careful stewardship extends to leaving hostile worlds undisturbed. Their patrol vessels ensure it stays that way.

planets.name: Berilia III
planets.atm_note: Dense hydrogen-helium envelope with striking blue-white banding
planets.access_note: No infrastructure. Patriark vessels occasionally use its gravity well for orbital manoeuvring.
hazards: Gas giant pressure and radiation zones
planets.desc: A large gas giant with several moons, visible from Berilia's ocean surface as a bright blue-white disc. The Patriarks have catalogued its moons but show no interest in colonisation or exploitation. It serves as a reference point for system navigation.

systems.name: Mangara System
systems.faction: Contested, Hakari Clans vs Jaulaus Tribes
systems.desc: Mangara is the homeworld of the Hakari and Jaulaus and one of the most uncomfortable chapters in Alliance history. Exploited by the Nerulian Empire and then by corporate interests, placed under Alliance embargo to protect what remains of its traditional life, and still burning from an inter-species civil war that has never stopped.

planets.name: Mangara
planets.atm_note: Breathable but degraded, centuries of industrial exploitation visible in atmosphere quality
planets.grav_note: Slightly above standard, both native species' physiology adapted over millennia
planets.demographics: Mixed Hakari and Jaulaus, no reliable census, both groups distributed across territories
planets.government: None, clan and tribal governance, no unified authority
planets.economy: Subsistence agriculture, conflict economy, illicit corporate extraction via intermediaries
planets.access_note: Alliance embargo, ships require Alliance waiver to enter system. Landing without waiver treated as hostile. Corporate vessels operate through legitimate-looking intermediaries.
hazards: Active inter-species civil war, all outsiders treated as potential threats by both factions
Alliance patrol ships operate in-system, entry without waiver risks boarding
Corporate intelligence extraction operations, unknown actors active throughout
Ecological degradation, significant terrain sectors toxic from historical extraction
Deep population hostility to outsiders runs across both species

notable_locations.name: The Contested Line
notable_locations.desc: The rough border between current Hakari-dominant and Jaulaus-dominant territories. It has moved continuously for centuries. Crossing it without appropriate cultural knowledge is extremely hazardous.

notable_locations.name: Old Extraction Sites
notable_locations.desc: The ruins of Nerulian-era and corporate mining and extraction operations, now mostly abandoned. Both species consider them sacred ground, reminders of what was taken from them.

notable_locations.name: Port Neutral
notable_locations.desc: A small, barely-functional port that somehow both sides allow to operate. Corporate intermediaries, smugglers, and the occasional genuine relief worker pass through here. The Alliance doesn't officially acknowledge its existence.

hooks: Diplomatic analysts who study the Mangara situation note that every negotiated ceasefire between the Hakari and Jaulaus in recorded history has been undermined from within by factions on both sides who benefit from the continuation of the conflict. The pattern is consistent enough that observers now treat ceasefire attempts as a reliable signal that a significant escalation is coming from one side or the other shortly afterward.

Port Neutral on Mangara is understood by Alliance intelligence to function as the primary point of entry for corporate extraction operations that violate the embargo, a fact the Alliance is aware of and has chosen not to act on, which is itself the subject of considerable speculation among analysts who study the system.

The phenomenon of Hakari and Jaulaus diaspora members in Alliance Space inheriting leadership positions in ancestral clans they have never lived among is well-documented and creates a recurring problem for both communities, leaders who hold cultural authority but lack cultural knowledge, and traditional communities that must decide how much weight to give inherited position versus lived experience.
planets.desc: Mangara's history is one of the most uncomfortable chapters in Alliance records. Five hundred years ago the Hakari and Jaulaus were technologically undeveloped, a fact the Nerulian Empire exploited without hesitation, treating both species as an inexhaustible labour resource. Corporate interests followed when the Empire fell. The Alliance eventually placed Mangara under embargo in an attempt to slow outside interference. Enforcement is imperfect. The civil war is continuous, deeply rooted in centuries of grievance and competition, and the Alliance's official position is that it does not get involved. The planet is simultaneously embargoed and ignored, protected on paper, exploited in practice, and burning from within.

planets.name: Mangara II
planets.atm_note: Marginal breathable, thin CO2 mix with trace oxygen, requires supplemental filtration
planets.faction: None, Alliance considers it within embargo zone
planets.access_note: Falls within the Mangara embargo zone. Alliance patrol ships apply the same access restrictions as the primary world.
hazards: Within Alliance embargo zone, approach will attract patrol interest
No infrastructure or rescue capability
Thin atmosphere provides minimal radiation protection
planets.desc: A small, arid outer world in the Mangara system, barren and largely featureless. The Alliance embargo technically covers the entire system, but enforcement at this remote body is minimal. Corporate survey teams have landed here covertly to use it as a waystation when running supplies through the embargo.

planets.name: Mangara Outer Giant
planets.atm_note: Dense hydrogen-helium gas envelope
planets.access_note: Alliance embargo coverage is unclear at this range, but Alliance patrols have intercepted vessels here before.
hazards: Alliance patrol presence in system
Gas giant hazards
planets.desc: A large gas giant at the outer edge of the Mangara system. Its moons have been used by smugglers running the Alliance embargo as staging points and fuel dumps, a use the Alliance is aware of and periodically disrupts.

systems.name: Carach System
systems.desc: The Carach system is the seat of Skalan civilisation. Caragh, the homeworld, is closed. The system perimeter is enforced by Skalan patrol vessels without legal framework or diplomatic negotiation. Non-Skalans who approach uninvited are turned away or fired upon. The distinction between the two outcomes is not always communicated in advance.

planets.name: Caragh
planets.atm_note: Pristine, no industrial pollution, ecosystem maintained as sacred
planets.grav_note: Noticeably above standard, Skalan physiology adapted. Non-Skalans experience fatigue under extended exposure.
planets.demographics: Skalan exclusively, no known non-Skalan permanent residents
planets.tech_level: Advanced (selectively applied, industrial tech rejected in sacred zones)
planets.economy: Internal subsistence, cultural production, military training, nothing exported
planets.access_note: Non-Skalans not permitted. Not formally legislated, enforced by the certainty that testing it is inadvisable. Skalan patrol vessels intercept any unauthorised approach.
hazards: Extreme hostility to non-Skalan visitors throughout
Skalan warrior culture, insult has immediate physical consequences
Alliance legal structures do not apply here
No diplomatic protection for non-Skalans who enter without invitation

notable_locations.name: Temple of the First Warrior
notable_locations.desc: The most sacred structure in Skalan culture. Non-Skalans have never been permitted inside. Its location is known. Its contents are not.

notable_locations.name: Training Grounds
notable_locations.desc: Extensive martial training facilities covering much of the planet's northern continent. The quality of what is produced here is evident to anyone who has encountered Skalan warriors.

notable_locations.name: The City of Memory
notable_locations.desc: Built to commemorate every Skalan who died during the Patriarks' attempted genetic extinction. The records kept here are the most complete surviving documentation of what was done.

hooks: It is known among people who work with Skalan warriors that they occasionally seek outside contractors for tasks they cannot pursue through Skalan channels, not because the Skalans lack capability, but because involving their own institutions would make the matter a political issue within Skalan culture. This pattern of selective use of outsiders is established enough that certain contractors maintain ongoing relationships with Skalan clients specifically for this purpose.

The relationship between the Skalans and the Patriarks is one of the most closely watched bilateral dynamics in Alliance Space, a species that survived an attempted extinction by the Patriarks maintaining formal diplomatic relations with the perpetrators. Diplomatic exchanges between the two are never conducted publicly, and accounts of what happens in direct meetings between their representatives are not shared in any accessible record.

The City of Memory on Caragh is believed by historians and legal scholars to contain the most complete surviving documentation of the Patriarks' genetic modification program against the Skalans, records that would be legally significant in Alliance jurisdictions if they could be accessed. They cannot be accessed without Skalan permission, which has never been granted to any outside party.
planets.desc: Caragh is the Skalan homeworld and it is closed. Non-Skalans do not land here. This is not formally legislated, it is simply a boundary that the Skalans enforce and that everyone with any familiarity with Skalan culture understands not to test. The planet is covered in temples, training grounds, and shrines to warrior traditions that predate the Skalans' existence as a distinct species. The Patriarks created the Skalans as a warrior caste and later attempted to eliminate them through genetic modification. The attempt failed. The Skalans remember.

planets.name: Carach II
planets.atm_note: Thin, unbreathable atmosphere
planets.grav_note: Standard gravity
planets.access_note: Within Skalan controlled space. Patrol vessels enforce exclusion throughout the system.
hazards: Skalan jurisdiction, approach without invitation treated as hostile
Unbreathable atmosphere
No infrastructure
planets.desc: A dry, rocky world in the inner Carach system. Uninhabited and geologically unremarkable, it holds no significance to Skalan culture. The Skalans claim it as part of their system and do not permit others to operate here on principle.

planets.name: Carach Outer Belt
planets.access_note: Skalan patrol vessels use the belt for positioning. Non-Skalan approach treated as intrusion.
hazards: Active Skalan patrol activity
Debris navigation hazards in denser belt sections
planets.desc: The outer belt of the Carach system. Skalan patrol vessels anchor among the larger bodies during long patrol rotations, using the belt as the de facto outer perimeter of territorial enforcement for the homeworld system.

systems.name: Seigh System
systems.classification: Self-Governed Territory, Skalan Training World System
systems.desc: The Seigh system is administered by the Skalan as a separate closed territory from the Carach homeworld system. The primary body, Seigh, is the site of the Skalan rite of passage. Non-Skalans are not invited. The fauna does not check jurisdiction.

planets.name: Seigh
planets.atm_note: Breathable but carries spores, pollen, and biological agents causing cumulative harm without proper filtration
planets.grav_note: Above standard. Escape from predators is significantly harder than expected.
planets.demographics: Skalan young adults completing rite of passage
planets.tech_level: None (Skalans enter with minimal equipment by cultural mandate)
planets.access_note: Skalan jurisdiction. Non-Skalans are not invited and the fauna does not distinguish. Skalan vessels enforce no-entry for outsiders.
hazards: Most lethal natural environment in the known galaxy (consensus survey rating)
Multiple apex predator species with no natural fear of prey
Toxic and corrosive flora, skin contact with many plant species causes immediate harm
Acidic swampland, large sections physically corrosive to standard materials
Volcanic terrain with unpredictable activity
Biological spore agents requiring constant respiratory filtration
No rescue or medical extraction for non-Skalans, ever

notable_locations.name: The Deep Jungle
notable_locations.desc: The interior of the continent-scale jungle. Navigation is extremely difficult without cultural knowledge of the terrain. Predator density at this depth has never been successfully surveyed, no survey team has survived to report it.

notable_locations.name: The Acid Flats
notable_locations.desc: A vast expanse of chemical-saturated wetland that can dissolve standard armour alloys over a period of hours. The path through it is known to Skalan trainees and transmitted only orally.

notable_locations.name: The Summit
notable_locations.desc: The highest point on Seigh, the goal of the rite of passage. What is found there is known only to those who complete the training. No outsider has reached it and returned.

hooks: Among bounty hunters and fugitive recovery specialists, Seigh is treated as a terminal destination, the effective end of any trail. The combination of lethality and Skalan jurisdiction means that anyone who reaches Seigh is considered as inaccessible as if they had died. In practice, some do not survive it; but those who do are simply unreachable.

The exotic specimen trade has a standing, persistent market for live Seigh megafauna that has never been successfully supplied, the Skalans consider the planet's wildlife sacred and the environment ensures that any attempt at capture would likely kill the captor before the specimen. This has not reduced the offered prices, which continue to rise in proportion to the known impossibility of delivery.

Among Skalans living in Alliance Space, it is understood and never discussed that families who lose a child to Seigh's rite of passage cannot acknowledge the loss publicly. This creates a visible but unspoken grief that communities who know Skalans well learn to recognise and leave unaddressed, the correct response, in Skalan cultural terms, is silence.
planets.desc: Every credible environmental survey of Seigh has reached the same conclusion: it is the most lethal naturally occurring environment in the known galaxy. The jungle is dense, the flora is largely toxic on contact, the predators are large and have evolved over millions of years to kill anything that moves, and the terrain alternates between impenetrable canopy, acidic swampland, and sheer volcanic rock. The Skalans send their young here. Surviving Seigh for the required period is the rite of passage that marks the transition to adulthood in Skalan culture. The survival rate for uninvited visitors is low enough that most insurers classify Seigh as uninsurable.

planets.name: Seigh II
planets.access_note: Skalan jurisdiction extends to all bodies in the system. Patrol vessels enforce exclusion.
hazards: Skalan jurisdiction, approach without invitation treated as hostile
Extreme cold
No infrastructure
planets.desc: A small, frozen rocky world at the outer edge of the Seigh system. The Skalans claim it as part of their territory. It holds no strategic or cultural significance; the Skalans simply do not permit others to operate in their systems on principle.

planets.name: Seigh Outer Belt
planets.access_note: Skalan patrol vessels use the belt for positioning. Non-Skalan approach treated as intrusion.
hazards: Active Skalan patrol activity
Debris navigation hazards in denser belt sections
planets.desc: The outer belt of the Seigh system. Skalan patrol vessels maintain a presence here as part of the broader perimeter enforcement around the training world.

systems.name: San Tien System
systems.desc: San Tien is the last world the Nerulians can call their own. When the Kravens obliterated the empire, survival came down to luck, those off-world, those on the fringes, those on ships fast enough to run. San Tien was remote enough to be overlooked and has remained so. It is a world haunted by what was lost.

planets.name: San Tien
planets.atm_note: Thin at altitude, breathable at ground level throughout
planets.demographics: ~98% Nerulian, small number of permanent non-Nerulian residents, mostly academics and diplomats
planets.government: Nerulian Government in Exile (Council of Survivors)
planets.tech_level: Advanced (Nerulian technology predates Alliance, much is unique)
planets.economy: Cultural preservation, historical archiving, small-scale manufacturing, knowledge trade
planets.access_note: San Tien accepts visitors but screens them carefully. Nerulian distrust of outsiders is deep-rooted given their history.
hazards: Proximity to Kraven Space, the border is not immovable
Haven Space pirates operate in nearby systems and occasionally probe the border
Internal political tensions, Government in Exile vs those who believe there is nothing left to govern
Nerulian technology not understood by outsiders, some remains active in unexpected locations

notable_locations.name: The Archive City
notable_locations.desc: The primary settlement on San Tien, built around the most comprehensive surviving collection of Nerulian cultural records, history, and pre-Kraven technology. The most important library the galaxy didn't know existed.

notable_locations.name: The Memorial Shore
notable_locations.desc: A coastal site maintained as a permanent memorial to the worlds lost in the Kraven invasion. The Nerulians count their dead here. The number is still being updated.

notable_locations.name: The Dry Docks
notable_locations.desc: Where the great fleet-cities that drift between systems are maintained and repaired when they return to San Tien. The technology here is unlike anything produced in Alliance Space, older, different, and in several cases more capable.

hooks: Nerulian archivists at the San Tien Archive City have long maintained, in private academic discourse, that pre-Kraven records contain references to technologies specifically developed to counter Kraven biological processes, technologies that were in development at the time of the invasion and never completed. The academic consensus is that the references are genuine. Whether anything retrievable survives is the question that has gone unresolved for decades.

Among the Nerulian diaspora communities that travel on fleet-cities, the loss of a fleet-city in transit is one of the most deeply feared outcomes, the combination of isolation, the Nemani Rift proximity on several routes, and the lack of rescue capability means that missing fleet-cities are almost never found. There are at least three fleet-cities that are known to be overdue and presumed lost in the past century.

The negotiation between the Nerulian Government in Exile and the Alliance over access to pre-Kraven technology records has been ongoing for over thirty years without resolution. Analysts who study the situation note that both sides appear to want an agreement and neither trusts the other enough to make the concessions one. The technology records are considered by Alliance naval intelligence to be potentially the most strategically valuable archive in existence.
planets.desc: San Tien is the last world the Nerulians can call their own. It is a world haunted by what was lost: libraries of Nerulian history, refugee camps that became cities, a government in exile that may never govern again. Most Nerulians encountered in the galaxy are from the great fleet-cities that drift between systems, but San Tien remains the spiritual and political home of the surviving people. The archive kept here is the most significant cultural repository of a civilisation that no longer has a civilisation, a last record of everything the Kravens destroyed.

planets.name: San Tien II
planets.access_note: San Tien system is open to vetted visitors. No infrastructure at this body.
hazards: No atmosphere
No rescue capability at this distance from San Tien
planets.desc: A small, airless rocky world catalogued in early Nerulian surveys under the designation Tien-Bav (Second Stone). The Nerulians have never developed it, their resources and attention are entirely on the inhabited world. It orbits in silence as it has for millions of years.

planets.name: Vel-Aroth
planets.atm_note: Hydrogen-helium envelope with distinctive green-amber bands, named in old Nerulian charts
planets.access_note: No restrictions. Nerulian navigators historically used it as a reference point on approach to San Tien.
hazards: Standard gas giant hazards
planets.desc: A large gas giant known in old Nerulian navigation as Vel-Aroth, meaning roughly "the watcher at the edge." Nerulian navigators traditionally gave it a silent acknowledgement on approach to San Tien, a custom maintained by the Government in Exile's fleet-cities as a gesture of continuity with the civilisation they carry in memory.

systems.name: Ishtar System
systems.desc: Ishtar exists to produce. The volcanic geology provides near-limitless geothermal energy. The crust is mineral-dense enough that raw materials are extracted metres from where they are processed. The atmosphere is permanently toxic from centuries of unregulated industrial output. The weapons that come out of Ishtar's foundries are carried by soldiers on every side of every war in the galaxy.

planets.name: Ishtar
planets.atm_note: Permanently toxic from centuries of unregulated industrial output, breathers mandatory outside sealed zones
planets.demographics: Mixed, predominantly human, significant Hakari labour contingent
planets.economy: Weapons manufacturing, heavy industry, geothermal energy, raw material extraction
planets.access_note: Arms Corp employment credential or contractor license required. Tourist access does not exist.
hazards: Toxic atmosphere, breather mandatory at all times outside sealed zones
Volcanic activity, eruption zones shift without reliable warning
Acid precipitation in certain atmospheric bands
Industrial accident rate significantly above Alliance average
Arms Corp security forces with lethal escalation policy
Geothermal venting, some districts are periodically unworkable

notable_locations.name: The Foundry Districts
notable_locations.desc: The core of Ishtar's weapons production capacity. Dozens of enormous manufacturing complexes producing the full range of Arms Corp weaponry. The noise and heat are extreme even inside sealed areas.

notable_locations.name: Arms Corp HQ (Ishtar Campus)
notable_locations.desc: The primary administrative and research hub for the largest weapons manufacturer in the galaxy. Security is military-grade. Visitor access is not offered.

notable_locations.name: Residential Sealed Zones
notable_locations.desc: The pressurised living areas where the workforce spends its off-shifts. Designed for efficiency, not comfort. The waiting list to transfer out is years long. Arms Corp pays well because it has to.

notable_locations.name: The Extraction Front
notable_locations.desc: The active mining zones where raw materials come out of the crust. Geologically unstable, worked in shifts around the clock, and statistically the most dangerous workplace in Alliance Space.

hooks: It is well-established among weapons dealers and military procurement officers that Arms Corp production from Ishtar consistently exceeds what appears on any filed export manifest, a discrepancy that has persisted across multiple audit cycles and is understood in the trade to represent an ongoing internal diversion operation that Arms Corp has chosen to manage quietly rather than expose.

Labour organising on Ishtar has a documented history spanning over a century: attempts are made, participants are transferred to less accessible work sites, and the organising effort dissolves. The cycle is consistent enough that experienced labour advocates consider it part of Arms Corp's standard operating procedure rather than a response to any specific threat.

Arms Corp's Ishtar research division is known in materials science circles to produce significant advances that never appear in publicly accessible literature, innovations that go directly into proprietary production rather than academic publication. The gap between what is observed in their manufactured output and what can be explained by known metallurgy has been widening for decades.
planets.desc: Ishtar is one of the most productive worlds in the known galaxy and one of the least pleasant to live on. Nobody who works here chose it for the scenery. Arms Corp pays well because it has to, the working conditions are brutal, the life expectancy is below average, and the waiting list for transfer off-world is years long. The sky is a permanent orange-brown. The air outside a sealed zone will kill you. The weapons produced here are on every battlefield in the galaxy.

planets.name: Ishtar II
planets.atm_note: Negligible atmosphere, trace nitrogen
planets.population: ~80, automated extraction station, minimal crew rotation
planets.demographics: Non-Born operators with small human technical team
planets.economy: Raw material extraction, titanium, chromium, rare earths for weapons manufacturing
planets.access_note: Arms Corp property. No civilian access. Station crew only.
hazards: Arms Corp security protocols, unrequested approach treated as industrial espionage
Automated mining equipment operates in unsecured surface zones
Low gravity and no atmosphere, full EVA
planets.desc: A small barren world close to Ishtar that Arms Corp uses as a raw material extraction site. Automated mining equipment operates almost without human presence, a small crew rotation maintains the extraction station and manages ore transport. The materials go directly to the Ishtar foundry complexes.

planets.name: Ishtar Outer Belt
planets.demographics: Mixed, contract workers from various corporations
planets.economy: Bulk ore extraction, primarily ferrous and nickel-iron asteroids
planets.access_note: Commercial mining licenses required. Alliance licensing authority is strict about claim boundaries.
hazards: Multiple competing mining operations with disputed claim boundaries
High-velocity industrial equipment
Debris from mining operations creates navigation hazards
Labour disputes in isolated stations can become violent
planets.desc: A moderately dense asteroid belt in the middle reaches of the Ishtar system, parcelled out under Alliance mining licenses to half a dozen corporations and independent operators. The ore quality is good but not exceptional, Arms Corp dominates the most valuable asteroids and leaves the rest to smaller operators who accept the dangerous working conditions in exchange for the proximity to Ishtar's market.

planets.name: Ishtar Outer Giant
planets.atm_note: Banded hydrogen-helium atmosphere
planets.economy: Potential fuel skimming, no licensed operation established
planets.access_note: No infrastructure. Alliance survey completed.
hazards: Standard gas giant hazards
planets.desc: A large gas giant at the outer boundary of the Ishtar system.
