Arms Corp surveyed it for potential fuel skimming operations and concluded the logistics did not justify the investment given Sirius's existing fuel infrastructure. It orbits largely unobserved at the edge of the system's navigational charts.

systems.name: Damph System
systems.desc: Damph is a frozen hellhole that happens to sit on the only known deposits of Coronthia in the galaxy. Without Damph, a significant portion of the galaxy's most powerful ships stop moving. The workers who extract it know exactly how much leverage that gives them. Governed by a patchwork of worker clans, tough, territorial, deeply suspicious of outsiders, and fiercely proud of what they do.

planets.name: Damph
planets.atm_note: Breathable but extremely cold, thermal suits required outside pressurised zones
planets.demographics: Mixed, predominantly human and Hakari, several generations of clan families
planets.government: Clan Council (rotating chairs by extraction volume, largest producing clan holds primary vote)
planets.economy: Coronthia extraction and export, heavy equipment maintenance, clan-run supply logistics
planets.access_note: Clan vetting required for landing. Corporate vessels operate under clan-issued extraction licenses. Unsanctioned arrivals are treated as claim-jumpers.
hazards: Extreme cold, unsurvivable exposure without thermal suits
Coronthia instability, extraction and transport accidents are common and severe
Clan territorial disputes, boundaries are not always marked and are always enforced
Corporate intelligence operations, multiple factions maintain covert presence
Coronthia is restricted in most Alliance atmospheres; transit documentation scrutinised heavily

notable_locations.name: The Deep Seams
notable_locations.desc: The primary Coronthia extraction sites, kilometres below the frozen surface. The most dangerous workplaces on Damph. The clans that work the Deep Seams have the most political weight, and the most casualties.

notable_locations.name: Clan Central (Vethara Station)
notable_locations.desc: The largest pressurised settlement on Damph, built at the intersection of the three largest clan territories. Hosts the Clan Council, the main trading post, and the only medical facility with full surgical capability.

notable_locations.name: Corporate Liaison Offices
notable_locations.desc: Where the corporations do their business with the clans, under conditions dictated by the clans. The offices are comfortable. The negotiations are not.

notable_locations.name: The Storage Flats
notable_locations.desc: Vast insulated storage fields on the surface where processed Coronthia is held before transit. Well-defended. The clans treat any approach without authorisation as hostile.

hooks: Clan traders on Damph have documented for decades that corporate buyers operating through unfamiliar intermediaries consistently offer above-market rates for Coronthia, and that clans who accept these offers tend to experience unexplained leadership disruptions within the following year. The pattern is well-known and has not reduced the number of clans willing to test it, because the rates are genuinely attractive and the evidence of causation is considered circumstantial.

Coronthia geologists who study the Damph deposits have long estimated that the known clan territories represent a small fraction of the total deposit, that significant seams exist outside current boundaries and that whoever identifies them first will face a political challenge to their claim of historic proportions. Discovery claims outside current territory are considered the most volatile situation in Damph politics.

Coronthia shipping volume discrepancies on Damph are a persistent feature of the system's trade records. The clans have been aware of unexplained shortfalls in licensed shipping volumes for years and have never publicly identified the route being used, an omission that suggests either the route is sophisticated enough to defeat investigation or the clans have reasons to prefer not knowing.
planets.desc: Damph is governed by a patchwork of worker clans, tough, territorial, deeply suspicious of outsiders, and fiercely proud of what they do. Corporate interests are present but operate carefully. Anyone who has tried to simply take control of Damph has found the clans remarkably unified on the subject of not allowing that. The planet is cold, hostile, and absolutely essential to the galaxy's most powerful drive systems. The clans understand their position exactly.

planets.name: Damph II
planets.economy: None, surveyed for Coronthia deposits, none found
planets.access_note: Outside clan territorial jurisdiction. No clan has claimed it. Alliance survey has been completed.
hazards: No atmosphere
Extreme cold
No infrastructure
planets.desc: A frozen outer world in the Damph system that has been surveyed for Coronthia deposits and found to contain none. The clans have not claimed it and show no interest. It is the one body in the system that nobody argues about.

planets.name: Damph Outer Giant
planets.atm_note: Pale brown hydrogen-helium gas envelope
planets.access_note: No infrastructure or restrictions.
hazards: Standard gas giant hazards
planets.desc: A large gas giant at the outer reach of the Damph system. The clans have occasionally discussed establishing a fuel skimming operation here to reduce their dependence on external fuel supply, a discussion that has not progressed into a formal proposal because the clans cannot agree on who would control it.

systems.name: Alsa System
systems.desc: Alsa is where the galaxy eats. The system's worlds are extraordinarily fertile, geology, climate and water distribution aligned in a combination that produces agricultural output unmatched anywhere in known space. Most of the food consumed across Alliance Space originates here in some form. Quiet, green, and vastly important.

planets.name: Alsa Prime
planets.atm_note: Pristine, no industrial pollution, ecosystem rigorously protected by consortium charter
planets.demographics: Mixed, predominantly human with significant Patriark and Hakari communities
planets.economy: Grain production, protein cultivation, processed food export, water export, agricultural research
planets.access_note: Open with standard Alliance ID. Agricultural zone access requires consortium permit. Naval exclusion zones around orbital platforms enforced.
hazards: Alliance navy patrols, the system is a designated strategic asset, naval response is fast
Corporate sabotage operations, several major corps have historical interest in disrupting Alsa supply chains
Ecological protection law is absolute, violations carry severe penalties
Weather manipulation infrastructure, regional climate is actively managed, interference is criminal

notable_locations.name: The Breadplains
notable_locations.desc: The central agricultural zone of Alsa Prime, hundreds of thousands of square kilometres of managed cultivation producing the bulk of the system's export crop. Heavily mechanised, lightly populated, and the reason the galaxy eats.

notable_locations.name: Consortium Administration (Alsa City)
notable_locations.desc: The seat of the Agricultural Consortium. Manages production quotas, export contracts, and the insurance frameworks that protect Alsa's output. Every major food distribution corporation has an office here.

notable_locations.name: Alliance Naval Station Alsa
notable_locations.desc: The permanent military presence protecting the system. Sized for deterrence, not just patrol, attacking Alsa would mean fighting a standing fleet. This is deliberate.

notable_locations.name: The Seed Vaults
notable_locations.desc: The most comprehensive collection of agricultural genetic material in the known galaxy. Maintained as a strategic reserve. Location partially classified.

hooks: Agricultural economists who follow food futures markets closely have noted that commodity prices occasionally move on information that cannot be explained by any publicly available data about Alsa production, suggesting that non-public information about cultivation zone conditions reaches certain traders before it becomes generally known. The Consortium has investigated this repeatedly without published findings.

The practice of Alliance naval personnel using exclusion zone access to move personal cargo through the Alsa system without manifesting it is documented in enough whistleblower accounts and court records from other systems that it is considered standard in naval cultures near strategic assets. What specifically moves through the Alsa exclusion zone has never been established.

Geneticists who study agricultural heritage varieties have identified strains in current commercial cultivation that do not match any recorded lineage in open databases, but that do match descriptions of varieties registered under corporate licenses that were dissolved in ways that should have ended the line. The Seed Vaults are believed to hold records that would explain the discrepancy, but access to the relevant sections has never been approved.
planets.desc: Alsa Prime is the most fertile world in the known galaxy. The combination of geology, climate and hydrology that produces this output is not fully understood and has never been successfully replicated elsewhere. The Agricultural Consortium operates it under Alliance charter with the explicit strategic priority of keeping the supply chain intact. Three Alliance navy cruisers are on permanent station in the system. Disrupting Alsa's output is one of the most inadvisable things anyone could attempt in the known galaxy.

planets.name: Alsa Inner Rock
planets.access_note: Within the Alliance military exclusion zone perimeter but no specific restriction at this body.
hazards: Extreme surface temperatures
No atmosphere, full EVA
planets.desc: A small, scorched rocky world close to the Alsa star, too hot and airless to support any activity. The Agricultural Consortium has never shown interest in it. It sits inside the Alliance navy's patrol perimeter and is occasionally used as a navigational reference point on approach to Alsa Prime.

planets.name: Alsa Secondary Worlds
planets.atm_note: Maintained atmospheres across all inhabited bodies
planets.climate: Variable by body, temperate to arid
planets.demographics: Mixed Alliance demographic, primarily rural and agricultural worker communities
planets.economy: Secondary crop production, livestock, aquaculture, processing facilities
planets.access_note: Standard Alliance access. Remote agricultural bodies have limited infrastructure, arrivals are noted.
hazards: Extreme isolation, emergency response times on remote bodies are long
Consortium security on commercial zones is assertive
Weather dependency, these worlds have less managed climate than Alsa Prime

notable_locations.name: Processing Stations
notable_locations.desc: Where raw agricultural output is processed for interstellar shipping. Enormous, busy, and surrounded by the constant traffic of freighters and bulk haulers.

hooks: Among freight crews who run the Alsa secondary world routes regularly, there are persistent accounts of crew members going missing between system entry and destination arrival, not falling overboard or deserting, but simply not present when the ship docks, with no record of departure and no body found. The accounts span multiple decades and multiple crews and are considered by those who make the runs to be an established occupational hazard that nobody has successfully explained.
planets.desc: The secondary worlds of the Alsa system extend the system's agricultural capacity well beyond Alsa Prime alone. Each body is cultivated for specific outputs that complement the primary world's production. Together they make the Alsa system the single most productive food-production system in known space by volume. The scale of what moves through here daily is difficult to overstate, and difficult to audit completely.

planets.name: Alsa Outer Giant
planets.atm_note: Banded hydrogen-helium atmosphere
planets.access_note: Outer system. No restrictions beyond Alliance military general patrol coverage.
hazards: Alliance navy patrols in the system, vessels at this range should be prepared to respond to standard ID challenge
planets.desc: A large gas giant visible from Alsa Prime's surface as a bright point of light at opposition. The Alliance navy has surveyed its moons but established no permanent installation. The Consortium considers the system's outer region adequately protected by the patrol fleet without additional infrastructure investment.

systems.name: Ash System
systems.desc: Ash sits at the edge of the Nemani Rift. The Alliance military maintains a permanent and substantial presence here, monitoring the Rift and ensuring whatever is on the other side stays there. Around the military has grown an ecosystem of salvage yards, scrappers, and pilots who come specifically to attempt the Rift. Most do not come back. The ones who do come back wealthy, famous, or permanently changed.

planets.name: Ash
planets.atm_note: Thin but breathable at standard altitude, weather is severe and unpredictable
planets.climate: Arid to Temperate (Unstable, Rift proximity affects local weather patterns)
planets.demographics: Highly mixed transient population, military personnel, salvagers, independent pilots, traders, researchers
planets.government: Alliance Military Command (Zone 7 jurisdiction) / civilian municipal councils in non-military zones
planets.economy: Military logistics, salvage, Rift-adjacent research, independent trade, black market
planets.access_note: Standard Alliance access to civilian zones. Military zones require appropriate credential. Rift approach vectors are regulated, launching without clearance is treated as hostile.
hazards: Nemani Rift proximity, spatial anomalies, communication disruption and navigation errors increase near the Rift boundary
Missing persons, Rift pilots who do not return are common. The search-and-rescue operation is understaffed by design.
Intelligence operations, the strategic position of Ash means it is extensively monitored by multiple parties
Salvage disputes, territorial conflicts among salvage operators are frequent and sometimes violent
Alliance military operating procedures, in Rift exclusion zones, challenge-response is short

notable_locations.name: Rift Station Alpha (Military)
notable_locations.desc: The primary Alliance monitoring installation for the Nemani Rift. Permanently staffed, heavily armed, and not open to civilian visitors. The intelligence gathered here is among the most restricted in the Alliance.

notable_locations.name: The Departure Yards
notable_locations.desc: Where Rift pilots fuel up, equip, and say their goodbyes. The culture here is unique, a combination of technical professionalism, fatalism, and the particular energy of people who have decided to do something they know is probably going to kill them.

notable_locations.name: Salvage Basin
notable_locations.desc: The primary civilian economic zone. Salvage operators bring finds here for assessment, trade and processing. A significant portion of the goods traded have unclear provenance. The Alliance inspectors are aware of this. Their interest in it varies.

notable_locations.name: The Wall
notable_locations.desc: The informal name for the Rift boundary as it appears in local space, a visible spatial distortion line that can be observed with the naked eye under the right conditions. Looking at it for extended periods is not recommended.

hooks: Rift pilots who return from runs into the Nemani Rift occasionally bring back objects they cannot identify and will not discuss. The Departure Yards at Ash have developed an informal culture around not asking, partly from respect for pilot privacy and partly from the understanding that what comes out of the Rift may be something where ignorance is preferable. Alliance registries contain no records matching any of the described objects.

The Alliance military exclusion zone around the Nemani Rift has been extended multiple times over the decades without public announcement. Salvagers who know the old zone boundaries notice the changes when they are redirected by patrol vessels who give no explanation. The cumulative area absorbed over the years suggests the military has found or observed things in successive zones that warranted extending the perimeter.

Research teams studying Rift proximity anomalies near Ash have a documented history of communication gaps that do not match equipment failure profiles and are longer than emergency protocols allow for without being treated as a loss. The Alliance military's standard response to inquiries about missing teams, that it has no information about their location, is precise enough that experienced observers treat it as a formal statement that says less than it appears to.
planets.desc: Ash has the particular energy of a place where people go to do something they know is probably going to kill them, surrounded by others who respect that decision. The Alliance military is the largest employer and the largest source of structure. The independent operators fill in every gap the military leaves, some of them legitimate, some of them not, all of them aware that proximity to the Rift means proximity to things the galaxy does not yet understand.

planets.name: Ash II
planets.atm_note: Marginal trace atmosphere
planets.faction: None, within Alliance military patrol zone
planets.access_note: No restrictions at this body. Alliance military patrols the broader system and will challenge unidentified vessels.
hazards: Within Alliance military patrol zone, identity challenges expected
Rift proximity creates occasional navigation anomalies even at this distance
No atmosphere
planets.desc: A cold, airless rock in the Ash system, unremarkable in composition and uninhabited. Its significance is purely navigational, it sits just outside the Alliance military exclusion zone boundary and is occasionally used by salvagers as an orientation reference before committing to a Rift approach run.

planets.name: Ash Outer Giant
planets.atm_note: Hydrogen-helium gas envelope with unusual radio emission patterns attributed to Rift proximity
planets.population: Uninhabited, Alliance sensor station on one moon
planets.access_note: Alliance military sensor station on primary moon. Approach to the moon requires clearance. The planet itself is unrestricted.
hazards: Alliance military installation on moon, approach challenge expected
Unusual electromagnetic emissions from Rift proximity, navigation instruments may behave unexpectedly
planets.desc: A gas giant at the outer edge of the Ash system, selected as a monitoring platform because of its position relative to the Nemani Rift boundary. The Alliance military operates a sensor station on its largest moon, collecting data on Rift behaviour and any activity near the boundary. The data collected here feeds directly to Rift Station Alpha. The station crew is rotated on classified schedules.

systems.name: Palentium System
systems.desc: Palentium was the first planet humans set foot on in Alliance Space, a fact the tourism industry has milked for centuries. The world is genuinely beautiful: tropical, warm, long coastlines, no atmospheric modification required. The corruption is so deeply embedded it is treated as a feature of the climate. Everything is for sale if you know who to ask.

planets.name: Palentium
planets.atm_note: Clean and warm, the atmosphere is a genuine selling point of the tourism industry
planets.grav_note: Slightly below standard, contributes to the pleasant physical sensation the tourism industry highlights
planets.demographics: Highly mixed, all Alliance races, significant permanent corporate expatriate community, rotating tourist population
planets.government: Palentium Planetary Council (formally Alliance-chartered; practically, major decisions require corporate approval)
planets.economy: Luxury tourism, financial services, offshore corporate administration, entertainment, hospitality
planets.access_note: Open with standard Alliance ID. Criminal records are flagged on entry, but flags can be managed for the right fee.
hazards: Pervasive corruption, every institution has a price, which means every institution is also a liability
Law enforcement is enthusiastically underpaid and comprehensively for sale
Political office is an investment vehicle, decisions are made for financial return, not public interest
Intelligence operations from multiple major corporations, the offshore financial sector means sensitive information passes through constantly
Tourist-targeting crime is endemic in resort zones, well-organised and ignored by local enforcement

notable_locations.name: The Coastal Resorts (Gold Coast)
notable_locations.desc: The headline tourism product. Luxury accommodations, private beaches, every amenity. The prices are extraordinary. The service is genuine. The staff all have a secondary income of some kind.

notable_locations.name: The Financial District (Palentium City)
notable_locations.desc: Where the offshore corporate administration happens. Shell companies, trust structures, financial instruments that do not exist in most other jurisdictions. If you need money to disappear or reappear with different paperwork, Palentium City is where it happens.

notable_locations.name: The Old Landing Site
notable_locations.desc: The original site of the first human footfall in Alliance Space, now a tourist monument of modest grandeur. The historical records associated with the site are impeccably maintained and selectively edited.

notable_locations.name: The Interior
notable_locations.desc: Away from the coastal resorts, Palentium's interior is lush, beautiful, and largely ignored by the tourism industry. It is where the people who make the tourism industry work actually live. Conditions vary dramatically from the coastal image.

hooks: Palentium's offshore financial sector is believed by Alliance financial intelligence to be used by every major corporation in the known galaxy at some point in their operational history, not just for tax efficiency but for the specific function of creating transaction records that are technically accessible but practically unacoverable without physical presence on the planet and relationships with people who will not cooperate by default.

The practice of using compromising material obtained on Palentium for political leverage is so well-established that it has acquired a colloquial name in diplomatic circles. The island resort districts are understood to be under observation by multiple private intelligence operations simultaneously, all recording independently. The material eventually circulates into hands where it becomes useful.

Historians who have studied the original human survey mission that landed on Palentium have noted for decades that the official record contains inconsistencies with independently surviving accounts, accounts that are themselves inconsistent with each other in ways suggesting multiple versions of events were circulating immediately after the landing, rather than a single set of facts that was later disputed. What the survey mission actually found when it made first contact with the planet has never been definitively established.
planets.desc: Palentium is one of the most visited worlds in Alliance Space and one of the most thoroughly corrupt. The tourism industry is genuine and the scenery is real. The institutions are not. Law enforcement is underpaid because underpaid enforcement is easier to work with. Political office is contested because it generates return. The financial sector exists because some transactions need a location where the paperwork does not follow standard Alliance trail requirements. Players who arrive expecting Alliance law to protect them will be educated quickly and expensively.

planets.name: Palentium II
planets.demographics: Non-Born operators, small human management rotation
planets.access_note: Corporate property. No tourist or civilian access.
hazards: Corporate jurisdiction, armed security drone patrol
No atmosphere, full EVA at all times
planets.desc: A barren outer world being quietly mined by a corporation with shell structures based in Palentium City's financial district. The arrangement benefits from Palentium's financial opacity, the actual ownership chain of Palentium Mining LLC has been investigated twice by Alliance financial regulators and disappeared into offshore trust structures both times.

planets.name: Palentium Outer Giant
planets.atm_note: Dense hydrogen-helium gas envelope
planets.access_note: No restrictions. No infrastructure.
hazards: Standard gas giant hazards
planets.desc: A large gas giant at the outer edge of the Palentium system, occasionally visible from the Gold Coast resorts as a bright wandering star. No commercial operation has been established here, the corporations active in the system prefer to invest closer to the planet's profitable financial and tourism infrastructure.

systems.name: New Earth System
systems.desc: New Earth is what happens when a group of humans decides the galaxy's progress has gone too far. Founded by settlers who rejected multiracial Alliance society, New Earth operates at a technological and social level comparable to 18th-century Earth, by choice. Firearms exist but advanced technology is culturally rejected. Non-humans are not welcome.

planets.name: New Earth
planets.atm_note: Clean, technological rejection means no industrial pollution
planets.demographics: ~99% human, any non-human discovery results in expulsion or worse
planets.economy: Agriculture, small-scale manufacturing, barter-based internal trade
planets.access_note: Non-humans not permitted. Outsiders treated with extreme suspicion. Advanced technology confiscated on arrival. Alliance law does not apply.
hazards: Extreme ideological hostility to non-humans, discovery means violence
Advanced technology confiscated, entering with FTL or combat tech invites aggression
No Alliance legal protection, colonial law is the only law
Surveillance by colonial militia throughout populated areas

notable_locations.name: Founder's Rest (Capital)
notable_locations.desc: The main settlement. Architecturally and technologically resembles a 17th-18th century Earth settlement. The colonial council meets here. Outside visitors are watched closely.

notable_locations.name: The Perimeter
notable_locations.desc: The outer edge of the settled territory where the colonial militia patrols. People can enter New Earth without going through Founder's Rest, but the militia patrols are irregular and aggressive.

notable_locations.name: The Hidden District
notable_locations.desc: Rumoured to exist beneath Founder's Rest, a section where people who do not entirely share the colony's ideology keep themselves quiet. Its existence is unverified.

hooks: New Earth is well-documented among intelligence professionals as a place where individuals can live for extended periods without any record of their presence appearing in Alliance systems, the colony's rejection of external technology means no biometric scanning, no network connectivity, and no data sharing with Alliance databases. This makes it a reliable refuge for people who need to disappear, which the colonial council is aware of and views as an accidental benefit of their chosen way of life.

Non-humans living under cover in New Earth are an established phenomenon, documented in accounts from defectors and people who have left the colony. The community's surveillance capabilities are lower-tech but thorough, neighbours watch each other closely, and the tolerance for anything unusual is zero. The average period before cover breaks is measured in months rather than years.

Pre-industrial cultural archives exist on New Earth that have not been digitised, catalogued, or shared with any external institution, physical records from Earth's history that the colonists preserve as part of their cultural programme and consider their own property. Academics who have tried to access them through formal channels have universally been refused. The materials are understood to exist but their specific contents are not known to anyone outside the colony.
planets.desc: New Earth is what happens when a group of humans decides the galaxy's progress has gone too far. Founded by settlers who rejected multiracial Alliance society, it is a place where fugitives hide, where certain ideologies fester, and where players who arrive expecting normal Dark Space frontier life will find something far stranger. It is not powerful enough to be a serious threat to anyone, but it is exactly dangerous enough to be a problem for anyone who looks wrong, sounds wrong, or carries the wrong equipment.

planets.name: NE-II
planets.access_note: Colonial jurisdiction is limited to the inhabited main world. This body is unclaimed.
hazards: No atmosphere
Dark Space, no Alliance rescue coverage
planets.desc: A small, airless rock in the New Earth system. The colonists have no interest in it, their technological rejection precludes any space-based industrial activity. The designation NE-II comes from an old Dark Space survey catalogue they never adopted.

planets.name: NE-III
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant atmosphere
planets.access_note: No restrictions. Dark Space, no Alliance coverage.
hazards: Standard gas giant hazards
Dark Space, no emergency response capability
planets.desc: A gas giant visible from New Earth's surface as a slow-moving bright object. The colonists named it something in their internal tradition but the name was never logged in any public navigational record. Dark Space survey charts list it only by catalogue number.

systems.name: Andromede System
systems.desc: Andromede is where the Alliance Navy maintains its primary strategic command infrastructure. Not flashy, not open to visitors, the system exists for one purpose: to ensure that the most powerful fleet in the known galaxy is organised, supplied, and ready. Most civilians who visit Andromede do so by accident and leave quickly.

planets.name: Andromede
planets.atm_note: Standard, well maintained in all inhabited zones
planets.population: ~12 million, military personnel and support contractors
planets.demographics: Mixed, predominantly human and Patriark command staff, diverse enlisted personnel
planets.economy: Military operations, naval logistics, weapons research, advanced ship systems development
planets.access_note: Military credentials or authorised contractor clearance required. Civilian landing zones exist but are heavily monitored.
hazards: Alliance navy security response is extremely fast and heavily armed
Intelligence operations from every major faction, this is the most surveilled world in the galaxy after Orion 3
Restricted zones with lethal automated defence systems
Political sensitivity, wrong conversations on Andromede have ended careers and lives

notable_locations.name: Naval High Command (NHC)
notable_locations.desc: The operational brain of the Alliance Navy. Deep underground, heavily shielded, permanently staffed at full capacity. No civilian access, ever.

notable_locations.name: The Proving Grounds
notable_locations.desc: Extensive military testing range covering the planet's uninhabited northern continent. New weapons systems, ship components, and combat doctrines are evaluated here before deployment.

notable_locations.name: The Contractor Ring
notable_locations.desc: The orbital and surface zones where civilian contractors operate. Ship builders, weapons manufacturers, and tech firms maintain offices here. Enormously profitable if you can get a contract. Intensely competitive.

hooks: Alliance naval personnel who go missing from Andromede are handled through a classified process that does not interface with any public records system, a fact documented by families who have tried to locate loved ones stationed there and found no accessible record of their assignment, their disappearance, or any investigation. The Navy's standard response to external inquiries confirms neither the personnel's presence nor their absence.

The contractor community that operates around Andromede's perimeter has developed a strong informal culture of not discussing what they observe in the course of their work. This is partly contractual, partly practical, and partly the product of watching what happens to contractors who have discussed things. The culture is consistent and self-enforcing.

Weapons test results from the Andromede Proving Grounds that produce unusual outcomes are classified at source with no external notification, a practice that has been in place long enough that the weapons research community treats the absence of published results from any Andromede test as more informative than any paper that is published. What the Navy considers publishable is the subset of results it considers safe to share.
planets.desc: Andromede does not appear on civilian navigation charts in any detail. The Alliance Navy operates its strategic command from here, the centre of the most powerful military organisation in the known galaxy. Civilians who come to Andromede are contractors, diplomats with specific agendas, or people who made a navigation error. The navy's presence here is so complete that the local civilian population is essentially an extended support community for military operations. There is nothing to see, which is exactly how the Navy likes it.

planets.name: Andromede II
planets.type: Rocky Moon System, Naval Testing Range
planets.access_note: Full military exclusion. Approach without clearance triggers automated defensive response.
hazards: Military exclusion, automated response systems active
Active weapons testing may occur without warning in this zone
Navy security response time from main world: minutes
planets.desc: A small airless body used by the Alliance Navy as a supplementary weapons testing range. The Proving Grounds on Andromede handle most work, but certain tests requiring distance from inhabited structures are conducted here. Test schedules are classified.

planets.name: Andromede Outer Giant
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant hydrogen-helium envelope
planets.population: ~350, monitoring station crew on largest moon
planets.demographics: Alliance Navy intelligence and monitoring specialists
planets.economy: Military intelligence monitoring, strategic approach observation
planets.access_note: Military monitoring station on primary moon. Moon approach restricted. Planet unrestricted.
hazards: Military installation active on moon
Navy patrol vessels use the planet as a navigation anchor
planets.desc: A gas giant hosting an Alliance Navy monitoring station on its largest moon. The station tracks all vessel movements in the outer system approaches to Andromede. Information collected here feeds directly to Naval High Command. The crew rotation is classified and the facility does not appear on public charts.

systems.name: System 5
systems.desc: System 5 has no official name, just its designation. The system was at the centre of the Tronik War and the Alliance has never been able to agree on what to call it. Three worlds were destroyed or rendered permanently uninhabitable. Two survive. The system is simultaneously a memorial, a political battlefield over historical memory, and a functioning civilian population trying to live with what surrounds them.

planets.name: The Remnant Fields
planets.atm_note: Three separate debris clouds, no atmosphere remaining on any
planets.grav_note: Each debris field generates minor unstable gravity wells, navigation requires current hazard charts
planets.economy: None, informal salvage operations exist but are legally grey
planets.access_note: Alliance navigational restriction in all three fields. Unofficial salvage runs operate with one eye on navy patrol patterns.
hazards: Three overlapping debris fields
Residual Tronik War weapons contamination, some areas remain active after decades
Gravitational instability from fragmented masses
Unknown salvage competition, multiple parties operating in the fields simultaneously

notable_locations.name: The Convergence Zone
notable_locations.desc: Where the outer edges of all three debris fields overlap. The densest navigational hazard in the system and the site of several famous Tronik War engagements. Memorial buoys placed by veterans' groups are periodically destroyed by debris impacts and replaced.

hooks: Salvagers who work the Convergence Zone where the three System 5 debris fields overlap report consistently that the densest sections contain intact sealed containers of a type not used for standard cargo, purpose-built survival or preservation pods from the Tronik War era, some of which are still broadcasting on military frequencies that should have been silent for decades. The Alliance acknowledges the reports and has not explained the broadcasts.

The practice of memorial vessels attempting to enter the System 5 debris fields for commemorative purposes is recurrent and contested, the Alliance discourages it without formally prohibiting it, veterans' groups support it, and several parties with interests in keeping the fields unvisited have historically worked to prevent specific voyages through means that are not easily attributed to any of them.
planets.desc: What remains of three Alliance worlds destroyed during the Tronik War. Official designation: Hazard Fields A, B and C. Unofficial name among veterans: The Three Graves. The debris fields are well-mapped but no safe path exists through them. The Alliance maintains the navigational hazard designation and discourages all entry. Salvagers who know the patrol patterns work the fields quietly.

planets.name: System 5 Station
planets.atm_note: Station-maintained throughout all public areas
planets.grav_note: Artificial gravity, uniform throughout
planets.population: ~200,000 permanent residents and rotating memorial visitors
planets.demographics: Highly mixed, veterans, historians, journalists, family members of war dead
planets.economy: Memorial tourism, historical research, small-scale trade, veteran support services
planets.access_note: Open to all with standard Alliance ID. Memorial zones require respectful conduct, security enforces this actively.
hazards: Historical and political tensions run extremely high, debates about Tronik War responsibility turn violent with some regularity
Intelligence operations, this station is a significant information hub for anyone studying the war
Veteran communities with deep grievances and sometimes unstable individuals

notable_locations.name: The Memorial Hall
notable_locations.desc: The largest structure on the station. Contains the official Alliance record of Tronik War casualties, 847 million names. Visitors can be found here at every hour.

notable_locations.name: The Archive (Contested)
notable_locations.desc: Historical records of the war, some classified, some disputed, some suppressed. Academics and intelligence services both want what is in here. The administration manages access carefully.

notable_locations.name: Veterans' Quarter
notable_locations.desc: The section of the station where long-term veteran residents have established permanent communities. Self-policing, deeply private about internal matters, and extremely protective of each other.

hooks: Among academics who study the Tronik War, it is a matter of consensus that the official version of the war's origin is incomplete, not a lie, exactly, but a version that omits the decisions and actors that made the outcome inevitable. The contested Archive at System 5 Station is believed to hold the records that would allow a full account to be written, and the administration's management of access to those sections is tracked closely by researchers who study what the Alliance considers worth suppressing.

System 5 Station veterans' communities maintain oral histories of the war that include accounts of individuals who were officially listed as casualties but were subsequently seen, spoken to, or otherwise encountered in circumstances suggesting they survived and chose or were compelled to disappear from official records. These accounts are treated seriously within veteran communities and dismissed by the Alliance's official historiography.

The periodic political effort to have the Alliance formally assign responsibility for the Tronik War has been made at least twelve times in the decades since the conflict ended, each time failing in ways that suggest the resistance is organised rather than simply political disagreement. The people who live on System 5 Station, veterans, historians, bereaved families, have views on who benefits from the question remaining unresolved.
planets.desc: System 5 Station was built after the war as a permanent memorial administration point and has grown into a community in its own right. Veterans live out their years here. Historians come to access the archive, what is accessible of it. Families come to find a name on the Memorial Hall wall. It is a place where the Tronik War is never quite over, where the official history is contested quietly and sometimes loudly, and where the gap between what is recorded and what actually happened is felt every day.

planets.name: System 5-IV
planets.atm_note: Dense hydrogen-helium atmosphere, traces of heavy industrial contamination in upper cloud layer from war-era weapons discharge
planets.access_note: Outer system, outside debris field exclusion zones. No restrictions.
hazards: Residual trace contamination from Tronik War weapons discharge detected in upper atmosphere, no surface hazard
Gas giant standard hazards
planets.desc: A large gas giant that survived the Tronik War undamaged, being too far from the conflict zones to be targeted. Its upper atmosphere shows trace contamination from the scale of weapons discharge in the inner system, residue that has persisted for decades. Veterans' groups occasionally pilot flyby missions past it as part of memorial activities.

planets.name: System 5-V
planets.access_note: Outer system. No restrictions.
hazards: Extreme cold
No infrastructure
planets.desc: A frozen outer world at the edge of the system. The Alliance memorial designation technically covers all of System 5, but enforcement at this remote body is minimal. No salvage interest, nothing of the Tronik War reached this far. It orbits unchanged, as it did before and during and after the war.

systems.name: B.I.G. (Beningen Ingratias Garlan)
systems.desc: The Beningen Ingratias Garlan black hole, universally shortened to B.I.G., sits at the edge of the inner Alliance core systems. It was named after the explorer who discovered it and did not survive the encounter. The naming was a posthumous gesture by the survey team that recovered the ship's log. B.I.G. is now a well-documented navigational hazard with clearly mapped exclusion zones.

planets.name: B.I.G. Exclusion Zone
planets.type: Stellar Phenomenon, Black Hole & Accretion Disc
planets.atm_note: Hard void, no atmosphere possible at any approach range within exclusion zone
planets.grav_note: Tidal forces sufficient to structurally damage standard vessels at inner exclusion boundary. Effects measurable well beyond mapped hazard zone.
planets.population: Uninhabited, no stable matter within exclusion zone
planets.government: None, Alliance navigational authority enforces exclusion
planets.access_note: Alliance-mandated exclusion zone enforced by automated beacon network. Specialised research vessels may apply for approach permits, approval rate is low.
hazards: Extreme tidal forces, structural damage to standard vessels inside inner boundary
Accretion disc radiation, lethal without specialised shielding
Gravitational lensing creates navigational anomalies for light-minutes in all directions
Hawking radiation flux elevates background radiation throughout surrounding space

notable_locations.name: The Garlan Research Platform
notable_locations.desc: A fortified deep-space platform positioned at the outer edge of the safe approach zone. Operated jointly by Alliance Science Authority and the GU Physics Institute. Heavily shielded, permanently crewed by specialists, and extremely interesting to intelligence services who assume the research done here has military applications.

hooks: Researchers at institutions that receive data from the Garlan Platform have noted for years that certain encrypted data channels transmit irregularly and without correspondence to the published research schedule, suggesting the platform conducts work that is not included in its official mission documentation. The Alliance Science Authority has not addressed this observation in any public statement.

B.I.G. approach permit applications filed under corporate research designations have become a recurring pattern over the past decade, applications with stated research parameters that do not correspond to any known scientific programme and that are approved without the standard peer review that academic applications undergo. The approvals come from an administrative branch that does not typically handle scientific research permits.
planets.desc: B.I.G. is as thoroughly mapped as a black hole can be. The exclusion zone is clearly marked. The research platform at its edge has been in operation for over two centuries. The Alliance treats it as a known hazard, a research asset, and a reminder that the galaxy contains things that simply cannot be engaged with on normal terms. The name has taken on cultural resonance, "B.I.G." in navigation slang has become shorthand for any problem that is too large and dense to go through directly.

systems.name: Garson Black Hole
systems.desc: The Garson Black Hole is older and less characterised than B.I.G., it sits in a more isolated region of Alliance Space and has been formally studied only intermittently. Named after the Garson cartographic survey that first plotted its position, it has recently attracted renewed scientific and intelligence interest due to anomalous readings near its outer accretion boundary.

planets.name: Garson Exclusion Zone
planets.atm_note: Hard void throughout
planets.grav_note: Tidal forces comparable to B.I.G. but less well-characterised, inner boundary may not be precisely mapped
planets.government: None, minimal Alliance enforcement presence compared to B.I.G.
planets.access_note: Alliance exclusion designation. Enforcement is less consistent than at B.I.G., the remoteness means patrols are infrequent.
hazards: Extreme tidal forces
Unexplained periodic gravitational pulse anomalies near outer boundary, cause undetermined
Lower quality navigational data, approach charts updated less frequently than B.I.G.
Reduced rescue and emergency response capability in the region

notable_locations.name: Anomaly Point Seven
notable_locations.desc: The location where gravitational pulse readings have been recorded on multiple independent surveys. The pulses do not match any known natural black hole behaviour. The Alliance Science Authority has classified the survey data pending further investigation. The previous survey team's full report has not been released.

hooks: The recall of the previous Garson survey mission before it completed its work at Anomaly Point Seven is documented in official records but not explained in any accessible filing. Survey team members who were recalled have consistently declined to discuss the mission in any professional or public context. The scientific community has noted the pattern without being able to investigate it.

Private research firms with survey rights to Garson Black Hole's outer boundary zone have been documented in permit filings spanning several years, approvals that proceeded through bureaucratic channels faster than comparable applications for less sensitive locations. The firms named in the permits are shell structures whose beneficial ownership has not been publicly established.
planets.desc: The Garson Black Hole has never received the same research attention as B.I.G., it is more remote, less convenient to reach, and until recently the readings from it were unremarkable. The anomalous gravitational pulses recorded near its outer boundary in the last decade have changed that assessment quietly and without public announcement. The Alliance Science Authority's classification of the survey data has not gone unnoticed by independent researchers or by intelligence agencies that monitor what the Alliance Science Authority decides to classify.

systems.name: Nulneon System
systems.desc: Nulneon is the homeworld of the Realmsingers, the rarest and most singular beings in the known galaxy. Each Realmsinger forms exactly one bond in their existence, with any object from the size of a pea to the size of a planet, and through that bond literally shapes its history and future. They are believed to be immortal. The system is closed not by force but by the simple understanding that a species of immortal world-shapers requires no protection and extends no invitations.

planets.name: Nulneon
planets.atm_note: Breathable but subtly altered, visitors report a quality to the air that is difficult to describe and impossible to forget
planets.climate: Variable (Deeply Settled, Shaped by centuries of Realmsinger bonds)
planets.grav_note: Standard, but gravitational constants have been observed to shift subtly in proximity to bonded Realmsingers
planets.population: Unknown, census impossible; Realmsingers' immortality and isolation make population count meaningless
planets.demographics: Realmsinger exclusively, the rarest sapient species in the known galaxy
planets.government: None that outsiders have been able to identify, decisions appear to emerge from consensus formed over centuries
planets.tech_level: Unknown, Realmsinger technology does not map to any known classification framework
planets.economy: None in any conventional sense, a species of immortals who can shape reality has no conventional economic needs
planets.access_note: Not enforced, simply understood. No known unauthorised visit has ended well, though accounts vary on what "not well" means in this context.
hazards: Reality distortion in proximity to active Realmsinger bonds, the fabric of what is possible shifts
A Realmsinger who has bonded with an object in your vicinity may reshape your experience of that object's history at any moment
No conventional threat assessment applies, these are immortal beings who reshape reality
Navigating Nulneon without a Realmsinger's knowledge is navigating a world that may not stay consistent

notable_locations.name: The Bonding Grounds
notable_locations.desc: The site where Realmsingers perform their singular life bond. The landscape here shifts in ways that cannot be mapped, what was there last year may not be there today, and what is there today may have been there for millennia from another perspective.

notable_locations.name: The Archive of Shaped Things
notable_locations.desc: A repository, apparently naturally formed, where objects that have been bonded to Realmsingers across history are kept. Not a museum, closer to a geological record of decisions made over centuries.

notable_locations.name: The Waiting Shore
notable_locations.desc: Where Realmsingers who have not yet bonded spend their time in contemplation. Their existence pre-bond is described by those few outsiders who have glimpsed it as profoundly quiet, a patience of a kind that requires immortality to maintain.

hooks: Encounters with Realmsingers in the wider galaxy are rare enough that each one generates extensive documentation in the communities that experience them, and the documentation consistently describes a quality of observation that those who experienced it find impossible to adequately convey. Whether a Realmsinger who takes an interest in something or someone is doing so casually or with purpose is a question that has never been answered from the outside.

Objects that have been bonded to Realmsingers and have subsequently entered general circulation in the galaxy are documented in academic literature, usually identified retrospectively when their behaviour defies physical explanation. The Realmsingers who bonded with them have never commented publicly on the objects' subsequent histories. What the bond means for the object's current holder is considered one of the more open theological and practical questions in Realmsinger scholarship.

The category of objects believed to be pre-bond Realmsinger artefacts, items that a Realmsinger has considered but not yet committed to, is itself contested in academic circles, with some scholars arguing that the distinction between bonded and unbonded is not observable from outside and others arguing that certain objects exhibit qualities consistent with being in a state of consideration. The market for putative pre-bond artefacts is substantial and largely unverifiable.
planets.desc: Nulneon cannot be understood on normal terms. The Realmsingers are so rare that most Alliance citizens have never seen one and never will. What is known about them comes from chance encounters, a Realmsinger travelling between systems, one seen at a distance in a major spaceport, a handful of accounts from individuals who received brief visits and spent years trying to process what happened. They are immortal. Each forms one bond in an existence of indefinite length. Through that bond they shape reality, the history and future of whatever they have bonded with becoming something they author rather than observe. What they want, what they value, what constitutes a goal for a being without a lifespan, nobody knows.

planets.name: Nulneon II
planets.atm_note: Thin breathable, unusual for a body this size; believed to be an artifact of Realmsinger shaping activity
planets.access_note: Realmsinger system, all bodies treated as closed territory.
hazards: Realmsinger territory, all approach warnings apply
Surface shows geometric formations inconsistent with natural geology, nature unknown
planets.desc: A small rocky world in the Nulneon system that shows surface features inconsistent with natural geological processes, large-scale geometric formations and regular structures that Alliance survey drones have photographed from prohibited range. Whether these represent Realmsinger shaping activity or something much older is not established.

planets.name: Nulneon Outer Giant
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant atmosphere, but with unusual spectral readings not attributable to known gas compositions
planets.access_note: Realmsinger system. No known non-Realmsinger has approached this body and reported on the experience.
hazards: Realmsinger territory
Unusual spectral readings of uncertain significance
planets.desc: A large gas giant with anomalous spectral readings that Alliance instruments cannot attribute to any known atmospheric composition. Whether it has been bonded to by a Realmsinger, or whether its unusual properties are purely natural, has not been established. The prohibition on approach makes investigation impossible.

systems.name: Uether System
systems.classification: Occupied System, Under Torc Federation Control
systems.desc: Uether was a system of profound cultural significance to the Realmsingers, the site of several ancient bonds that shaped entire worlds. The Torc Federation moved in during a period when the Realmsingers' attention was elsewhere and have been consolidating their hold since. No Realmsinger has responded publicly. Whether this means they do not care, have not noticed, or are responding in ways that are not yet visible, nobody can say.

planets.name: Uether Prime
planets.atm_note: Standard breathable, Torc Federation industrial operations have begun degrading atmospheric quality in settled zones
planets.population: ~3 million, primarily Torc Federation military and corporate personnel
planets.demographics: Predominantly Torc personnel, original system inhabitants displaced or absent
planets.economy: Military operations, resource extraction, industrial development, Torc Federation economic model imposed
planets.access_note: Torc Federation military zone. Visitors require Torc corporate sponsorship or diplomatic credentials. Alliance diplomatic presence is technically maintained but practically marginalised.
hazards: Torc Federation security forces, well-equipped and operating under orders that prioritise strategic assets over civilian considerations
Political tension, the occupation is not universally accepted
Industrial extraction operations have altered several site that were historically significant
Proximity to Realmsinger territory, the unpredictable factor that Torc strategists apparently believe they have planned for

notable_locations.name: Federation Garrison Command
notable_locations.desc: The primary Torc military installation. Heavily fortified, self-sufficient, and the administrative heart of the occupation. Torc's investment in this facility suggests a long-term presence.

notable_locations.name: The Altered Sites
notable_locations.desc: Locations of historical Realmsinger significance that have been built over or industrially developed. The Torc Federation's official position is that these are archaeological designations only. Realmsingers who have visited have not shared their assessment.

notable_locations.name: The Alliance Consulate
notable_locations.desc: A nominally operating Alliance diplomatic facility. The Alliance representative has filed multiple official protests about the occupation's terms. All have been acknowledged and none have produced change.

hooks: Torc Federation officers stationed at Uether who have made contact with the Alliance Consulate, even through indirect channels, have a documented history of being transferred out of the system within weeks, to postings that remove them from any further contact with Alliance diplomatic staff. The pattern is consistent enough that the Alliance Consulate staff consider it predictable. The subjects of the transfers are not heard from again in any accessible record.

Construction crews working on Uether have given consistent accounts, in communities they trust, of sites where work was stopped without explanation and surrounded by military exclusion zones, sites that correspond to locations identified in pre-occupation records as significant Realmsinger bond locations. The Torc Federation has not publicly acknowledged the connection.

Realmsinger scholars who track the rare sightings of Realmsingers in the galaxy have noted that reported sightings near Uether, while never confirmed, have increased in frequency since the occupation began. The Federation's official position is that no Realmsinger activity in the system has been detected. The scholars who study the pattern note that what the Federation chooses to detect is itself a form of evidence.
planets.desc: Uether was worth taking, good resource base, strategic position, and the Torc Federation moved when the opportunity was there. What the Federation's strategists may not have fully accounted for is that the system's significance to the Realmsingers is not merely cultural. Several bonds were formed here. What those bonds mean for the long-term future of everything the Torc Federation has built on Uether is a question that nobody currently holding authority over the system appears to have asked out loud.

planets.name: Uether-II
planets.atm_note: Trace sulphur dioxide and carbon dioxide, unbreathable without equipment
planets.access_note: No active Torc presence, deemed not worth extracting given focus on Uether Prime operations.
hazards: Thin toxic atmosphere, full sealed suit required
Low gravity, equipment handling requires care
planets.desc: A barren rocky world surveyed by Torc Federation prospectors early in the occupation. Mineral content was assessed as marginal relative to the investment required, and the Federation chose to focus extraction operations on Uether Prime. Uether-II has sat untouched since the survey, a footnote in the occupation's resource accounting.

planets.name: Uether-IV
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant composition, Torc atmospheric extraction platform operating at cloud level
planets.economy: Hydrogen fuel extraction for naval yard supply chain
planets.access_note: Platform access requires Torc Federation contractor clearance. The fuel produced here feeds the naval yards at Vasophus.
hazards: Gas giant atmospheric operations, platform stability in storm systems
Remote from primary garrison, limited emergency response
planets.desc: The system's outer gas giant, retained by the Torc Federation as a fuel source rather than an occupation asset. A small atmospheric extraction platform operates continuously at cloud level, harvesting hydrogen for the naval logistics chain. The platform crew rotate on ninety-day cycles and have minimal contact with the occupation operations on Uether Prime.

systems.name: Ithov System
systems.desc: Ithov is the deeper of the two former Realmsinger systems now under Torc Federation control, taken later and held with a heavier garrison. Unlike Uether, which the Federation industrialised, Ithov appears to contain something the Torc Federation wants intact. The nature of that asset is classified at the Federation's highest level.

planets.name: Ithov Prime
planets.atm_note: Standard breathable, the planet has been kept in better condition than Uether. Environmental preservation appears deliberate.
planets.demographics: Torc Federation military, corporate specialists, and a classified contingent whose roles are not in any public manifest
planets.government: Torc Federation Military Administration (Special Operations Designation)
planets.economy: Unknown primary economy, resource extraction has not been the Federation's focus here
planets.access_note: Torc Federation black site designation. No Alliance presence. No diplomatic access. Ships approaching without Torc military transponder codes are treated as hostile.
hazards: Highest concentration of Torc Federation elite military in any single system
Classified project, nature of what is here and what it does is unknown
No external verification of conditions inside the exclusion zone
Realmsinger bonds confirmed in this system, nature of interaction with Torc operations unknown

notable_locations.name: Site Omega (Classified)
notable_locations.desc: The primary Torc Federation classified installation. Visible from orbit as a massive construction project but what is being built inside is not inferable from external observation.

notable_locations.name: The Bonded Object
notable_locations.desc: Confirmed by multiple intelligence sources: a Realmsinger bond object exists on Ithov Prime. The Torc Federation has built around it, over it, or within it. The Realmsinger who bonded with it has not publicly responded to the occupation.

hooks: Intelligence analysts who study the Torc Federation's classification practices have noted that Ithov-related materials are the most consistently over-classified set of documents in any accessible Federation record, classified at levels that suggest the information is considered more sensitive than military operational planning or executive council deliberations. What justifies that classification level is not known outside the Federation.

Among defectors from the Torc Federation who have been debriefed by Alliance intelligence, those with any knowledge of the Ithov project have consistently produced the same assessment: that what the Federation is attempting to do with the bonded object is something that practitioners of magic across every tradition consider either impossible or inadvisable in the strongest terms. The defectors universally describe having no desire to return to the project.

The Realmsinger scholarship community tracks what it considers credible sightings with methodical care, and the consensus view is that Realmsinger presence near Ithov since the occupation has been greater than in any comparable territory in the past century. Whether this constitutes monitoring, a response to the Federation's activities, or something with no equivalent in previous Realmsinger behaviour is a question the scholarly community has been unable to resolve with available data.
planets.desc: Ithov is where the Torc Federation is keeping its most significant secret. The system was taken with more force than Uether and defended with more resources than any strategic military assessment of the system's conventional value would justify. Something on Ithov Prime is more important to the Federation than anything they will publicly acknowledge. Intelligence agencies across the galaxy have been trying to establish what for years. The most consistent theory, that the Federation is attempting to study, interact with, or exploit a Realmsinger bond, is considered likely by analysts who specialise in Torc behaviour. What the consequences of attempting that might be is another question entirely.

planets.name: Ithov-II
planets.atm_note: Trace nitrogen atmosphere, unbreathable, no industrial interest noted
planets.access_note: Within the Federation's classified exclusion zone around Ithov. No civilian access permitted. Automated sensor buoys positioned throughout.
hazards: Federation exclusion zone, approach triggers military response
Thin unbreathable atmosphere
planets.desc: A standard rocky world with no significant resources, retained within the Torc Federation's exclusion zone purely for its strategic proximity to Ithov Prime. The Federation has seeded the area with passive sensor arrays as part of the perimeter monitoring system for the classified operations on the primary world.

planets.name: Ithov Belt
planets.atm_note: Void between inner and outer system
planets.access_note: Federation automated sensor arrays positioned throughout the belt. Any vessel transiting the belt is logged and challenged.
hazards: Automated Federation sensor response, military intercept follows detection
Navigation hazard, dense asteroid field
planets.desc: The asteroid belt between Ithov's inner and outer system, converted by the Torc Federation into a passive monitoring perimeter. Hundreds of automated sensor platforms are distributed through the belt, providing overlapping coverage of all approach vectors to the inner system. The belt serves as an early-warning system for the classified operations on Ithov Prime.

systems.name: Vasophus System
systems.desc: Vasophus is the capital of the Torc Federation, a corporate empire that operates under the legal form of a trade federation while functioning as an aggressively expansionist state. The Federation's naval yards, political apparatus, and primary corporate infrastructure all centre on Vasophus. It is a system of extraordinary wealth and extraordinary violence, both maintained at high intensity simultaneously.

planets.name: Vasophus
planets.atm_note: Heavily managed, visible industrial haze in manufacturing zones, pristine in administrative and residential elite areas
planets.demographics: Mixed, Torc citizen-employees of all races, significant slave and indentured labour underclass
planets.economy: Military-industrial production, finance, political administration, advanced technology development, resource processing
planets.access_note: Torc Federation corporate identity or visitor visa required. Surveillance is comprehensive and intrusive by Alliance standards.
hazards: Pervasive state surveillance, all communication monitored, all movement tracked
Corporate security forces with broad mandate and minimal accountability
Slave and indentured labour system, Alliance law does not apply; ownership disputes can become violent
Political purges, dissent is managed efficiently

notable_locations.name: Federation Executive Tower
notable_locations.desc: The administrative capital of the Torc Federation, where the Executive Council operates and where the real decisions about Federation policy, military deployment, and corporate expansion are made.

notable_locations.name: The Naval Yards
notable_locations.desc: The largest military shipyard outside Alliance Space. Produces warships at a rate that makes the Alliance's intelligence analysts uncomfortable. The scale and output are not a secret, the Federation considers them a deterrent in plain sight.

notable_locations.name: The Corporate Campus
notable_locations.desc: The operational headquarters of Torc Corp itself, the parent entity that owns the Federation. The distinction between corporate headquarters and governmental palace is intentional and also meaningless.

notable_locations.name: The Lower Tier
notable_locations.desc: The part of Vasophus that does not appear in Federation promotional materials. Indentured workers and corporate-owned labour units live here. Conditions are kept at a level calibrated to maintain productivity without inspiring revolt.

hooks: The trade in Torc Federation classified information conducted by Federation officials themselves is well-documented in Alliance intelligence archives, a consistent pattern where officials sell specific, bounded intelligence to outside parties rather than defecting outright, suggesting an internal calculation that partial disclosure is profitable and that full defection carries costs they are not prepared to accept. The Ithov project information specifically has appeared in brokered intelligence markets at prices consistent with material of extraordinary sensitivity.

Slave liberation networks operating within Torc Federation territory are known to exist and are believed to be operating with external support that the Federation has been unable to identify and terminate despite years of active counterintelligence effort. The Lower Tier of Vasophus is identified in multiple independent accounts as the hub through which the most significant extractions are coordinated.

Alliance naval architects who monitor Torc shipyard output have tracked the emergence of a hull configuration from the Vasophus yards that does not match any design in any accessible registry, not a classified Alliance design, not a known Torc class, not a derivative of any previously observed vessel. The configuration has been under construction long enough that the production rate can be estimated. What it is designed to do has not been established from external observation.
planets.desc: Vasophus is what you get when a corporation achieves complete political control and decides to formalise it. The Torc Federation looks like a government from the outside and functions like one, but its legal foundation is corporate charter and its decision-making is driven by profit, strategic expansion, and the personal interests of its executive class. It is powerful enough that the Alliance treats it diplomatically rather than confrontationally. It is aggressive enough that the systems on its borders have learned to be either very useful to it or very hard to reach. Vasophus is the centre of all of it, beautiful in its upper tiers, brutal below, and completely serious about both.

planets.name: Vasophus-II
planets.atm_note: No atmosphere, all operations are sealed and pressurised
planets.economy: Major ore extraction, strategic metals for the naval yards
planets.access_note: Torc Federation contractor clearance required. Primary ore supply chain for the Vasophus naval yards.
hazards: No atmosphere, full sealed operations throughout
Industrial extraction equipment at scale
planets.desc: The second world of the Vasophus system, stripped of atmosphere by its proximity to the star and valued for what is in its crust. Torc Federation mining operations here run continuously, feeding strategic metals directly to the naval yards in orbit above Vasophus Prime. The workforce rotates on sixty-day cycles.

planets.name: Vasophus Mining Belt
planets.atm_note: Void
planets.economy: Automated asteroid mining, Torc Corp operates hundreds of extraction drones
planets.access_note: Federation exclusion zone, automated defensive systems respond to unregistered vessels.
hazards: Dense asteroid field, navigation hazard
Automated Federation defence drones throughout
No rescue capability, emergencies are managed by the nearest crewed station
planets.desc: The asteroid belt between Vasophus-II and the outer system, managed entirely by Torc Federation automated extraction systems. Several hundred mining drones operate continuously, supervised by a minimal human staff at a central coordination platform. The ore output supplements the Vasophus-II mines.

planets.name: Vasophus-IV
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant composition, massive atmospheric extraction platform at cloud level
planets.economy: Hydrogen fuel extraction, primary fuel depot for the Vasophus naval yards
planets.access_note: Naval logistics restricted zone. The fuel produced here is the lifeblood of the Torc Federation's naval operations.
hazards: Gas giant atmospheric operations
Remote from primary garrison support
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Vasophus system, hosting a massive atmospheric fuel extraction platform. The Federation's naval yards require enormous quantities of hydrogen fuel, and Vasophus-IV provides the primary local supply. The platform is the largest in the Federation's fuel infrastructure network.

systems.name: Yagmir System
systems.desc: Yagmir is the only non-Alliance system with an active gate travel link, and the gates do not open for anyone but Psylons, and even then only for most Psylons. The homeworld of a species so psychically advanced that they require almost no physical infrastructure, Yagmir is closed to all non-Psylons and to the majority of Psylons who have not received invitation or passage authorisation. What little is known comes from the rare Psylon who discusses it.

planets.name: Yagmir
planets.atm_note: Breathable, exact composition unknown. The few non-Psylons who have entered the system have not been in a position to report accurately.
planets.grav_note: Believed standard, unverified
planets.population: Unknown, Psylon population estimates are disputed even among academics who study them
planets.government: Unknown, Psylon political structure does not correspond to any framework the Alliance has been able to map
planets.tech_level: Unknown, Psylon use of technology versus psychic capability is not externally distinguishable
planets.economy: Unknown, likely inapplicable in standard economic terms
planets.access_note: Gate travel link is the only known access route, gates open only for Psylons and only for those with authorisation. The gates actively resist forced entry in ways that have proven fatal to anyone who tested this.
hazards: Active gate defence systems, psychic in nature and lethal to non-Psylons
Even authorised Psylons who travel here are not guaranteed return passage
Complete intelligence blackout, nothing inside the system is known with certainty
Psylon whose authorisation lapses mid-visit do not have reliable return options

notable_locations.name: The Gate (Outer)
notable_locations.desc: The external face of Yagmir's gate travel node, visible in space, activated by Psylon psychic signature, and studied extensively by Alliance science teams who have never succeeded in interfacing with it. The gate activates when it chooses to and not otherwise.

hooks: Accounts of non-Psylons claiming to have been inside Yagmir appear occasionally in the galaxy's broader circulation, accounts that are internally inconsistent, contain descriptions of impossible things, and yet include verifiable details that the claimant could not have known without having been somewhere very unusual. Academic institutions that study the Psylons maintain a collection of these accounts and have never been able to fully explain or fully dismiss them.

Psylons who are observed requesting assistance from non-Psylons for retrieval tasks near gate access routes are documented rarely enough that each instance is considered significant by scholars who study Psylon behaviour, the implication being that a Psylon who needs non-Psylon help has encountered a constraint that their considerable psychic capabilities cannot address, which is itself a category of information about Psylon limits that is not otherwise available.

Gate activation frequency at Yagmir is monitored passively by Alliance sensors at a distance, and analysts who track the data have noted that the pattern has changed over the past decade in ways consistent with increased traffic, either more Psylons travelling or the same Psylons travelling more frequently. The Psylons who interact regularly with non-Psylon communities have not commented on any change in their own mobility patterns.
planets.desc: Yagmir is the galaxy's most complete information blackout. A habited system, home to a known sapient species, connected by active gate travel infrastructure, and nothing verifiable is known about its interior. Psylons encountered in the wider galaxy discuss it obliquely if at all. The gates that provide access are not technological in any sense the Alliance can replicate or interface with. Non-Psylon attempts to enter, the few that have been made, produced results that ended the attempt. Yagmir is simply closed, in a way that implies the Psylons have decided it is closed and that this is sufficient.

planets.name: Yagmir-II
planets.atm_note: External spectroscopic survey only, trace atmosphere, unbreathable. No verified direct observation.
planets.grav_note: Estimated from long-range data, unverified
planets.access_note: Inside the Psylon gate system. No external access permitted. Designation "Yagmir-II" is Alliance catalogue notation only, actual Psylon designation, if any, is unknown.
hazards: Gate system defence, same lethal response as approach to Yagmir itself
Complete intelligence blackout
planets.desc: The second body of the Yagmir system, known only from long-range survey data gathered before the gate system actively denied approach. The Alliance catalogue designation "Yagmir-II" is used by external astronomers; whether Psylons have any designation for it, or any interest in it, is entirely unknown.

planets.name: Yagmir-IV
planets.atm_note: Estimated from long-range spectroscopy, unverified. Standard gas giant composition assumed.
planets.grav_note: Estimated, unverified
planets.access_note: Inside the Psylon gate system. External survey data only. Psylon status unknown.
hazards: Gate system defence, lethal to non-Psylon approach
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Yagmir system, catalogued by Alliance astronomers from long-range survey data gathered at safe distance from the gate system. What the Psylons use this body for, if anything, is entirely unknown. The designation "Yagmir-IV" is an external catalogue notation.

systems.name: Hanov System
systems.desc: Hanov sits in the loose outer region between organised space and the true frontier, close enough to Alliance Space to benefit from trade connections, far enough to operate outside close Alliance oversight. It has a reputation as a place where questions are not asked and answers are not required, which makes it attractive to independent operators of all kinds.

planets.name: Hanov
planets.atm_note: Standard breathable, mild
planets.demographics: Highly mixed, transient population rivals permanent residents at any given time
planets.economy: Transit trade, independent contracting, grey market services, information brokering
planets.access_note: Open entry, Trade Council requires registration but enforcement is perfunctory. Anonymous docking available for a fee.
hazards: No Alliance law enforcement, local security is private and profit-motivated
