Bounty hunters operate freely here without Alliance restriction
Debt collection can be violent and public
Information sold here flows in every direction simultaneously

notable_locations.name: The Open Market
notable_locations.desc: A sprawling physical and digital marketplace operating continuously. Almost anything can be sourced here given time and credits. Almost nothing is asked about origin or intended use.

notable_locations.name: The Council Halls
notable_locations.desc: Where the merchant families that control Hanov conduct business and resolve disputes. Outsiders who understand the power structure find this useful. Outsiders who don't treat it as scenery find it becomes relevant to them unexpectedly.

hooks: Hanov's bonded warehouses are understood by experienced traders to hold, at any given time, a significant volume of cargo from false manifests whose registered buyers have not appeared, goods in limbo between their actual origin and actual destination, held in a legal grey zone that Hanov's charter structure makes difficult to resolve and easy to exploit. The Trade Council manages these situations with pragmatic indifference to the original paperwork.

The Hanov Trade Council's communication infrastructure is a persistent target for access requests from external factions, an interest that the Council has historically rebuffed while profiting from the intelligence value of knowing who is making the requests. The Council's neutrality on this issue is itself a form of leverage that it maintains carefully.
planets.desc: Hanov works because it is useful to too many different parties to be cleaned up. The Trade Council maintains just enough order to keep commerce flowing and not enough order to make anyone who needs privacy feel unwelcome. It is not lawless, it is selectively legal, which is a more sophisticated and more profitable arrangement.

planets.name: Hanov Prospect
planets.atm_note: Airless, sealed suits required throughout
planets.government: None, claim disputes settled by Trade Council on request
planets.economy: Independent mineral extraction, modest yields, multiple competing claims
planets.access_note: No restrictions, independent mining claims registered with the Trade Council but not enforced rigorously.
hazards: Low gravity, equipment handling requires care
No atmosphere, sealed suit required
Claim disputes occasionally become violent
planets.desc: A small rocky world in the Hanov system with modest mineral deposits that have attracted a scattering of independent mining claims. Miners come and go on their own schedules, register claims loosely with the Trade Council, and resolve disputes with varying degrees of civility. Nothing here is worth fighting hard over, which is why the fighting stays at a manageable level.

planets.name: Hanov's Giant
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant composition
planets.economy: Hydrogen fuel extraction, sells to passing ships at rates below organised space
planets.access_note: Open, fuel prices are competitive and no questions are asked about the ships purchasing.
hazards: Ageing platform infrastructure, maintenance is ad hoc
Gas giant atmospheric operations, weather events
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Hanov system, where a small independent fuel extraction platform has operated for years under loose cooperative management. The fuel is cheaper than anything available in organised space and the operators do not ask about the ships they service. The platform's ageing infrastructure is maintained by people who understand that if it fails, there is nothing and no one to replace it.

systems.name: Mulbaring System
systems.desc: Mulbaring sits on several significant mineral deposits that multiple corporations have been circling for years. The system's independent status has held primarily because none of the interested parties trusts the others enough to allow any single corporation exclusive access. The result is a precarious equilibrium that everyone in the system knows is temporary.

planets.name: Mulbaring
planets.atm_note: Thin but breathable, altitude sickness above 2000m
planets.population: ~1.5 million, mostly mining workers and their families
planets.government: Independent Council (worker-elected, under significant corporate pressure)
planets.economy: Mineral extraction, heavy industry, resource export
planets.access_note: Formally open, corporate contractor vessels logged and monitored by the Council. Three different corporate security forces also conduct informal surveillance.
hazards: Three competing corporate security forces operating simultaneously, jurisdictional conflict is routine and occasionally lethal
Mining environment hazards, unstable shafts, toxic gas pockets, heavy equipment
Political instability, Council authority is challenged regularly
Corporate recruitment-by-coercion, "job offers" that are difficult to decline

notable_locations.name: Shaft Seven Complex
notable_locations.desc: The richest mineral deposit in the system and the primary point of corporate competition. Currently operated by the Council but with three different corporate security forces maintaining "observer" presences nearby.

notable_locations.name: Council Hall
notable_locations.desc: The administrative and political centre of the independent governance structure. Regular meetings devolve into heated arguments about corporate access agreements. The Council members are aware their independence is under sustained pressure.

hooks: The Mulbaring Independent Council's record of exclusive extraction deals is a study in how the same situation repeats: a deal is proposed, the other corporate interests respond in ways that make the deal impossible to execute, and the Council returns to equilibrium, poorer from the process but technically still independent. Workers on Mulbaring consider this cycle as reliable as the seasons and equally impossible to interrupt.

Mulbaring geological surveys routinely produce evidence of mineral concentrations significantly larger than the currently exploited deposits. The survey reports are technically the property of the Council but the data consistently reaches all three corporate observers simultaneously, suggesting either a systematic leak or a deliberate Council policy of maintaining the three-way equilibrium by ensuring no party gains exclusive advance knowledge.
planets.desc: Mulbaring is a system trying to stay independent in conditions that do not favour independence. The mineral wealth that makes it valuable is also what makes it contested. The Council has maintained autonomy by playing the corporate interests against each other, but the balance is eroding. Workers here are paid well compared to corporate-controlled equivalents but live with the knowledge that the situation is not stable.

planets.name: Mulbaring-II
planets.type: Rocky Barren World, Corporate Survey Site
planets.atm_note: Trace carbon dioxide, unbreathable, full equipment required
planets.access_note: Three corporate factions have competing survey claims. None has begun extraction. The dispute mirrors the standoff on the primary world.
hazards: Competing corporate survey teams, confrontations have occurred
Thin toxic atmosphere
planets.desc: A barren low-gravity world in the outer Mulbaring system, independently surveyed by all three corporate factions competing for the primary world's resources. Each has filed extraction claims. None has been able to begin operations because beginning would require the others to stand aside. The standoff is a smaller version of the political situation on Mulbaring Prime.

planets.name: Mulbaring Prospect Belt
planets.atm_note: Void
planets.demographics: Mixed, independent prospectors and corporate survey teams
planets.economy: Prospecting, potential extraction not yet begun
planets.access_note: No formal restrictions, but survey teams from competing factions operate simultaneously and tensions are high.
hazards: Navigation hazard, irregular asteroid distribution
Competing faction survey teams with private security
planets.desc: The asteroid belt in the Mulbaring system has attracted the same corporate competition as the primary world, with survey teams from multiple factions operating simultaneously in an unregulated environment. Independent prospectors who had claims here before the corporate interest arrived find the current situation significantly more dangerous than it was.

systems.name: Cetune System
systems.desc: Cetune is a waypoint system, the last fuelling and resupply stop before several of the more remote frontier routes. It has no particular strategic value, no remarkable resources, and no political significance. What it has is location: anyone heading into the deep frontier passes through Cetune or adds significant time to their journey.

planets.name: Cetune Station
planets.atm_note: Station-maintained breathable atmosphere throughout habitable sections
planets.grav_note: Artificial gravity, standard throughout inhabited sections
planets.population: ~80,000, rotating transient population rivals permanent staff
planets.demographics: Extremely mixed, the transient population represents every species and faction in the galaxy
planets.economy: Fuel sales, resupply, ship servicing, transit accommodation, information trade
planets.access_note: Open to all, payment required for services. Station Authority enforces a strict no-conflict zone. Violence results in permanent banning and ejection.
hazards: Information security risk, everyone passing through is a potential intelligence source for multiple factions
Debt and contract disputes from across the frontier end up here
Cargo disputes at a system with minimal legal framework
Smuggling operations running through the station are well-established and not easily disrupted

notable_locations.name: The Fuel Depot
notable_locations.desc: The reason Cetune exists. The largest independent fuel reserve outside Alliance Space, maintained with extraordinary care by the Station Authority because it is the station's entire economic reason for being.

notable_locations.name: The Crossroads Bar
notable_locations.desc: The social centre of Cetune Station. Information flows here freely and at a price. People who are running into the frontier and people coming back out of it both stop here, which means the table next to you contains a remarkable density of useful intelligence if you know how to listen.

hooks: Ships arriving at Cetune and failing to communicate or depart are common enough that the Station Authority has established a standard protocol for them, wait times, approaches, and escalation steps that are written down because the situation recurs. The outcomes range from mechanical failure to crews that chose to stay to vessels that arrived without anyone capable of communicating. The Station Authority does not keep detailed records of the less explicable cases.

The Crossroads Bar on Cetune has a reputation among information traders as the location where frontier route intelligence commands the highest prices in the region, not because the information is uniquely valuable there, but because buyers who need it badly enough end up at Cetune eventually, and their need is visible in what they are willing to pay. Experienced sellers know to wait.
planets.desc: Cetune Station is everyone's stop and nobody's home, a waypoint that draws its community from the constant flow of transit. The Station Authority runs it with the pragmatism of a community that knows its survival depends entirely on remaining useful and remaining neutral. They have enforced the no-conflict zone against parties who did not believe they were serious, and they have not done it twice to the same party.

planets.name: Cetune-II
planets.atm_note: Airless
planets.economy: None, mineral survey on file, no extraction interest
planets.access_note: No restrictions. The Station Authority has filed a nominal claim to prevent corporate intrusion but has no interest in mining it themselves.
hazards: Airless, full suit required
planets.desc: A small airless rocky world in the Cetune system. The Station Authority filed a mineral survey and a nominal claim years ago, not because they intend to mine it, but because an unclaimed world adjacent to a waypoint station is an invitation for corporate parties to establish a presence that would complicate neutrality. The claim is the simplest deterrent available.

planets.name: Cetune Outer Gas Body
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant composition, no extraction operations
planets.access_note: No restrictions. Used as a navigation reference point for ships approaching or departing the system.
hazards: Gas giant approach without extraction platform support
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Cetune system, used primarily as a navigation reference point for ships transiting to and from the station. The Station Authority has considered fuel skimming operations here on multiple occasions and concluded each time that the capital investment is not justified by the marginal improvement in fuel supply over what trading ships already provide.

systems.name: Sunstrope System
systems.desc: Sunstrope is the most consistently inhabited system in the Dragon Tail's Expanse and the closest thing the region has to a capital, not by any formal designation but because the largest pirate confederation operating in the Expanse calls it home. The system has a reputation that ensures legitimate traders give it wide berth, which suits its current residents perfectly.

planets.name: Sunstrope
planets.atm_note: Breathable throughout, thick lower atmosphere with persistent cloud cover
planets.population: ~600,000, pirates, support crews, families, traders who prefer anonymity
planets.demographics: Mixed, predominantly human, significant Skalan and Non-Born presence
planets.government: Confederation Council (rotating captains, decisions by weight of guns)
planets.tech_level: Mixed, captured and salvaged technology spans multiple generations
planets.economy: Piracy, salvage, illegal goods trade, protection rackets, privateering-for-hire
planets.access_note: Visitors without confederation sponsorship are boarded on approach. Having something worth trading is the fastest path to temporary welcome.
hazards: Active piracy, ships in this system without confederation transponders are considered targets
Confederation internal politics, rival captains settle disputes violently
No external legal protection
Captured goods and persons are a commodity here

notable_locations.name: The Confederation Dock
notable_locations.desc: The largest port in the Dragon Tail's Expanse, a sprawling, improvised facility built over generations. Every ship here tells a story about where it was taken from.

notable_locations.name: The Council Table
notable_locations.desc: Where captains meet to divide territory, resolve disputes, and plan operations. Technically open to any captain who can get there, in practice, only those with fleets worth counting have a real seat.

notable_locations.name: The Free Market
notable_locations.desc: Stolen goods, salvaged technology, and services of every kind change hands here without documentation. The best prices for certain categories of items in this sector of the galaxy are found at the Free Market.

hooks: Among Alliance families with members held on Sunstrope, it is a well-documented phenomenon that a significant percentage of captives choose not to return when given the opportunity, a pattern the Confederation attributes to the quality of life it offers compared to whatever the individual was living before capture, and that family members in Alliance Space find genuinely difficult to accept. Recovery operations that succeed logistically do not always succeed in their stated objective.

The Dragon Tail Pirate Confederation's capacity for large-scale coordinated military operations is systematically underestimated by outside parties, who tend to focus on the individual pirate culture and miss the scale of what the combined confederation can deploy. Corporate clients who have worked with the confederation on private military contracts have noted that the capability exceeds most standing corporate security forces in professionalism if not in doctrine.

Nerulian cache maps obtained through piracy in the Dragon Tail's Expanse are a persistent feature of the informal intelligence market there, enough of them have circulated that experienced traders in such information regard them with scepticism, but enough have proven genuine that the scepticism has a floor. The genuine ones tend to have a history of changing hands rapidly and violently.
planets.desc: Sunstrope has been pirate territory for as long as anyone currently alive can remember. The Confederation is not an organisation with a charter, it's an agreement between captains that cooperation is more profitable than constant conflict. It works, more or less. The system sustains itself on what passes through the Dragon Tail's Expanse and what can be taken from the edges of more organised space. For players, Sunstrope is a place where legitimate credentials are irrelevant and capability is everything.

planets.name: DT-7 Survey Rock
planets.atm_note: Airless
planets.access_note: Confederation designation only, non-confederation ships will be challenged.
hazards: Pirate presence, anyone not confederation-flagged is a target
Airless environment
planets.desc: A small airless rocky world catalogued in the Confederation's informal survey system as "DT-7". The Confederation uses it as a cache location and salvage staging area, goods taken from prizes in the Expanse are sometimes stored here before distribution. The small crew rotate through on an irregular schedule.

planets.name: The Deep Skimmer
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant composition
planets.economy: Fuel extraction, supplies the Confederation fleet
planets.access_note: Confederation fuel platform, non-confederation vessels will be fired upon.
hazards: Pirate platform crew, well-armed
Gas giant operations with salvaged equipment
planets.desc: The system's outer gas giant, where the Confederation maintains a fuel extraction platform assembled from salvaged components over several decades. It provides cheap fuel for the Confederation fleet and eliminates dependence on outside sources. The platform captain runs a tight operation by Confederation standards, which means only the equipment that is absolutely critical gets maintained.

systems.name: Carth System
systems.desc: Carth was an industrial system that operated for roughly two centuries before the economics stopped working. The corporations that owned it pulled out progressively over thirty years, leaving behind infrastructure they could not profitably recover. What remains is a system of derelict facilities, unstable orbital platforms, and the accumulated refuse of a large-scale extraction operation.

planets.name: Carth
planets.atm_note: Atmospheric contamination from centuries of unregulated industrial discharge, respirator mandatory outside sealed zones
planets.demographics: Transient, anyone who stays long-term has a specific reason
planets.access_note: No restriction, the system's hazardous state is its own deterrent.
hazards: Atmospheric toxicity, immediate without respiratory protection
Structural instability in all abandoned facilities
Unexploded industrial equipment and automated systems still active after decades
Toxic groundwater throughout, no safe surface water sources
Zero emergency or medical support

notable_locations.name: The Processing Complex
notable_locations.desc: The largest surviving structure on Carth, a continent-scale industrial processing facility. Partially powered by autonomous systems that never received a shutdown command. Salvagers know to listen for the sounds that indicate which sections are still active.

notable_locations.name: Orbital Platform Wreckage
notable_locations.desc: The remains of the orbital industrial platforms, most descended over the decades and impacted the surface, creating a secondary salvage field layered on top of the ground-level ruins.

hooks: Salvagers who work the Carth Processing Complex on a regular basis have documented finds that predate the industrial occupation and cannot be attributed to any manufacturing tradition associated with that era, objects whose origin and purpose are not identifiable from any available technical reference. The existence of such finds is considered established fact in the salvage community. Their nature remains unknown.

Corporate withdrawal records from Carth, accessible through indirect chains of corporate succession documentation, contain references to assets deliberately left in the system rather than recovered, described in the records as requiring isolation rather than transport. The nature of what was left is not specified in any accessible version of the records, and the relevant pages of the original documentation appear to have been redacted before filing.
planets.desc: Carth is a monument to extraction economics, a system consumed entirely by the industrial process and discarded when consumption was complete. Salvagers who know what they are doing can find useful technology here, sometimes cutting-edge relative to what was available when the systems were installed. The hazards are significant. The payoff, for the right team, can be considerable.

planets.name: Carth-II
planets.atm_note: Trace industrial discharge has drifted here over the years, trace toxins, not dangerous but unbreathable
planets.access_note: No restrictions, nothing here worth restricting. Occasionally visited by salvagers who have already cleaned out Carth Prime.
hazards: Trace toxic atmosphere
Isolation, no rescue possible
planets.desc: The second world of the Carth system, surveyed by the same corporations that stripped the primary world and deemed not worth the extraction cost. A handful of old survey markers remain on its surface, the only evidence that anyone ever came this far. Salvagers occasionally check it for any equipment the corporations might have left behind; they rarely find anything.

planets.name: Carth Outer Gas Body
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant, the corporations planned a fuel platform here and pulled the project when they exited
planets.access_note: No restrictions, partially constructed platform infrastructure in orbit, never completed.
hazards: Partially constructed orbital infrastructure, navigation hazard in orbit
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Carth system. The corporations that operated here had plans for a fuel skimming platform, the orbital framework was partially assembled before the withdrawal order came and the project was abandoned in place. The incomplete structure orbits in a deteriorating path and is a navigation hazard for any ship approaching the gas giant.

systems.name: Briea System
systems.desc: Briea is currently the site of an ongoing conflict between two pirate factions over a resource deposit that both sides believe is worth killing for. The system has changed hands four times in the past three years. Local civilian population has largely evacuated. What remains is a low-grade war zone with excellent salvage potential for anyone willing to operate in active fire.

planets.name: Briea
planets.atm_note: Breathable but carries smoke and combustion debris in contested zones
planets.population: ~20,000, combat forces from both sides, no civilian population remaining
planets.economy: Resource extraction contested by both factions, salvage of ongoing combat debris
planets.access_note: No safe entry. Both factions treat unidentified vessels as enemies. Even known allies of one side are at risk from the other.
hazards: Active combat operations throughout
Unexploded ordnance and weapon mines throughout contested zones
No medical or emergency support
Both factions prone to "friendly" interrogation of anyone not immediately identifiable as theirs

notable_locations.name: The Deposit Site
notable_locations.desc: What both factions are fighting over, a significant rare mineral deposit with applications in advanced propulsion systems. Currently under neither faction's firm control; contested daily.

notable_locations.name: The Wreck Field
notable_locations.desc: Four years of ongoing conflict has produced a significant debris field of destroyed ships and equipment. For salvagers with the appropriate risk tolerance, some of what is in the field is worth recovering.

hooks: The use of outside contractors for non-combat operations in the Briea conflict, extractions, intelligence runs, and supply route operations, is established practice for both factions, who recognise that the presence of neutral-flagged contractors creates operational options that direct military action would foreclose. The contractors who work both sides simultaneously are known to both factions and tolerated because the alternative is having no neutral intermediaries at all.

Weapons supply analysts who have studied the Briea conflict have concluded that both factions are receiving materiel at volumes and regularity that their own economic bases cannot support, implying external supply of one or both sides by a party or parties who have not been publicly identified and who have an interest in the conflict continuing. The conflict has lasted long enough and remained sufficiently balanced that the analysis is widely accepted as correct.
planets.desc: Briea would be unremarkable frontier territory except for what is in the ground. The two factions currently destroying each other over it were allied until eighteen months ago. The conflict has become self-sustaining, both sides have invested too much to walk away, and neither trusts the other enough to negotiate. Outside parties with the right capabilities and the right introductions can find work here, if they accept that the work environment is actively trying to kill them.

planets.name: Briea-II
planets.type: Rocky Barren World, Forward Operating Position
planets.atm_note: Airless
planets.population: ~400, forward military units from both sides
planets.access_note: Both factions use Briea-II as forward staging. Unidentified vessels are fired upon.
hazards: Active military operations, forward positions for both factions
Airless environment, sealed operations throughout
Unexploded ordnance
planets.desc: A small airless rocky world that both factions in the Briea conflict have established forward operating positions on, each side on opposite faces of the world, aware of the other and maintaining a tense standoff that occasionally becomes an artillery exchange. The positions exist primarily to prevent the other side from having exclusive use of the high-ground orbit.

planets.name: Briea Outer Gas Body
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant
planets.faction: Contested, fuel extraction controlled by whichever faction is currently winning
planets.population: ~60, whichever faction currently holds the platform
planets.economy: Fuel extraction, strategic logistics asset for both factions
planets.access_note: Controlling faction treats the platform as a military asset. Current controlling faction changes.
hazards: Military occupation, contested control
Gas giant operations
planets.desc: The outer gas giant, home to a fuel extraction platform that the two Briea factions have fought over nearly as hard as the deposit on the primary world. Whoever controls the fuel controls logistical advantage. The platform has changed hands six times in the past year. The crew that runs it has developed a careful pragmatism about which flag is flying.

systems.name: Soth L4 System
systems.desc: Soth L4 is a system notation rather than a proper name, the fourth catalogued system in the Soth survey cluster, designated L-type for its unstable stellar configuration. The star is a variable that cycles through significant energy output fluctuations on an irregular schedule. Most navigators route around it. The few who don't either have good reason or didn't check their charts.

planets.name: Soth L4 Survey Zone
planets.atm_note: No habitable bodies, all planetary matter has been degraded by stellar variability over geological time
planets.grav_note: Standard gravitational dynamics but stellar mass variability creates anomalous gravitational effects during peak cycles
planets.government: None, navigational hazard designation on all standard charts
planets.access_note: No restrictions, the hazard is the deterrent. Shielded research vessels make periodic transit during low-cycle periods.
hazards: Stellar flare events, unpredictable, lethal to unshielded vessels
Electromagnetic disruption during flare cycles renders navigation instruments unreliable
No shelter or refuge anywhere in the system
Flare cycle prediction models have margins of error that are operationally significant

notable_locations.name: Survey Point Alpha
notable_locations.desc: The closest habitable approach distance during documented low-cycle periods. The original Soth survey team placed a beacon here. It has been replaced three times after destruction by flare events.

hooks: Navigation crews who have transited near the Soth L4 system during low-cycle windows have filed reports over several decades describing transmissions originating from within the system, not survey beacons, not standard navigation signals, but patterns that do not correspond to any format in the registered signal database. The reports are consistent enough across independent sources to have generated an ongoing academic dispute about what is producing them.

The reputation of low-cycle window calculations for Soth L4 transit is poor enough among experienced navigators that the calculation methodology is considered a factor nearly as important as the transit itself. The group whose previous estimate placed a vessel directly in a major flare event continues to produce window calculations that are considered by some research institutions as their best available option, which is taken as an indication of how limited the alternatives are.
planets.desc: Soth L4 is on the charts with a hazard designation and not much else. The stellar variability that makes it dangerous also makes it intermittently navigable, there are windows when transit is relatively safe. What is inside the system that might be worth the risk is unknown because nobody has successfully surveyed the inner system during a low cycle and returned with usable data. Whether there is anything there worth the risk has not been established. Several parties appear to believe there might be.

planets.name: Soth L4 Inner Rocky Body
planets.atm_note: Any atmosphere long since stripped by stellar flare activity
planets.access_note: Within the stellar hazard zone. Reachable only during documented low-cycle windows, if those windows are correctly calculated.
hazards: Stellar flare events, potentially lethal to any ship in the inner system during a high cycle
Surface conditions extremised by periodic irradiation
planets.desc: A small rocky body in the inner system of Soth L4, identified from long-range survey during a low-cycle window. Its surface shows extensive scarring from flare events across geological time. Whether it contains anything of value is unknown, no survey has been completed at close range. Several research proposals have identified it as the most accessible survey target if a reliable low-cycle window can be confirmed.

planets.name: Soth L4 Fragment Belt
planets.atm_note: Void
planets.access_note: Navigation through the belt requires precise timing relative to stellar activity. The belt composition is partially consistent with the remains of a planetary body disrupted by historical flare events.
hazards: Stellar flare, transit during high cycle is immediately lethal
Fragment field navigation, dense and irregular
planets.desc: A belt of fragmented rocky material in the mid-system of Soth L4, the remnants of what long-range survey analysis suggests may have been a larger planetary body disrupted over geological time by the star's flare cycles. The belt is not navigable except during the narrowest low-cycle windows and then only with precise calculation.

systems.name: Gnoth Q714 System
systems.desc: Gnoth Q714 is a Freeland charter system, one of the scattered independent worlds that form the loose collective known as Freeland. Charter systems operate under a minimal governance framework: no corporate monopolies, no Alliance oversight, and a strong cultural tradition of non-interference in others' business. Q714 has grown into a significant trade node precisely because of what it refuses to regulate.

planets.name: Gnoth Q714
planets.atm_note: Standard, mild
planets.demographics: Mixed, significant transient population, all species represented
planets.government: Charter Council (elected, minimal mandate, primarily trade law)
planets.economy: Free trade, brokerage, information services, light manufacturing, transit trade
planets.access_note: Open entry under Freeland charter. No identity verification required beyond ship registration. Registration itself is not verified beyond its own claim.
hazards: No extradition, Alliance warrants are not recognised
Corporate interests operate here without regulation, which cuts both ways
Debt enforcement is private and can be aggressive
Information security is entirely self-managed, no privacy laws

notable_locations.name: The Charter House
notable_locations.desc: The Charter Council's administrative seat, also the location of the only functioning law court in the system. Cases that reach this court tend to be financial disputes; the outcomes are commercially pragmatic rather than strictly just.

notable_locations.name: The Freezone Docks
notable_locations.desc: The largest port in Gnoth Q714, operating under a specific charter provision that makes cargo manifests optional. The busiest section of the busiest system in this part of Freeland.

hooks: Gnoth Q714 is known among corporate fugitives and individuals seeking to disappear from Alliance Space as one of the most reliable destinations in the galaxy, the charter structure makes extradition impossible, the lack of biometric infrastructure makes identity verification impossible, and the community's cultural indifference to others' histories makes social investigation difficult. The length of time a fugitive can remain in the system is limited primarily by their own discipline rather than any external pressure.

The recurring debate within Freeland charter systems about whether to permit Alliance enforcement presence is most active in Gnoth Q714, where the economic stakes are highest. The debate has been held and resolved against Alliance presence on four separate occasions. Each occasion has been preceded by significant outside investment in the voting process from parties on both sides whose identities are never made public.
planets.desc: Gnoth Q714 is what Freeland looks like when it works, a functioning society built around the principle that people left to handle their own affairs mostly manage. The Charter Council keeps trade flowing and handles the disputes that cannot be resolved privately. Alliance citizens sometimes describe Freeland systems as lawless. The people who live here describe Alliance Space as surveillant. Both descriptions contain some truth.

planets.name: Gnoth Q714-B
planets.atm_note: Thin nitrogen atmosphere, unbreathable without equipment
planets.access_note: Charter Council nominal claim prevents outside corporate assertion. No one is actually there.
hazards: Thin unbreathable atmosphere
No infrastructure
planets.desc: The secondary rocky body in the Gnoth Q714 system, catalogued by the Charter Council and held under nominal claim to prevent outside parties from asserting corporate interest in proximity to the free zone. Nobody lives here and nobody is expected to. The claim is a legal instrument, not a settlement.

planets.name: Gnoth Q714-C
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant
planets.access_note: No restrictions.
hazards: Gas giant approach
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Gnoth Q714 system, used as a navigation reference by ships transiting to and from the free zone. The Charter Council has discussed fuel skimming operations here more than once but has never found a business case that justifies the infrastructure investment when fuel is available from trade ships at competitive prices.

systems.name: Lides H45 System
systems.desc: Lides H45 is a Freeland agricultural system, one of the quieter charter worlds with a productive economy based on food and raw material production rather than trade. It supplies several nearby systems and maintains the kind of community-scale governance that larger systems cannot sustain.

planets.name: Lides H45
planets.atm_note: Clean, rich, excellent growing conditions
planets.demographics: Mixed, predominantly settled families, some transient harvest workers
planets.government: Agricultural Council (community elected, focused on land use and resource management)
planets.tech_level: Standard to Low (by choice in many areas)
planets.economy: Food production, raw material export, small-scale manufacturing
planets.access_note: Open entry. Charter Council registers visitors but does not restrict them.
hazards: Remote, emergency services are self-provided
Weather events on agricultural worlds can be severe
Charter independence means dispute resolution is locally managed, outside legal frameworks don't apply

notable_locations.name: The Growing Fields
notable_locations.desc: Extensive agricultural land managed by a cooperative structure that predates the Freeland charter. Visitors consistently report that the food here is among the best they have encountered anywhere.

notable_locations.name: The Waystation
notable_locations.desc: Lides H45's primary port, more of a large farmyard with docking facilities than a commercial spaceport. The atmosphere is unhurried. People who arrive in a rush tend to slow down.

hooks: Agricultural communities in Freeland charter systems have documented a pattern of crop failures that trace to external rather than environmental causes, failures that weaken a system's economic independence before a corporate buyout offer arrives. The pattern is well-known enough among Freeland agricultural councils that "corporate season" has become an informal term for periods following poor harvests when unusual corporate interest in acquisition follows. Lides H45 is considered particularly aware of this dynamic.

Lides H45 is known among people who need to be forgotten as a place where a quiet life can be maintained for decades, the small population and low transient traffic mean that new arrivals who integrate genuinely become part of the community rather than remaining visible outsiders. The people who come here to disappear tend to have chosen carefully. The people who find them tend to have been looking for a long time.
planets.desc: Lides H45 is a Freeland system that chose not to be a trade hub. The community that built it wanted something quieter: agricultural land, self-governance, and distance from the busier parts of the galaxy. They have maintained that for generations. It is a peaceful system in the specific sense that peace has been a priority rather than a side effect, and in Freeland, that requires active maintenance.

planets.name: L-45-B
planets.atm_note: Airless
planets.access_note: Council claim on file, no active use. The community has no interest in it.
hazards: Airless
planets.desc: The inner rocky body of the Lides H45 system, claimed by the Agricultural Council under the standard Freeland practice of holding nominal territory to prevent intrusion. The community here has no interest in the rock itself, they came for farmland and found it on the primary world. The claim is renewed each charter cycle as a formality.

planets.name: L-45-C
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant
planets.access_note: No restrictions. Used as navigational reference by ships visiting the agricultural world.
hazards: Gas giant approach
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Lides H45 system, named in the Freeland catalogue but otherwise unremarkable. Ships visiting the agricultural world use it as an approach reference. The community on the primary world is indifferent to it. It does its job as a large gravitational object.

systems.name: Mivenia System
systems.desc: Mivenia has built a reputation as the best place outside Alliance Space to get a ship repaired, a weapon modified, or a technological problem solved without paperwork. Engineers who could not work in the regulated Alliance environment have been coming to Mivenia for decades. The result is an extraordinary concentration of technical capability operating under no oversight at all.

planets.name: Mivenia
planets.atm_note: Standard, mild haze in the engineering districts from workshop output
planets.demographics: Mixed, unusually high concentration of Non-Born and Hakari engineers
planets.government: Engineering Collective (self-governing, disputes resolved by technical arbitration)
planets.economy: Ship repair and modification, weapons engineering, technology development, bespoke manufacturing
planets.access_note: Open entry under charter. Engineering work is by agreement, no jobs the Collective collectively refuses to take.
hazards: No oversight means military hardware of every classification can be worked on here, so can its owners
Test events, new technology is tested on Mivenia's test ranges and the results are not always contained
Corporate attempts to acquire key personnel are ongoing and sometimes not subtle

notable_locations.name: The Workshop Rings
notable_locations.desc: The industrial heart of Mivenia, a series of concentric engineering districts where every type of technical work is available. Visiting a ship yard here is an education in what ships look like when someone smart decided the regulations were getting in the way.

notable_locations.name: The Collective Hall
notable_locations.desc: Where the engineering community meets, debates, and occasionally argues violently about technical philosophy. Also where contracts are formalised and disputes resolved. Both of the previous statements are handled with equal seriousness.

hooks: The Mivenia Engineering Collective has a standing reputation for taking on weapons development contracts that no regulated facility would accept, a reputation that has made it the destination for prototype work that cannot be done anywhere with oversight. The consequence is that significant military technology in the galaxy has passed through Mivenia at some stage of its development, and the Engineering Collective holds technical knowledge that no government has been able to fully inventory.

Engineers who leave Alliance Space for Mivenia after corporate disputes routinely produce work there that their former employers consider either proprietary or dangerous, the Collective's policy of not sharing client work and not being subject to Alliance intellectual property law creates a practical reality where what is built on Mivenia stays on Mivenia until the builder chooses otherwise. Former employers who want the work destroyed or recovered have found the Collective's position on this consistent and non-negotiable.
planets.desc: Mivenia is where good engineers go when they want to build things without asking permission. The Collective has maintained the charter not out of political principle but because unrestricted technical work is profitable and because the alternative, corporate or state oversight, would destroy what makes Mivenia valuable. The Alliance monitors Mivenia from a cautious distance and occasionally makes formal protests about the technology that comes out of it. The Collective acknowledges the protests and continues.

planets.name: Mivenia Test Range
planets.atm_note: Airless, kept that way intentionally for testing purposes
planets.economy: Technical testing, enables the primary world's engineering work
planets.access_note: Collective test range, access by project assignment only. What is being tested at any given time is not publicly disclosed.
hazards: Active weapons and systems testing, live fire and experimental energy systems
Uncontrolled test events, containment failures are documented
Airless environment
planets.desc: The inner rocky body of the Mivenia system, repurposed entirely as a testing range for the Engineering Collective's projects. The lack of atmosphere makes containment cleaner for most categories of test. The range is in continuous use; what is being tested depends entirely on what the Collective currently has under development. Alliance intelligence analysts would very much like to know what is out there on any given day.

planets.name: Mivenia Outer Gas Body
planets.type: Gas Giant, Fuel and Test Buffer
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant, some test events are conducted in the upper atmosphere for environmental containment
planets.economy: Fuel extraction plus atmospheric test range (high-energy tests)
planets.access_note: Collective fuel platform and test operations. Fuel is available to clients by arrangement.
hazards: Active high-energy test events in upper atmosphere
Fuel platform operations
planets.desc: The outer gas giant serves the Collective both as a fuel source and as a testing environment for high-energy experiments where the primary world's surface range creates too much risk to the inhabited areas. The platform crew have developed a practical attitude toward the occasional unscheduled events that occur during tests in the upper atmosphere.

systems.name: Zunide System
systems.desc: Zunide is on the edge of the Freeland cluster, a frontier outpost that marks the approximate boundary between Freeland and the broader uncharted frontier. It is small, self-sufficient, and deeply committed to remaining that way. Charter systems further in sometimes route resupply through Zunide specifically because it has no political entanglements.

planets.name: Zunide
planets.atm_note: Thin at altitude, breathable throughout inhabited zones
planets.grav_note: Below standard, residents adapt over time; visitors sometimes find movement unexpectedly easy
planets.demographics: Mixed, heavily transient population of frontier operators
planets.government: Outpost Council (minimal structure, primarily resource management and emergency response)
planets.economy: Resupply, cold storage, equipment rental, frontier guide services
planets.access_note: Open under charter. The Council does not ask questions and does not provide answers to parties who arrive asking about previous visitors.
hazards: Frontier adjacent, what comes back from the deep frontier sometimes carries things that shouldn't come back
Cold environment, equipment failures in low temperatures have severe consequences
Resource limited, serious emergencies cannot be addressed with what is available here

notable_locations.name: The Outpost
notable_locations.desc: Zunide's primary settlement, functional, warm, and stocked with everything a frontier operator needs. The welcome is practical rather than warm but entirely genuine: the community here depends on transit trade and looks after the people it depends on.

notable_locations.name: The Last Light
notable_locations.desc: The bar and information exchange at the edge of the settlement. What goes out of Zunide into the frontier and what comes back in both pass through here. The proprietor knows more about frontier conditions than any published chart.

hooks: Frontier ships returning to Zunide carrying cargo the crew will not discuss are documented often enough that the Outpost Council has an informal protocol for them, a period of observation, careful indirect inquiry, and a threshold at which outside assessment becomes necessary. The community's experience with the deep frontier has produced a practical and unsentimental approach to things that come back from it that cannot be explained.

The record of frontier expeditions that fail to return on schedule and are never found is displayed at Zunide's Last Light bar, which maintains a list of vessels and departure dates going back to the outpost's founding. The proprietor's knowledge of frontier conditions, accumulated from conversations with hundreds of crews over decades, is considered by those who know to be more operationally reliable than any chart.
planets.desc: Zunide is a system that knows what it is and has made peace with it. Frontier outposts succeed by being necessary and not becoming a destination, Zunide has maintained that balance well. The community is tight, the information flows freely among the residents, and the policy toward outsiders is one of professional welcome and careful neutrality. It is the last reliable stop before the deep frontier and the first thing returning from it. That position is worth maintaining.

planets.name: Zunide-II
planets.atm_note: Airless
planets.access_note: No restrictions. The Outpost Council holds a survey claim. Frontier operators occasionally cache supplies here.
hazards: Airless
Extreme cold
No rescue capability
planets.desc: The second rocky body of the Zunide system, surveyed by the Outpost Council as part of their standard territory management. No settlement is planned or desired. Frontier operators who know the system sometimes use it to cache emergency supplies, a cache that has been accessed in genuine need more than once.

planets.name: Zunide Outer Body
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant
planets.access_note: No restrictions.
hazards: Extreme distance from any support
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Zunide system, marking the outermost navigational reference point before the true frontier begins. Ships heading into the deep frontier take their final positional fix from this body. Ships returning from the frontier confirm their position against it. It serves its function well by simply being large and consistent.

systems.name: Valtis System
systems.desc: Valtis is the primary commercial hub of the Zegitor Trade Guild, the galaxy's largest independent trade organisation operating outside both Alliance jurisdiction and corporate frameworks. The Guild is studiously neutral in all political conflicts and extraordinarily wealthy because of that neutrality. Valtis is where major Guild contracts are brokered and where the Guild's administrative functions are centred.

planets.name: Valtis
planets.atm_note: Standard, Guild maintains air quality standards throughout commercial zones
planets.demographics: Highly mixed, the Guild's neutrality makes Valtis the most cosmopolitan system outside Orion 3
planets.government: Guild Directorate (commercial governance, legally binding contracts, neutral arbitration)
planets.economy: Interstellar trade brokerage, contract arbitration, financial services, neutral logistics coordination
planets.access_note: Open entry with Guild visitor registry. Registry is non-discriminatory, the only requirement is a valid commercial purpose.
hazards: Guild contracts are legally binding in ways that Alliance law is not, violation has consequences
Corporate intelligence operations are present but the Guild's own security is formidable
Financial manipulation, the sums involved here are large enough to be destabilising if mishandled
The Guild maintains armed forces for contract enforcement that most political entities would call a navy

notable_locations.name: The Exchange Floor
notable_locations.desc: The single largest commercial trading operation in any neutral territory. Guild-brokered contracts for goods, services, and logistics across the galaxy are formalised here. The volume of what is agreed here in a single day affects prices across multiple systems.

notable_locations.name: The Arbitration Court
notable_locations.desc: The Guild's dispute resolution function. Neutral, technically sophisticated, and final, Guild arbitration rulings are honoured by parties who would ignore court orders because the alternative is having the Guild's enforcement arm involved.

notable_locations.name: The Diplomatic Quarter
notable_locations.desc: Every major faction in the galaxy maintains a diplomatic presence on Valtis specifically because the Guild will work with all of them simultaneously without it becoming a problem.

hooks: Guild arbitration at Valtis has a reputation among contract lawyers as a process where the formal outcome is occasionally supplemented by parallel informal processes, cases that cannot be cleanly resolved through arbitration are known to attract outside assets from both parties, operating in ways that technically occur off the Guild's books but whose existence is an open secret among practitioners. The Guild tolerates this within limits that are widely understood but never written down.

The Zegitor Trade Guild's intelligence capacity, maintained to protect the neutrality and commercial interests that make it function, is considered by outside analysts to be comparable to a mid-tier government intelligence service. The Guild does not publicise this. Parties who have attempted to exploit neutral territory on Valtis for operations against other parties have, consistently, found this assumption incorrect in ways that ended the attempt.

The Diplomatic Quarter on Valtis is understood by professional diplomats to be the most comprehensively monitored single location in the galaxy outside Orion 3, every faction maintaining a presence there assumes they are being observed by every other faction simultaneously, and adjusts their behaviour accordingly. What the Guild does with the intelligence it collects through this monitoring has never been definitively established, but the Guild's commercial decisions show a consistent pattern of appearing very well-informed.
planets.desc: Valtis is neutral in the way that the galaxy's wealthiest organisation can afford to be neutral, not because it lacks capability for involvement but because non-involvement is more profitable than any side it could take. The Guild has maintained this position for two centuries by being useful to everyone and by responding to violations of that neutrality with the kind of enforcement response that makes future violations less likely. The system is wealthy, orderly, and commercially sophisticated in a way that most political entities envy.

planets.name: ZTG-V2
planets.atm_note: Trace nitrogen-CO2 mix, unbreathable
planets.economy: None, surveyed, held as territorial asset
planets.access_note: Guild territorial designation, no restrictions on transit, but Guild registry required for any surface operations.
hazards: Thin toxic atmosphere
planets.desc: The second rocky world of the Valtis system, catalogued under Guild territory designation ZTG-V2. The Guild holds it as a territorial asset rather than an operational one, maintaining the claim serves legal purposes in the Guild's arbitration framework. No development is planned.

planets.name: ZTG-V Belt
planets.atm_note: Void
planets.access_note: Guild patrols the belt as a buffer zone approach to Valtis. All traffic is logged. The Guild does not ask questions, but they record everything.
hazards: Guild security monitoring, all transiting ships are identified and logged
planets.desc: The asteroid belt between Valtis's inner and outer system, maintained by the Guild as a monitored buffer zone. Guild security patrol vessels transit the belt on continuous rotation, logging all traffic. The Guild's neutrality means nothing is stopped without cause, but nothing goes unrecorded either. The data is commercially and diplomatically valuable.

planets.name: ZTG-V Outer Gas Body
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant
planets.economy: Fuel extraction, supplies Guild fleet operations from Valtis
planets.access_note: Guild fuel platform, available to registered vessels at competitive rates.
hazards: Gas giant operations
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Valtis system, where the Guild operates one of its most significant fuel platforms. The fuel here is priced at Guild-standard rates, which are consistently competitive, and available to any registered vessel regardless of faction. The Guild's fuel logistics are considered a significant element of the neutrality that makes Valtis function, everyone needs fuel.

systems.name: Nopenop System
systems.desc: Nopenop handles the operational side of the Zegitor Trade Guild, logistics, fleet management, and the physical infrastructure of moving enormous volumes of trade goods across the galaxy. Where Valtis is the Guild's commercial brain, Nopenop is its working hands. It is a less glamorous system than Valtis and considerably more useful day-to-day.

planets.name: Nopenop
planets.atm_note: Standard, industrial operational activity keeps air quality at acceptable but not pristine levels
planets.demographics: Mixed, heavy Non-Born presence in logistics and automated systems operations
planets.economy: Logistics management, fleet maintenance, cargo processing, Guild supply chain operations
planets.access_note: Open with Guild registry. Commercial visitors are directed to Valtis. Operational contracts and logistics work are handled here.
hazards: Security operations are continuous and well-resourced, the Guild's physical assets are concentrated here
Industrial operations hazards, large-scale cargo handling, ship servicing
The volume of goods moving through Nopenop makes it a target for theft operations that are correspondingly sophisticated
Being in the middle of the Guild's logistics chain without authorisation tends to produce problems quickly

notable_locations.name: The Transit Yards
notable_locations.desc: Hundreds of square kilometres of cargo processing infrastructure. The sheer volume of material handled here at any given time is difficult to comprehend at human scale.

notable_locations.name: Fleet Operations Command
notable_locations.desc: Where the Guild's fleet movements are coordinated, convoys, escorts, commercial transport routes, and the Guild's own enforcement vessels. More ships are managed from this building than most navies control.

hooks: Cargo discrepancies in Nopenop's transit yards, items moving through without corresponding filed contracts, are documented in internal Guild records at a frequency that the Guild considers acceptable given the volume of material handled, and which outside observers consider evidence of systematic exploitation of the facility's scale. The Guild investigates selectively, prioritising discrepancies that are large enough to affect commercial reputation if they become known externally.

Guild fleet coordinators at Nopenop who go silent are treated differently depending on circumstances, communication failures in the logistics chain are common enough to have standard protocols, and the line between a technical failure and a deliberate one is not always immediately apparent. Coordinators who go silent after querying specific shipments have a documented history of being found at their stations physically present but communicating nothing that helps explain what they queried or why.
planets.desc: Nopenop is the part of the Guild that makes the money-making part possible. Without the logistics infrastructure here, the contracts brokered on Valtis are agreements without execution. The Guild treats its operational arm with the same commercial seriousness it applies to everything else, Nopenop is well-funded, efficiently run, and protected because disrupting it has exactly the financial consequences that any entity contemplating disruption would prefer to avoid.

planets.name: ZTG-N2
planets.atm_note: Airless
planets.economy: Bulk cargo staging, overflow from Nopenop main operations
planets.access_note: Guild logistics operations only. Not open to commercial visitors.
hazards: Airless, all operations sealed
Industrial cargo handling at scale
planets.desc: The secondary rocky body of the Nopenop system, used by the Guild as bulk cargo staging for overflow from the main transit yards. When Nopenop's primary facilities are at capacity, which is frequently, cargo is routed here for temporary holding before onward movement. The Guild built the facility without fanfare; it works, and that is the Nopenop standard.

planets.name: Nothavar
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant
planets.economy: Fleet anchorage and maintenance, Guild enforcement vessels
planets.access_note: Guild military vessel anchorage. Not accessible to commercial or non-Guild traffic.
hazards: Guild enforcement vessels present, heavily armed
planets.desc: Named Nothavar in Guild navigational records, the outer gas giant of the Nopenop system, where the Guild maintains its primary fleet anchorage for the enforcement vessels that protect Guild operations and contracts. The size of the fleet here is not publicly disclosed. Parties who have had the opportunity to observe Nothavar from a distance tend to revise their assumptions about the Guild's military capability in an upward direction.

systems.name: Bah System
systems.desc: Bah was a prosperous Nerulian frontier world, the first system in what became the Nerulian Empire's outer ring. The Kraven consumed it in hours. What remains of the Nerulian infrastructure is buried under Kraven bio-mass and the accumulated biological transformation that follows Kraven occupation. The system now feeds Kraven expansion toward the Nemani Rift.

planets.name: Bah
planets.atm_note: Completely altered by Kraven bio-processing, no breathable zones remain
planets.access_note: Active Kraven territory. Approach within Kraven-controlled space is an act of war. No vessel engaging Kraven forces at scale has returned.
hazards: Active Kraven presence, any biological signal attracts response
Kraven bio-weapons systems active throughout system
Atmospheric toxicity, requires full environmental containment, not just respiratory protection
Unknown Kraven adaptation to Nerulian defensive technology observed here

notable_locations.name: Ruins of Bah Station
notable_locations.desc: What can be identified from long-range scan as the remnants of the Nerulian system station, buried under decades of Kraven biological processing. Nerulian historians consider it one of the significant archaeological losses of the invasion.

hooks: Nerulian archivists at San Tien have documented references to objects and structures on Bah that were considered culturally and strategically significant before the invasion, items that were not evacuated because the invasion came faster than any response could be organised. The question of what remains buried under the Kraven bio-layer on Bah is one the Archive returns to periodically, without resolution.

Long-range observation of Kraven-held systems routinely produces behavioural data that does not cleanly match established models, Kraven behaviour in any given system changes over time in ways that suggest adaptation rather than static patterns. Analysts who specialise in Kraven behaviour treat small deviations as significant data rather than noise, because the Kraven's history of adaptation means small deviations have preceded major shifts before.
planets.desc: Bah is consumed. The Nerulian world that existed here, its people, its culture, its physical infrastructure, was processed by the Kraven invasion in the early stages of the offensive that destroyed the empire. Nothing has returned to reclaim it. The Nemani Rift is the only thing that has stopped the Kraven from extending further westward from systems like Bah. For Nerulian survivors, Bah is a name that represents the beginning of everything that followed.

planets.name: Bahrel
planets.atm_note: Airless, Kraven bio-processes have not engaged with this body
planets.access_note: Kraven territory. Alliance external designation K-BH-1; Nerulian name Bahrel recorded in San Tien archives.
hazards: Kraven space, proximity to active Kraven territory
planets.desc: Known as Bahrel in Nerulian records, a small rocky companion to the primary world, catalogued in the San Tien archive under the Bah system survey records. The Nerulians had no settled presence here; it was surveyed and deemed of marginal industrial value. The Kraven bio-processing that consumed the primary world has shown no interest in this body. It remains an inert rock in a dead system, its Nerulian name surviving in archive records even as the civilisation that gave it that name did not.

planets.name: Othalveth
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant, no Kraven bio-activity detected from long-range survey
planets.access_note: Kraven space. Nerulian name Othalveth; Alliance external designation K-BH-2.
hazards: Kraven space proximity
planets.desc: Named Othalveth in Nerulian navigational records, the outer gas giant of the Bah system, used as a fuel reference point and likely a source of hydrogen extraction for the system's transit operations. The Nerulian name translates loosely as "the far wanderer." The Kraven have shown no interest in it. It remains one of the only unchanged things in a system that has been entirely transformed.

systems.name: Sicon System
systems.desc: Sicon housed the Nerulian Empire's primary scientific research complex, the most advanced research facilities the empire produced. The Kraven consumed it along with everything else, but intelligence estimates suggest the physical structures of Sicon's underground facilities may have survived in some form beneath the Kraven bio-layer. What they contained is unknown and potentially extraordinary.

planets.name: Sicon
planets.atm_note: Transformed by Kraven bio-processes, entirely replaced
planets.access_note: Active Kraven territory. Intelligence estimates that significant surviving structure may remain underground, but access is considered effectively impossible.
hazards: Kraven presence throughout
Underground facility structural integrity unknown after decades of bio-processing overhead
Any surviving technology that the Kraven cannot consume may have defensive systems still active
Nerulian automated systems of unknown function may remain operational

notable_locations.name: Sub-Strata Research Complex (estimated)
notable_locations.desc: Long-range seismic surveys suggest significant intact underground structure. The depth and composition of the Kraven bio-layer above it makes access effectively impossible with current technology. What was being researched here before the invasion is documented only in fragmentary records at the San Tien Archive.

hooks: The San Tien Archive maintains records of transmissions received on Nerulian-era encrypted frequencies that cannot be attributed to any known source, fragments that, when analysed, appear consistent with automated system outputs rather than deliberate communication. The academic consensus is that some portion of Sicon's automated research infrastructure survived the invasion and continues to operate, transmitting into space with no receiver capable of acting on the data.

The proposal to attempt a physical penetration of Sicon's underground facilities is discussed periodically in intelligence and academic circles as the highest-value impossible mission in the known galaxy. The research that the Nerulian Empire was conducting there at the time of the invasion, documented in fragmentary records that survived to San Tien, included multiple programmes that Alliance science has not been able to replicate in the decades since. Each generation of analysts produces a new version of the proposal and reaches the same conclusion about its feasibility.
planets.desc: Sicon represents the most significant single loss of scientific knowledge in the Kraven invasion. The empire's research establishment was concentrated here and nowhere else. Everything they were working on, everything they had developed, if any of it survived in the underground facilities, it is sitting under Kraven territory and has been for decades. Whether that knowledge is recoverable is not a question that can be answered without someone going to find out.

planets.name: Vethar-Sicon
planets.atm_note: Trace atmosphere, possibly modified by Kraven bio-processes interacting with outgassing, unbreathable
planets.access_note: Kraven space. Nerulian name Vethar-Sicon; Alliance external designation K-SC-1.
hazards: Kraven space proximity
Possible Kraven bio-spillover from primary world
planets.desc: Known in Nerulian records as Vethar-Sicon, "the lesser companion of Sicon", this rocky inner body was used for raw material extraction to supply the research complex on the primary world. Long-range spectroscopy has detected trace atmospheric anomalies consistent with Kraven bio-process outgassing drifting outward from Sicon, an unusual indicator of particularly intense bio-processing on the primary world. The Nerulian extraction infrastructure on Vethar-Sicon's surface was presumably minimal and is not expected to have survived.

planets.name: Ilorath
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant
planets.access_note: Kraven space. Nerulian name Ilorath; Alliance external designation K-SC-2.
hazards: Kraven space proximity
planets.desc: Named Ilorath in Nerulian navigational records, the outer gas giant of the Sicon system. The Nerulian research establishment on Sicon would have required fuel; Ilorath was the extraction source. San Tien archive records note fuel routing through the Ilorath skimming platform as a standard logistical notation in the pre-invasion operational records of the Sicon research complex. No Kraven bio-activity has been detected here. The platform is gone.

systems.name: Shev System
systems.desc: Shev was not the Nerulian capital, that honour belonged to a system now so thoroughly consumed that its location is disputed. But Shev was the administrative heart of the empire's middle territories, a world of extraordinary cultural richness that the Nerulians described as the most beautiful they had built. Its destruction is considered by survivors the most complete cultural loss of the invasion.

planets.name: Shev
planets.atm_note: Transformed, no breathable atmosphere remains
planets.access_note: Active Kraven territory.
hazards: Active Kraven presence throughout
Atmospheric lethality
Historical trauma, Nerulian survivors with personal connection to Shev have been known to pursue access despite impossibility, creating additional complications

notable_locations.name: The Old City (Lost)
notable_locations.desc: What Nerulian records describe as one of the most architecturally significant urban environments ever built. The location is known from records. Whether anything physical remains is unknown. Several Nerulian survivor communities hold annual commemorations oriented toward Shev's coordinates.

hooks: Nerulian artists whose work depicts Shev with architectural and environmental detail that exceeds any surviving documentary record are a recurring presence in diaspora communities, work that can only be explained by access to sources not in any public archive, or by something else that the artists consistently decline to discuss. The question of how the knowledge was obtained has been asked and not answered across multiple generations.

The commemorative pilgrimage tradition oriented toward Shev's coordinates has included vessels that have crossed from observation into confrontation with Kraven patrol patterns, incidents documented in Alliance military records that the communities responsible for the vessels have never publicly acknowledged. The pattern suggests that grief, over enough time, produces actions that the communities would not have chosen to explain in advance.
planets.desc: The loss of Shev is the Nerulian cultural wound that does not heal. Survivors speak of it differently than other consumed systems, not with the flat political language of military defeat but with a grief that does not diminish with time. The memorial tradition oriented toward Shev's coordinates is maintained by survivor communities throughout the galaxy. The Kraven who destroyed it have no concept of what it meant.

planets.name: Shevren
planets.atm_note: Airless
planets.access_note: Kraven space. Nerulian name Shevren recovered from diaspora memorial art; Alliance external designation K-SH-1.
hazards: Kraven space proximity
planets.desc: Known as Shevren in recovered Nerulian records, a diminutive companion to the primary world, airless and uninhabited. The name was recovered not from administrative records but from diaspora memorial art: a body of work depicting the Shev system from cultural memory that includes astronomical detail precise enough for researchers to reconstruct the system's pre-invasion configuration. Shevren appears in several such works, named in accompanying text. Whether the Nerulians had any practical relationship with it is not known. It is remembered because Shev is remembered.

planets.name: Valon
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant
planets.access_note: Kraven space. Nerulian name Valon; Alliance external designation K-SH-2.
hazards: Kraven space proximity
planets.desc: Named Valon in Nerulian astronomical records recovered from the San Tien Archive, the outer gas giant of the Shev system. Valon appears in multiple diaspora memorial depictions of the Shev system, typically rendered as a background presence in images focused on the primary world. Its role in the system's pre-invasion life was functional and unremarkable; its significance now is that it is a named thing in a named system that survivors carry in their memory.

systems.name: Capio System
systems.desc: Capio was the Nerulian Empire's primary naval construction system, home to the shipyards that built the greatest fleet the galaxy had produced up to that point. Those yards and the fleet they were building at the time of the invasion were consumed along with everything else. The Alliance has studied Nerulian naval technology from recovered fragments and considers it a significant technological benchmark.

planets.name: Capio
planets.atm_note: Transformed
planets.access_note: Active Kraven territory.
hazards: Active Kraven presence
What the Kraven adapted from Nerulian military technology, potentially including naval-scale weaponry, may be operative in this system
Structural remnants of the naval yards may exist but are completely inaccessible

notable_locations.name: The Ghost Yards
notable_locations.desc: Long-range scan suggests orbital structures of significant size still exist above Capio, the remnants of the naval shipyards. They are within Kraven territory. Whether they are occupied, studied, or simply ignored by the Kraven is not known.

hooks: Alliance naval intelligence has maintained for decades the assessment that the Nerulian fleet under construction at Capio when the invasion began included at least one vessel class that significantly exceeded anything produced before or since, based on fragmentary production records and eyewitness accounts from survivors who saw the partially-completed hulls before the invasion consumed them. What made them remarkable has never been established from the available fragments, which is itself considered the most significant gap in Alliance naval technical knowledge.

Kraven behaviour analysis applied to Capio has produced an unresolved debate among specialists: the pattern of Kraven activity around the Ghost Yards is inconsistent with the simple occupation-and-ignore pattern observed in most other consumed systems, suggesting some form of interaction with the existing structures. Whether the Kravens are studying, using, or simply encountering the orbital remnants in ways that affect their behaviour is not established.
planets.desc: Capio is where the Nerulian fleet was born and where it ended. The naval tradition that built the most capable warships the galaxy had seen before the Kravens arrived was centred here. The yards produced vessels that Alliance naval architects still reference as design benchmarks. Everything that was being built when the Kravens arrived was consumed with everything else. The Ghost Yards orbiting above, if they still exist, represent the physical remains of an industrial capability that has not been matched since.

planets.name: Capeth
planets.atm_note: Airless
planets.access_note: Kraven space. Nerulian name Capeth; Alliance external designation K-CP-1.
hazards: Kraven space proximity
planets.desc: Known as Capeth in Nerulian naval records, the inner rocky body of the Capio system. The proximity to the naval yards makes material extraction from Capeth economically logical, and fragmentary supply chain records from the San Tien Archive reference raw material sourcing from the inner system body. The scale of the Nerulian naval construction program at Capio would have required significant material throughput. Whether any extraction infrastructure remains on Capeth's surface is unknown, the Kraven have no interest in rocky bodies, but they consumed everything around it.

planets.name: Mahror
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant
planets.access_note: Kraven space. Nerulian name Mahror; Alliance external designation K-CP-2.
hazards: Kraven space proximity
planets.desc: Named Mahror in Nerulian naval records, the outer gas giant of the Capio system and the fuel supply for the empire's most important shipyard complex. The scale of operations at the Capio yards required continuous hydrogen fuel; Mahror's extraction platform was a critical node in the naval supply chain. Alliance naval intelligence analysts note that any surviving orbital infrastructure near Mahror would be of significant historical interest. Long-range survey has not identified any such structure, but the survey resolution at this distance into Kraven space is limited.

systems.name: Sarag System
systems.desc: Sarag was the Nerulian Empire's agricultural heartland, a system of exceptional fertility that fed a significant portion of the empire's population. Its loss in the early stages of the Kraven invasion accelerated the collapse of the empire's ability to sustain its remaining forces and contributed directly to the speed with which the empire fell after initial resistance.

planets.name: Sarag
planets.atm_note: Transformed, the extraordinary fertility that made Sarag valuable has been processed into Kraven bio-mass
planets.access_note: Active Kraven territory.
hazards: Kraven presence
The bio-transformed environment of a formerly lush agricultural world creates a particularly dense and active Kraven biome

notable_locations.name: The Green Grave
notable_locations.desc: What Nerulian records describe as the most fertile agricultural land in the empire, a continent of exceptional soil and climate. Kraven bio-transformation has processed this environment into its current state. The transformation is considered ecologically complete.

hooks: Agricultural genetics researchers who study Nerulian food systems have documented in the San Tien Archive detailed descriptions of crop varieties that contained traits, disease resistance, yield characteristics, adaptation profiles, that have not been replicated in any Alliance crop development programme despite the traits being clearly desirable and the Archive descriptions being technically precise. The varieties were cultivated on Sarag and exist nowhere else. The loss is considered by the relevant research community to be one of the most significant agricultural knowledge losses in recorded history.
planets.desc: Sarag's loss was strategic as well as cultural. When the Kravens took the empire's food system, they took its ability to sustain an extended defence. The agricultural empire the Nerulians had built over centuries was consumed in the same weeks as their military. Sarag is remembered not just as a loss but as a turning point, the moment when survival rather than resistance became the only viable goal.
