planets.name: Sarel
planets.atm_note: Minimal atmosphere with Kraven bio-process contamination drifting from the primary world
planets.access_note: Kraven space. Nerulian name Sarel; Alliance external designation K-SG-1.
hazards: Kraven space proximity
Atmospheric trace contamination
planets.desc: Known as Sarel in Nerulian survey records, the inner rocky body of the Sarag system. The Nerulian agricultural civilization on Sarag had no need of Sarel; it was surveyed, found to have no arable potential, and left alone. It sits in Kraven space now, inert and unchanged, while the agricultural world it shares a sun with has been entirely transformed into Kraven biomass. Trace atmospheric contamination has drifted from Sarag, a reminder of the bio-processing happening in the inner system.

planets.name: Tolverath
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant
planets.access_note: Kraven space. Nerulian name Tolverath; Alliance external designation K-SG-2.
hazards: Kraven space proximity
planets.desc: Named Tolverath in Nerulian navigational records, the outer gas giant of the Sarag system. The agricultural transport network that moved food from Sarag to other Nerulian worlds would have used Tolverath as a fuel source for the long-haul transit vessels that sustained the empire's food distribution system. Whatever fuel infrastructure existed at Tolverath is gone. The gas giant itself is unchanged, a passive witness to the destruction of the most productive food system the Nerulian Empire produced.

systems.name: Agua System
systems.desc: Agua was remarkable in the Nerulian Empire for its system of ocean worlds, multiple water-covered planets with thriving aquatic ecosystems and a significant Nerulian marine culture. The Kraven invasion reached Agua later than most systems but consumed it completely. The ocean worlds of Agua are now Kraven aquatic biomes of a kind not seen elsewhere in their territory.

planets.name: Agua Prime
planets.atm_note: Atmospheric chemistry transformed by Kraven bio-processes interacting with the oceanic environment
planets.access_note: Active Kraven territory. The aquatic Kraven variants observed here have not been encountered in other systems, their capabilities are not fully characterised.
hazards: Kraven aquatic variants, different physiology and combat profile from standard Kraven
Atmospheric toxicity prevents conventional surface approach
Oceanic depth and pressure for any sub-surface investigation
No intelligence on Kraven underwater operational patterns

notable_locations.name: Nerulian Deep Station (Lost)
notable_locations.desc: Records from the San Tien Archive describe a significant deep-sea installation on Agua Prime, Nerulian marine engineering at its most advanced. Whether it survived the invasion in any form is unknown.

hooks: Long-range marine survey instruments capable of detecting Agua Prime's oceanic conditions from outside Kraven territory have produced data across multiple independent surveys suggesting that the deep-water ecosystem is evolving in ways that do not match Kraven bio-pattern behaviour in any other system, changes that suggest either autonomous adaptation by the aquatic Kraven variants or something in the deep water that is affecting Kraven behaviour in ways that are not understood.
planets.desc: Agua is where the Kraven demonstrated that their consumption patterns adapt to any environment. The aquatic variants that appeared in Agua's ocean systems have not been observed anywhere else in Kraven territory. What they represent for Kraven capability development, whether an isolated adaptation or a template for future expansion, is a question that military analysts cannot answer without data that requires entry into Kraven territory to collect.

planets.name: Aqueth
planets.atm_note: Airless
planets.access_note: Kraven space. Nerulian name Aqueth; Alliance external designation K-AQ-1.
hazards: Kraven space proximity
planets.desc: Known as Aqueth in Nerulian survey records, a dry, airless rocky body in the Agua system. The Nerulian marine culture centred on Agua's ocean worlds had no use for a waterless rock; it was noted, named, and left alone. The Kraven have likewise shown no interest in it. Aqueth remains the one unchanged body in a system that has been thoroughly transformed, an inert witness to everything that happened around it.

planets.name: Marea-Vel
planets.atm_note: Transformed by Kraven bio-processes, atmospheric chemistry reflects interaction between Kraven biological processing and the oceanic environment of this secondary ocean world
planets.population: None, Kraven aquatic variant presence unverified on this body
planets.access_note: Kraven space. The Kraven aquatic variants documented at Agua Prime may have spread here.
hazards: Kraven space
Possible Kraven aquatic variant presence
Toxic atmosphere
planets.desc: Named Marea-Vel in Nerulian records, the secondary ocean world of the Agua system, meaning "lesser sea" in the old Nerulian coastal tongue. The Nerulian marine culture maintained settlements across multiple ocean worlds in this system; Marea-Vel's population was smaller than Agua Prime's but significant. It was consumed along with everything else. Long-range survey suggests atmospheric transformation similar to the primary world, though whether the distinctive Kraven aquatic variants observed at Agua Prime have spread here has not been verified.

systems.name: Bet System
systems.desc: Bet was the communication nexus of the Nerulian Empire, a system whose location made it the routing centre for long-range communication across the empire's territory. The Kraven took it in the first wave specifically to blind the empire's ability to coordinate a response. The communication systems were destroyed almost immediately. What remains is silence.

planets.name: Bet
planets.atm_note: Transformed
planets.access_note: Active Kraven territory.
hazards: Active Kraven presence
The communication infrastructure ruins may contain functional elements, whether those elements are dangerous is not characterised

notable_locations.name: Central Relay Ruins
notable_locations.desc: The physical remains of the communication relay network that connected the Nerulian Empire. The strategic importance of its destruction in the first hours of the invasion cannot be overstated, it is the reason the empire could not coordinate a response to the attack.

hooks: Signals received on old Nerulian communication frequencies that cannot be attributed to any San Tien transmitter or known diaspora installation have been documented in Alliance communication logs spanning several decades, with source triangulations pointing consistently toward the former location of Bet's central relay network. The signals are fragmented, irregular, and undecodable with current Nerulian protocol keys, which has not prevented their existence from being a significant and unresolved item in the intelligence community's Kraven Space monitoring files.
planets.desc: Bet was taken first, and taking it first was probably the single decision that made the Kraven invasion as devastating as it was. Without the communication network, the empire's systems could not warn each other, could not coordinate defence, could not request aid. By the time any individual world understood what was happening at scale, it was already too late. The silence that replaced the network is still felt by Nerulian survivors as a specific kind of wound.

planets.name: Bethar
planets.atm_note: Airless
planets.access_note: Kraven space. Nerulian name Bethar; Alliance external designation K-BT-1.
hazards: Kraven space proximity
planets.desc: Known as Bethar in Nerulian records, the inner rocky body of the Bet system. The communication relay network that made Bet strategically critical was on the primary world; Bethar had no role in that infrastructure. It exists as an unremarkable rock in the system where the Nerulian Empire's ability to respond to its own destruction was severed. The anomalous signals triangulated toward the Bet system do not originate from Bethar.

planets.name: Soloth
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant
planets.access_note: Kraven space. Nerulian name Soloth; Alliance external designation K-BT-2.
hazards: Kraven space proximity
planets.desc: Named Soloth in Nerulian navigational records, the outer gas giant of the Bet system. The communication relay infrastructure on Bet Prime required fuel for the relay vessels and maintenance craft that kept the network operational; Soloth was the supply source. The anomalous signals received on old Nerulian communication frequencies that analysts have triangulated toward the Bet system do not originate from Soloth, long-range survey places the likely source on the primary world's surface.

systems.name: Ghash System
systems.desc: Ghash was the Nerulian Empire's heavy industrial heartland, metal processing, large-scale manufacturing, and the material production that sustained the empire's construction projects. Its loss severed the supply chain for everything the empire was building. The Kraven bio-processing has transformed the industrial landscape into something that produces only biomass.

planets.name: Ghash
planets.atm_note: Transformed, industrial contamination has been layered over by Kraven bio-processing to produce an exceptionally hostile atmospheric chemistry
planets.access_note: Active Kraven territory. Atmospheric contamination is extreme even by Kraven territory standards.
hazards: Kraven presence
Atmospheric chemistry is both Kraven-transformed and industrially contaminated, lethal in double the normal number of ways
Industrial ruins containing pressurised systems, chemical reserves, and automated machinery of unknown state

notable_locations.name: The Smelting Complexes
notable_locations.desc: Long-range scan identifies what appear to be the physical remains of the processing complexes, enormous structures partially consumed and partially preserved by Kraven bio-processing. They may contain recoverable Nerulian manufacturing technology if anyone could get to them.

hooks: Materials scientists who study the Nerulian Empire's industrial output have identified from surviving manufactured objects a specific alloy whose formula is not documented in any archived record, an alloy whose properties are considered extraordinary by current standards and that appears to have been produced exclusively on Ghash. The theoretical possibility that uncontaminated samples exist in shielded sections of the Smelting Complexes is considered real by the research community. The practical possibility of accessing them is not.

Kraven behavioural analysis applied to Ghash has produced an ongoing disagreement among specialists about whether the pattern of Kraven activity around the industrial ruins represents active interaction with the structures or simply elevated presence as a consequence of the system's biological density. The disagreement has not been resolved by the available data and cannot be resolved without direct observation from within Kraven territory.
planets.desc: Ghash built what the Nerulian Empire needed to sustain its ambitions. When it fell, everything that depended on it fell with it. The industrial infrastructure, enormous, complex, deeply integrated into the empire's supply chain, is now buried under Kraven bio-layer and the atmospheric chemistry of both industrial contamination and biological transformation. It is, like all of Kraven Space, simultaneously a graveyard and a territory that functions for its current inhabitants in ways that the previous ones would find completely alien.

planets.name: Ghareth
planets.atm_note: Industrial contamination drifted from primary world, trace heavy metals and chemical compounds
planets.access_note: Kraven space. Nerulian name Ghareth; Alliance external designation K-GH-1.
hazards: Kraven space proximity
Trace industrial contamination in atmosphere
planets.desc: Known as Ghareth in Nerulian industrial records, the inner rocky body of the Ghash system and a primary source of raw material for the Ghash smelting complexes. Long-range spectroscopy has detected trace industrial contamination consistent with heavy metal compounds drifting from Ghash Prime's industrial history, contamination that predates the Kraven invasion by centuries and persists in Ghareth's thin atmosphere. The extraction operations on Ghareth fed the industrial machinery that sustained the Nerulian Empire's construction capability. When Ghash fell, so did Ghareth's purpose.

planets.name: Tolmaveth
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant
planets.access_note: Kraven space. Nerulian name Tolmaveth; Alliance external designation K-GH-2.
hazards: Kraven space proximity
planets.desc: Named Tolmaveth in Nerulian navigational records, the outer gas giant of the Ghash system. The scale of Ghash Prime's industrial operations demanded continuous fuel supply; the Tolmaveth extraction platform was one of the largest in the empire's fuel supply network. Significant orbital infrastructure would have been built here. Whether any trace of it remains is unknown, Ghash's Kraven bio-layer is among the densest observed in their territory, and what lies beneath the transformation at surface level is not visible to long-range survey. Tolmaveth itself remains unchanged.

systems.name: Heaven System
systems.desc: Heaven is a system unlike any other in the known galaxy, the primary body is not a planet but a vast field of floating ruins suspended in space, defying conventional physics in a way that has never been adequately explained by any scientific framework. The Bottenbak cult controls access, claims the ruins as sacred territory, and is in an ongoing conflict with the Berilian Order's Patriark Inquisition forces, who view the cult's theology as heresy requiring correction.

planets.name: Heaven Ruins
planets.atm_note: Breathable throughout the ruins despite their spatial configuration, widely regarded as a direct consequence of the magical properties that keep the structure floating
planets.grav_note: Artificial gravity zones throughout the ruins, localised and inconsistent. Moving between sections can involve significant gravitational shifts.
planets.population: ~30,000, cult members, pilgrims under supervision, researchers who have received access
planets.demographics: Mixed, the cult accepts members of all races; Patriark presence is adversarial rather than resident
planets.government: Bottenbak Council of Ascendants (theocratic governance through magical authority)
planets.tech_level: Combination of advanced pre-existing systems and magical infrastructure
planets.economy: Pilgrimage services, magical knowledge trade, artifact study, limited material extraction from ruin structures
planets.access_note: Bottenbak Cult controls all access. Pilgrims are admitted under supervision. Researchers may petition for access. The Berilian Order is actively denied entry and responds with intermittent military pressure.
hazards: Gravitational anomalies, standard navigation instruments unreliable in proximity to the ruins
Bottenbak Cult security forces protect the ruins with methods that combine conventional weapons and magical capabilities
Berilian Order Inquisition forces operate in the system outer boundary, violent clashes with cult vessels are regular

The ruins themselves contain sections where the physics are locally altered, fire does not behave predictably, objects fall in unexpected directions, time is reported to move differently by multiple independent observers
Unknown origin and nature of the magical properties, the ruins may react to certain actions in ways that cannot be predicted

notable_locations.name: The Central Spire
notable_locations.desc: The tallest surviving structure in the ruin field, the spiritual centre of Bottenbak theology and the location from which the Cult's Council of Ascendants governs. Non-members who have seen it describe it as architecturally unlike anything in the known galaxy, suggesting a civilisation of unknown origin built what Heaven once was.

notable_locations.name: The Archive of Ascent
notable_locations.desc: The Cult's collection of knowledge about the ruins, their magic, and the theology built around them. Academics who have gained access consider it the most significant single body of magical scholarship available outside the Mubothen Empire.

notable_locations.name: The Perimeter Conflict Zone
notable_locations.desc: The outer approach to the system where Bottenbak defence vessels and Berilian Order Inquisition ships regularly engage. The conflict is low-intensity by conventional military standards but ongoing. The dead from both sides are recovered and treated according to their respective traditions, even enemies here maintain certain protocols.

hooks: The Bottenbak Cult and the Berilian Order Inquisition are known to have communicated indirectly through third-party carriers on multiple occasions despite their ongoing armed conflict, both organisations use couriers with no institutional affiliation for messages they consider too sensitive to transmit through channels either party could intercept. The practice is established enough that there is an informal market for neutral couriers willing to make the transit through the perimeter conflict zone.

Researchers who have been granted access to the Archive of Ascent and subsequently lost contact with their originating institutions are documented at a frequency that has made academic bodies cautious about approving applications for access without extensive safeguards. The Bottenbak Cult's explanation, that the researcher departed of their own accord, is consistent across all cases and consistently unverifiable, as the researchers do not appear at any subsequent location in any accessible record.

Changes in the Bottenbak Council's public communication pattern, correlated against Berilian Order Inquisition patrol intensity increases in the Heaven system, have been noted by observers who track both simultaneously. The correlation has held across several cycles, suggesting that the Inquisition has access to information about conditions inside the ruins that the Cult does not publish, or that the Inquisition can observe the ruins in ways that are not apparent from outside.
planets.desc: Heaven defies physics and defies easy categorisation. The ruins float in space, breathe, and seem to respond to the people inside them in ways that researchers cannot systematically quantify. The Bottenbak Cult has built a theology around what they found here and defends it with the conviction of people who have seen the evidence with their own eyes. The Berilian Order considers that theology dangerous and its practitioners heretics. The result is a system in a permanent low-level state of religious conflict around something that both sides agree is genuinely, undeniably strange.

planets.name: Hesrath
planets.atm_note: Airless, but navigation instruments behave anomalously in proximity, consistent with the broader system's physical irregularities
planets.grav_note: Gravitational readings fluctuate, same anomalous pattern as the ruins field
planets.access_note: Cult territorial claim, within the system's anomalous zone. Berilian Order has contested this claim.
hazards: Gravitational anomalies, same pattern as the broader system
Navigation instrument unreliability
planets.desc: Named Hesrath by the Bottenbak Cult, one of the few conventional rocky bodies in the Heaven system. The Cult claimed it as sacred territory on the grounds that the anomalous properties of the system extend to this body. Navigation instruments behave erratically near Hesrath in the same way they do throughout the system. The Cult has placed no permanent presence here but uses the name in ceremonial mapping of the Heaven system's sacred boundary.

planets.name: Eon-Hem
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant composition, but the gas giant itself produces electromagnetic readings inconsistent with standard gas giant physics
planets.grav_note: Standard high gravity but with anomalous periodic fluctuations
planets.access_note: No formal restrictions but the anomalous electromagnetic output interferes with navigation at close range.
hazards: Electromagnetic anomalies affecting navigation instruments
Gas giant approach hazards
planets.desc: Named Eon-Hem by the Bottenbak Cult, "the threshold of the far" in their theological vocabulary, the outer gas giant of the Heaven system. Eon-Hem produces electromagnetic readings that scientists have been unable to attribute to standard gas giant physics. The Cult considers it a boundary marker: the point where the sacred properties of the Heaven system end and normal space begins. Alliance scientists have a different vocabulary for the same observation and no better explanation of what is causing the readings.

systems.name: Zoana System
systems.desc: Zoana exists because several corporations looked at its mineral content, its distance from meaningful regulation, and its existing population and made a calculation. The calculation produced the current arrangement: a corporate exploitation system where multiple corporate interests compete for extraction rights and the local population provides labour under terms that would not be legal in Alliance Space.

planets.name: Zoana
planets.atm_note: Breathable but carrying industrial output from extraction operations, quality declining year over year
planets.demographics: Mixed, predominantly Non-Born and human labour force under corporate contract terms
planets.government: Corporate Joint Administration Committee (no meaningful civilian governance)
planets.economy: Mineral extraction, heavy industry, corporate logistics
planets.access_note: Visitor access requires corporate contractor status or specific business purpose. Worker entry is on corporate-controlled terms.
hazards: Corporate security forces with no external oversight accountability
Labour conditions that would be illegal in regulated space, contract terms enforced through debt and isolation
Multiple corporate jurisdictions create legal grey zones where nothing clearly applies
Environmental degradation ongoing, long-term habitability of Zoana is being consumed by current operations

notable_locations.name: The Corporate Compounds
notable_locations.desc: Each major corporation operating on Zoana maintains a separate walled compound, better-equipped, better-fed, and insulated from the worker communities surrounding them. Relations between compounds range from competitive to hostile.

notable_locations.name: Worker Settlements
notable_locations.desc: The communities that have formed around the extraction sites, not planned, not supported by corporate infrastructure beyond minimum labour requirements. Self-organized, resilient, and accumulating grievances at a steady rate.

hooks: Documentation of Zoana worker contract terms has reached Alliance legal advocates on multiple occasions through couriers willing to transit corporate security, terms that, under Alliance law, would constitute unlawful labour conditions in every jurisdiction the Alliance recognises. The documentation has been reviewed, confirmed as genuine, and consistently failed to produce regulatory action, which advocates who work on the issue attribute to the political influence of the corporations involved rather than any deficiency in the evidence.

The pattern of corporate sabotage between competing factions on Zoana has escalated through several distinct phases across two decades, each phase producing a crisis in shared infrastructure, a temporary resolution through external pressure, and a subsequent escalation. Workers who have lived through multiple cycles treat the joint administration committee's deadlocks as predictable and the damage to shared infrastructure as an expected background condition of life on the planet.
planets.desc: Zoana is what happens at the intersection of valuable resources, minimal regulation, and corporate competition. The exploitation of what is here has been ongoing for two decades. The corporations involved have made the calculations about local population welfare and environmental impact and reached the same conclusion each time: the current arrangement is acceptable until it stops being profitable. Players on Zoana will find people who need help and corporations that do not want them to provide it.

planets.name: Zoana Minor
planets.atm_note: Airless
planets.economy: Secondary mineral extraction, less productive than primary world but disputed by same factions
planets.access_note: Corporate contractor affiliation required. The same jurisdiction disputes from the primary world apply here.
hazards: Corporate security forces
Airless environment, full suit required
Same jurisdictional disputes as primary world
planets.desc: Called Zoana Minor by the workers and operators who live here, a distinction that does not appear in any corporate official documentation, which refers to it only as a secondary extraction site. Less productive than Zoana Prime but close enough to the existing operations to be worth the jurisdictional fighting. Workers here experience the same conditions as on the primary world with the added hazard of the airless environment and the occasional escalation when competing corporate security forces occupy the same extraction site.

planets.name: Zoana-Gath
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant
planets.economy: Fuel extraction, contested by the same factions as the planetary operations
planets.access_note: Corporate fuel platform, access requires contractor clearance.
hazards: Corporate jurisdiction disputes extend to this platform
Gas giant operations
planets.desc: Named Zoana-Gath by the fuel platform crew in the absence of any corporate agreed designation, the outer gas giant of the Zoana system. A fuel extraction platform operates here under the same contested corporate jurisdiction as everything else in the system. The three corporations have been unable to agree on fuel distribution terms for two years. The platform operates anyway because none of the three parties can afford to have it not operate.

systems.name: Asar System
systems.desc: Asar was built as Harsh Corp's exclusive vacation destination, a system of genuine natural beauty developed with the kind of investment a major corporation makes when it wants to give its executive class something extraordinary. When Torc Corp's hostile takeover of Harsh sent the parent corporation into collapse, the mercenaries who had been providing Asar's security stopped receiving payment. They kept the system instead.

planets.name: Asar Prime
planets.atm_note: Pristine, the exceptional natural environment was what Harsh Corp built around
planets.faction: Asar Mercenary Council (former Harsh Corp security)
planets.population: ~200,000, former resort staff, mercenaries, and opportunistic new arrivals
planets.demographics: Mixed, the former staff community has remained; the original luxury clientele has not returned
planets.government: Mercenary Council (armed authority with no formal legitimacy)
planets.economy: Fragmented, resort infrastructure exists but operates informally, some tourism from adventurous visitors, mercenary services, strategic goods trade
planets.access_note: No official entry restrictions but Mercenary Council monitors all arrivals. Parties connected to Torc Corp or making claims related to the Harsh Corp takeover should expect a hostile reception.
hazards: Mercenary Council is well-armed and has the run of infrastructure originally designed for a much larger security operation
Post-corporate legal vacuum, no consistent rule of law, disputes resolved by whoever has more firepower
The exceptional natural environment has been maintained by people who liked it, but without corporate maintenance investment some facilities are deteriorating
Torc Corp has filed several legal claims to the system that have not been resolved

notable_locations.name: The Grand Resort Complex
notable_locations.desc: The centrepiece of what Harsh Corp built, an extraordinary luxury facility that was once the most exclusive vacation destination within several sectors. Still physically intact. Currently occupied by mercenary command and various informal businesses that have moved in.

notable_locations.name: The Natural Preserves
notable_locations.desc: The areas of Asar Prime that were kept as natural environment, the reason Harsh Corp chose this system. Genuinely remarkable. The mercenary council has maintained them, partly out of appreciation and partly because they understand that what makes Asar valuable is still here.

hooks: Former Harsh Corp executives who have attempted to assert ownership claims over Asar assets have a documented and consistent experience: the mercenary council acknowledges the claim, holds the claimant pending review, and the review process produces no resolution that satisfies any legal standard any party would accept. The council has been conducting these reviews since the takeover and has not concluded one in a manner unfavourable to itself.

Torc Corp's legal claim to Asar is filed and active in three jurisdictions simultaneously, the Alliance, the Zegitor Trade Guild's arbitration framework, and the Torc Federation's own courts. The claim has been pending long enough that it has become a background feature of the system rather than an active pressure. The mercenary council has operated continuously throughout the legal proceedings as if the claim does not exist.

The mercenary council on Asar includes several members whose influence exceeds their apparent rank or capability, individuals who arrived in the period immediately following the Harsh Corp withdrawal and whose subsequent rise in the council appears connected to knowledge or discoveries they have never shared publicly. The natural preserves are consistently mentioned in accounts of the post-takeover period as the area where the most significant findings were made.
planets.desc: Asar is a beautiful system with a complicated ownership problem. The mercenaries who took it did so in the practical vacuum created by the Harsh Corp collapse, and have made something of it, they've maintained what Harsh Corp built because the alternative was allowing it to deteriorate, and deterioration serves no one. Whether any legitimate authority will ever reassert control over Asar is uncertain. Whether that authority would be an improvement is a question the current residents are prepared to debate with weapons.

planets.name: Asar-II
planets.atm_note: Thin but breathable at lower elevations, Harsh Corp surveyed it for resort development that never proceeded
planets.access_note: The Council holds this under the same informal ownership as everything else in the system. No developed facilities, occasional use as a training ground.
hazards: Low gravity
Thin atmosphere at altitude
Mercenary Council training exercises, intermittent
planets.desc: The second world of the Asar system, surveyed by Harsh Corp as a potential secondary resort location and deemed insufficiently spectacular compared to the primary world. The mercenary council uses it occasionally as a training ground, the low gravity and varied terrain suit certain exercise types. The Harsh Corp survey notes describe the scenery as "adequate". The mercenaries have stopped reading Harsh Corp documents.

planets.name: Asar Outer Gas Body
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant
planets.economy: Fuel extraction, self-sufficiency fuel supply for mercenary operations
planets.access_note: The Council allows visiting ships to purchase fuel at market rates, it is a revenue source. The platform crew are armed.
hazards: Armed mercenary crew
Gas giant operations on aging Harsh Corp infrastructure
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Asar system, where the mercenary council maintains the fuel extraction platform that Harsh Corp built and that the mercenaries kept running because self-sufficiency in fuel was the first operational priority after they took the system. The platform is aging and maintained with determination rather than optimal parts, but it works. Visiting ships can purchase fuel, which has become a modest secondary income stream for the council.

systems.name: Solar System
systems.classification: Ancient Origin System, Abandoned Ghost World
systems.desc: The Solar System is where humanity began and where it ended, for a time. Earth, the original homeworld, was abandoned in 2530 CE when its biosphere finally failed beyond the point of human habitation. Mars, where terraforming was attempted and ultimately abandoned, went dark around the same time. The last surviving human presence was the Saturn colony, the main settlement of the species in its final pre-departure years. In 2530 CE, the generation ship Palentium departed from the Saturnian system carrying what was left of humanity on a 1,922-year journey that would end at a world that now bears the ship's name. The Saturn colony collapsed during that journey, its power systems failing without the expertise and resources of the departed population. By the time the generation ship reached Palentium in 4452 CE, the Solar System had been dark for centuries. It was rediscovered by Alliance survey teams in 5287 CE, nearly 800 years abandoned, its worlds preserved by vacuum and time into something between an archaeological site and a monument. The Alliance has maintained it under special preservation designation since. Most humans who visit experience something that does not map cleanly to any other kind of emotion.

planets.name: Earth
planets.atm_note: The atmosphere remains partially breathable in lower elevations but the biosphere has been in systemic collapse since before the 2530 departure, industrial toxins, collapsed oxygen-producing ecosystems, and centuries of unmanaged atmospheric chemistry have left it marginal at best and lethal in many zones. Respirator required outside sealed areas.
planets.demographics: None, Alliance survey and preservation teams conduct short rotations only
planets.access_note: Access requires Alliance Archaeological Authority permits. Short-rotation research teams only. The surface is treated as an active archaeological site. No permanent habitation permitted.
hazards: Atmosphere, degraded and toxic in many zones; respirator essential outside sealed preservation shelters
Structural collapse, centuries of abandonment have made most built structures unreliable or lethal to enter without survey
The biosphere collapse that drove the 2530 departure is not reversed; some ecological hazards remain active
The emotional weight of the site, not a safety hazard, but reported by virtually every team that has worked here

notable_locations.name: The Old Cities (Ruins)
notable_locations.desc: The great urban centres of ancient Earth, now centuries into decay. Alliance preservation teams have stabilised the most structurally sound sections of several cities. Walking through them is the most disorienting archaeological experience in the known galaxy: recognisable human architecture, completely empty, frozen in the last years of habitation. The streets are intact. The vehicles are still there. The departure was not orderly.

notable_locations.name: The Final Departure Record
notable_locations.desc: The location from which the generation ship Palentium launched its last transport shuttles from the Saturnian system had no equivalent on Earth's surface, the planet had already been abandoned when the ship departed. But the Preservation Authority has identified and marked what it believes is the last permanently inhabited location on Earth, abandoned shortly before 2530 CE. A small sealed monument stands there.

notable_locations.name: The Collapsed Ecosystems
notable_locations.desc: Large sections of Earth's surface show the ecology of a world that was dying before it was abandoned, soil chemistry altered by centuries of industrial use, collapsed forest zones, dry riverbeds, and coastal areas that no longer match the pre-industrial maps. The scale of what was done to the planet is visible from orbit.

hooks: Archaeological teams working Earth's abandoned urban zones have found evidence of accelerated and apparently planned removal of specific categories of material in the final years before abandonment, systematic clearances of certain record types, laboratories, and personal archives that do not match the pattern of general departure. The Preservation Authority has classified the relevant findings. Researchers who have seen them before classification describe the pattern as suggesting someone knew what was coming and chose what to take.

The question of whether Earth's biosphere failure was entirely natural, the result of centuries of industrial activity and ecological mismanagement, or whether it was accelerated by deliberate action in the final decades before 2530 is not a fringe question in the academic community that studies the departure. The data is incomplete. The relevant records were among those most systematically removed. The conclusion that the evidence supports the deliberate-acceleration hypothesis is held quietly by researchers who understand the political implications of saying it publicly.

Structures on Earth that should have been uninhabited for centuries have shown signs of very recent disturbance in Alliance survey sweeps conducted across multiple years. The Preservation Authority attributes these findings to settlement and equipment instability. The survey teams that made the initial reports used different language before the official finding was issued.
planets.desc: Earth is the origin of everything and the monument to what was lost. The world that produced the species now spanning the galaxy was abandoned in 2530 CE, its biosphere too far gone, its population too reduced, the resources needed to reverse the damage beyond what remained. The people who left were not the last humans; they were the last humans in the solar system, on their way to being the last humans anywhere. What they left behind was a planet in collapse: cities intact, roads empty, the ecosystem failing in slow motion. Nearly a thousand years of abandonment later, it is preserved and studied. The silence here is not peaceful. It is the silence of the end of a chapter that began before recorded history.

planets.name: Mercury
planets.atm_note: Essentially no atmosphere, exosphere of solar-wind particles only. Extreme temperature variance between sunlit side (+430°C) and night side (−180°C).
planets.grav_note: 0.38g, the smallest and innermost planet of the Solar System
planets.population: Uninhabited, small rotating survey teams only
planets.access_note: Alliance Preservation Authority permits required. Rotating survey teams conduct short operations. No permanent habitation.
hazards: Extreme thermal cycling, equipment must be rated for the full range
No atmosphere, full environmental suit required throughout
Solar radiation, proximity to Sol requires substantial shielding
Micrometeorite impacts, surface is actively cratered
planets.desc: Mercury was never permanently settled in humanity's expansion era, the conditions made the investment hard to justify when better worlds were available. It was a survey reference point and a mineral prospect. It is now the most unchanged body in the Solar System: still ancient, still blasted by Sol, its cratered surface recording billions of years of impact history that the absence of geological activity has perfectly preserved. Alliance survey teams study it in rotation. Nothing about it has changed since the system was abandoned. Nothing about it ever changed at all.

planets.name: Venus
planets.atm_note: Crushing atmosphere of CO2 and sulphuric acid clouds, surface pressure 90× Earth's, surface temperature ~465°C. Never breathable at any altitude without full environmental containment.
planets.grav_note: 0.9g, nearly Earth-sized
planets.population: Uninhabited, rotating survey teams occasionally operate atmospheric stations
planets.access_note: No surface access at acceptable cost. Atmospheric platforms at altitude require extensive preparation. Preservation Authority permits required.
hazards: Surface is instantly lethal without specialised high-pressure, high-temperature rated suits
Atmospheric sulphuric acid, corrosive to most standard equipment
Crushing pressure at surface and lower altitudes
Maintaining platforms at altitude is expensive; the risks of failure are non-survivable
planets.desc: Venus was never colonised by humanity, the conditions were simply too extreme for any practical permanent settlement with the technology of the early expansion era. It was studied from orbit and from brief atmospheric missions. Old Earth cultural traditions associated it with beauty because of how it looked from Earth's surface; the people who went close enough to look properly had a different vocabulary. Alliance survey teams occasionally deploy atmospheric stations to study the ongoing geological and atmospheric dynamics. Venus is unchanged by everything that happened to the solar system. It will still be here long after everything else in the system has turned to dust.

planets.name: Mars
planets.atm_note: Thin CO2 atmosphere, the terraforming programmes begun in the early expansion era increased atmospheric density and produced isolated breathable zones but never achieved a stable self-sustaining atmosphere. With the population gone and the atmospheric processors unmaintained for centuries, the partial terraforming has been slowly reversing.
planets.grav_note: 0.38g, unchanged by centuries of abandonment
planets.population: Uninhabited, abandoned with the solar system in 2530 CE
planets.demographics: None, rotating Preservation Authority survey teams only
planets.access_note: Alliance Preservation Authority permits required. The habitat domes are structurally compromised after centuries without maintenance; surface access outside surveyed corridors is dangerous.
hazards: Thin atmosphere, full respiratory assistance required; the partial terraforming has been reversing for centuries and breathable zone pressure is declining
Habitat dome structural failure, centuries of unmaintained infrastructure makes many settlements dangerous to enter
Dust storms, planet-scale events still occur; the weather pattern continues without population
Abandoned atmospheric processors, some remain partially operational in unpredictable states

notable_locations.name: Olympus Mons
notable_locations.desc: The largest volcano in the Solar System, unchanged by everything that happened to humanity. Its summit extends above most of the Martian atmosphere. Survey teams find it one of the few places on Mars where the scale of the landscape makes the silence feel appropriate rather than wrong.

notable_locations.name: Valles Marineris
notable_locations.desc: A canyon system stretching across a quarter of Mars's circumference. The lower sections, where atmospheric pressure was highest, were among the most densely settled areas. The settlements are intact, abandoned mid-occupation, preserved by the cold and the thin air. Everything the last Martians left behind is still there.

notable_locations.name: The Old Colony Domes (Abandoned)
notable_locations.desc: The habitat domes that housed the Martian population, from the earliest primitive shelters to the final large-scale installations. Some are structurally intact; others have collapsed. Preservation Authority teams have catalogued them but most remain as found: abandoned mid-life, centuries ago, by people who did not expect to come back.

planets.desc: Mars was where humanity proved it could live somewhere else. The terraforming programmes that began in the early expansion era brought the planet closer to habitable, not close enough to sustain an atmosphere without active maintenance, and certainly not close enough to survive the departure of the population that maintained it. When the generation ship left the Saturn system in 2530 CE, Mars was already in its final decline. The Martian identity, proud, distinct, shaped by centuries of difficult living, ended with the planet's abandonment. What the Alliance survey teams found in 5287 CE was a world in the slow process of reverting: the atmospheric processors failing, the pressurised zones deflating, the cities intact and empty. The terraforming that took centuries to achieve is slowly undoing itself. In a geological timeframe, Mars will be as it was before humanity arrived.

planets.name: Asteroid Belt
planets.atm_note: Void
planets.demographics: None, survey teams operate in the Belt periodically
planets.access_note: No unified access restrictions but the Belt is designated an archaeological zone. Survey teams operate under Preservation Authority permits. The stations are structurally compromised and dangerous.
hazards: Navigation hazard, Belt debris is unchanged; the abandoned mining equipment adds additional obstacles
Station structural failure, centuries of unpressurised vacuum exposure have made most Belt stations structurally unreliable
Abandoned automated mining systems, some remain partially operational in unpredictable states
planets.desc: The Asteroid Belt between Mars and Jupiter was one of humanity's most productive and distinctive environments, the Belt community that developed there had its own culture, its own identity, and its own economy that was neither planetary nor dependent on planetary support. The Belt stations went dark with the rest of the solar system in 2530 CE. The mining equipment is still there, the stations are still there, the personal effects of the people who left are still there. The Belt is the largest archaeological field site in the Solar System. Alliance survey teams work it in rotation, cataloguing what was left behind by a culture that had no equivalent anywhere else humanity settled.

planets.name: Jupiter
planets.atm_note: Massive hydrogen-helium atmosphere with visible cloud bands and the Great Red Spot, a storm system larger than Earth that has persisted for recorded history and continues undisturbed. Upper atmosphere accessible; interior crushes any conventional vessel.
planets.grav_note: 2.53g at the cloud tops, tidal forces on moons are significant
planets.population: Uninhabited, Jovian moon settlements abandoned 2530 CE
planets.access_note: Preservation Authority permits required. Moon settlements are archaeological sites, structurally compromised after centuries of abandonment. Europa subsurface access strictly controlled for ecosystem integrity.
hazards: Radiation belts, Jupiter's radiation environment is intense; extended operation requires hardened equipment
Abandoned moon infrastructure, Ganymede and Callisto settlements are structurally compromised after centuries without maintenance
Europa subsurface ecosystem, the life in Europa's ocean has been undisturbed for nearly a thousand years; Preservation Authority protocols restrict any access to prevent contamination

notable_locations.name: Ganymede Settlements (Abandoned)
notable_locations.desc: The largest of the abandoned Jovian moon communities, Ganymede hosted the most significant off-Earth settlement in the outer Solar System. The settlements are intact, frozen in the moment of departure. Survey teams describe them as the most complete window into late pre-departure human settlement life: everything left as it was, including evidence that the departure was hurried.

notable_locations.name: Europa, Protected Biosphere
notable_locations.desc: The ice-covered moon whose subsurface ocean hosts life, life that has now been completely undisturbed for nearly a thousand years. The Preservation Authority has classified Europa as a protected biosphere and restricts all subsurface access. The ocean continues in complete isolation, evolving without observation.

notable_locations.name: Io
notable_locations.desc: The most volcanically active body in the Solar System, the sulphuric eruptions that made it expensive to operate here before abandonment continue unchanged. Whatever research infrastructure existed on Io has been comprehensively destroyed by the geological activity of the past nine centuries.

planets.desc: Jupiter is unchanged. The Great Red Spot still turns. The radiation belts are as intense as they were when the last Jovian moon community went dark. The moons that were once home to the largest off-Earth population outside Mars now host only silence and the ruins of settlements that were abandoned with the rest of the system in 2530 CE. The Jovian communities were significant, Ganymede alone housed hundreds of thousands. Their departure was part of the same overall collapse and abandonment that ended the solar human presence. The Alliance survey teams who reached the Jovian system in the 5300s found the settlements structurally intact, the equipment still in place, and the records of a community that had been alive and functional days before the departure preserved in the cold and vacuum.

planets.name: Saturn
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant composition. The rings continue their ancient rotation, unchanged.
planets.grav_note: ~1.06g at cloud tops
planets.population: Uninhabited, the Saturnian colony collapsed during the generation ship voyage, 2530–4452 CE
planets.access_note: Preservation Authority permits required. Titan surface is an active archaeological site. Ring navigation requires modern navigational equipment.
hazards: Ring system navigation, the rings require careful transit planning even with modern equipment
Titan surface structural collapse, the colony infrastructure has been deteriorating for nearly a thousand years; most pressurised structures are compromised
Titan atmosphere, thick nitrogen-methane, extremely cold, no breathable oxygen; full environmental suit required

notable_locations.name: Titan, The Last Colony (Abandoned)
notable_locations.desc: Saturn's largest moon was the main settlement of humanity in its final solar years, the largest community remaining in the Solar System when the generation ship Palentium launched from Titanian orbit in 2530 CE. The colony continued for some time after the ship's departure, then failed as its power systems degraded without the expertise and resources that had left with the ship. The timeline of the collapse is reconstructed from data logs, it took decades, not years. What remains on Titan's surface is the most complete record of humanity's final solar chapter.

notable_locations.name: The Departure Orbital (Ruins)
notable_locations.desc: The orbital infrastructure from which the generation ship Palentium launched and from which the final shuttles returned those who chose to remain. The orbital station has been in free drift since 2530 CE. Portions remain intact; portions have been destroyed by minor impacts over nine centuries. The Preservation Authority has not moved it.

notable_locations.name: The Ring System
notable_locations.desc: Saturn's iconic rings, thousands of kilometres wide, only metres thick, composed of ice and rock that has orbited unchanged through all of human history. They were the last thing the generation ship crew saw as they left the Solar System. They are the same rings. Nothing about them has changed.

planets.desc: Saturn is the last chapter of humanity's solar story. When Earth's biosphere collapsed and Mars's terraforming failed, the surviving human population concentrated in the Saturnian system, primarily on Titan, whose dense atmosphere and hydrocarbon resources made it the most sustainable option in the outer system. By 2530 CE, this was the core of humanity in the solar system. In that year, the generation ship Palentium launched from Titanian orbit carrying the population that chose to attempt the journey to a surveyed destination world. Those who remained behind, those who were too old, too sick, or simply chose not to go, continued in the Saturnian colony for some time after the ship's departure. The colony's power systems were designed for a larger and more capable population. Without the technical expertise that had departed, degradation was inevitable. The colony died over decades, its records preserved in data systems that ran on backup power long after the last human there was gone. The ship arrived at Palentium 1,922 years later. What was left of humanity was on it. The Saturnian system waited in silence for nearly 800 more years before the Alliance survey teams found it.

planets.name: Uranus
planets.atm_note: Methane produces the characteristic blue-green colouration. Extremely cold at cloud tops. The axial tilt that makes Uranus unique is unchanged.
planets.grav_note: 0.89g, nearly standard despite the scale
planets.population: Uninhabited, small research outposts abandoned with the solar system
planets.access_note: Preservation Authority zone. The extreme distance and conditions make access rare even for survey teams. The moon outpost ruins are catalogued but not regularly visited.
hazards: Extreme cold throughout the system
Extreme distance, the Uranian system is at the outer edge of the solar system's inhabited range
The seasonal variation from the 98-degree axial tilt creates multi-decade periods of polar darkness, the abandoned outposts have spent decades in continuous darkness since the system went cold
planets.desc: Uranus was never a major settlement, the small research outposts on its moons were exactly that: small, remote, and oriented toward study of the gas giant's unusual seasonal dynamics rather than any practical exploitation. They went dark with the rest of the solar system. The ice giant itself is unchanged: still tilted at its improbable angle, still cycling through its decades-long seasons. The Alliance has catalogued the moon outposts from distance. Their priority for physical survey is low, the distance, the conditions, and the limited scientific yield compared to the inner system sites make them a long-term item on a long list.

planets.name: Neptune
planets.statusLabel: Abandoned, Most Remote Outpost Gone Dark
planets.atm_note: Similar composition to Uranus but with more internal heat and more violent weather. Wind speeds up to 2,100 km/h, the most extreme in the Solar System. Unchanged by everything that happened to humanity.
planets.grav_note: 1.14g, slightly above standard
planets.population: Uninhabited, the Triton outpost was the last Solar System settlement to go dark
planets.access_note: The most distant surveyed body in the Solar System. Transit time significant even with modern drives. Preservation Authority permits required.
hazards: Extreme winds, atmospheric entry is dangerous
Extreme distance, the outermost major body of the Solar System; emergency response is not available on any practical timescale
Triton surface structural deterioration, the research installation has not been maintained for centuries

notable_locations.name: Triton Research Installation (Abandoned)
notable_locations.desc: Neptune's largest moon, a captured Kuiper Belt object orbiting backwards relative to Neptune's rotation, geologically active with nitrogen geysers. The research installation here was the most remote permanent human outpost in the Solar System. Alliance survey records indicate it went dark sometime after 2530 CE, likely among the last solar settlements to fail, given its relative self-sufficiency. The installation is physically intact. The data logs recovered from it contain the final recorded observations of humans in the Solar System proper.

planets.desc: Neptune is the last world of the Solar System, the outermost major planet, home to the most isolated and most remote research installation humanity ever maintained in its home system. The Triton outpost was the last of the solar settlements to fail; its logs, recovered by Alliance survey teams, contain the final recorded observations of any human presence in the Solar System proper. What those logs say about the final days of the Triton community, and what the researchers there knew about the state of the rest of the system as it went dark, is among the most studied documents in the Alliance Archaeological Authority's possession. Neptune itself is unchanged. It will still be here when its geological record has outlasted everything else in the system by billions of years.

systems.name: Dicamia System
systems.desc: Dicamia is one of the three known systems of the Mubothen Empire, a magical theocratic dynasty that has maintained total communications blackout for over fifty years. No external contact, no trade, no diplomatic exchange. The empire went silent and has stayed silent. What is known comes from records predating the blackout.

planets.name: Dicamia
planets.atm_note: Believed standard, no current data
planets.grav_note: Believed standard
planets.demographics: Unknown, pre-blackout records indicate mixed population under theocratic governance
planets.government: Mubothen Dynastic Theocracy (High Council of the Divine Compact)
planets.tech_level: Unknown, Mubothen technology and magical capability both were significant before blackout
planets.economy: Unknown, self-sufficient theocratic economy implied by fifty years of isolation
planets.access_note: All ships that have attempted entry into Mubothen space have either turned back or not returned. No official response to any communication in fifty years.
hazards: Complete intelligence blackout, no knowledge of current conditions
Ships that crossed the declared boundary have not returned, whatever enforcement exists is effective
Magical capability of Mubothen forces was significant before the blackout and may have developed further in isolation
Religious fundamentalism of an intensity that produced complete voluntary isolation

notable_locations.name: The Grand Theocratic Complex (Pre-Blackout)
notable_locations.desc: Records from before the blackout describe an extraordinary complex of temples, administrative structures, and magical research facilities. Whether this remains as described is entirely unknown.

hooks: Physical objects that appear to originate from Mubothen space have been documented on the open market on several occasions across the five decades of the blackout, objects whose material composition and construction methods are inconsistent with any known manufacturing tradition, and whose presence outside Mubothen territory cannot be explained by any verified transit record. Each documented case has generated significant intelligence community interest and left the object's origin unresolved.

Academic profiles of what the Mubothen Empire might have become after fifty years of isolated development, particularly the magical research programmes that were already advanced before the blackout, are produced periodically by researchers who study the pre-blackout records. The conclusions consistently involve capability projections that the researchers themselves describe as alarming, and consistently note that the only way to verify them is to obtain information that is definitionally inaccessible.
planets.desc: The Mubothen Empire went silent fifty years ago. No explanation was ever given. Ships that approach the border either turn back of their own accord or do not return. No communication has been received from inside in any form. The Alliance has periodically attempted formal contact through multiple channels and received no response. What the Mubothen Empire is now, what it believes, what it has developed, what it wants, is genuinely unknown. Whether the silence will end, and on whose terms, is one of the galaxy's significant unanswered questions.

planets.name: Verath-Osin
planets.atm_note: Pre-blackout records note a thin breathable atmosphere, no current data
planets.climate: Unknown, pre-blackout data indicates cold and barren
planets.grav_note: Pre-blackout survey data, unverified current conditions
planets.access_note: Within Mubothen space, same access restrictions as all Empire systems.
hazards: Inside Mubothen space, whatever enforcement exists
Complete intelligence blackout
planets.desc: Designated Verath-Osin in pre-blackout Mubothen records, a cold rocky world in the Dicamia system that the Empire used for material extraction to supply the theocratic construction projects on the primary world. Whether extraction operations continue in isolation is unknown. The name is taken from pre-blackout Mubothen documents; the Empire's internal designation may have changed in fifty years of silence.

planets.name: Koreth-Amon
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant composition, pre-blackout records note a fuel extraction platform operated here
planets.access_note: Within Mubothen space.
hazards: Inside Mubothen space
Complete intelligence blackout
planets.desc: Designated Koreth-Amon in pre-blackout records, the outer gas giant of the Dicamia system. Pre-blackout records indicate a fuel extraction platform operated here under Imperial supervision. Whether it continues to operate fifty years into the blackout is unknown. The Mubothen Empire was self-sufficient before the silence; the assumption is that whatever it needed from this body, it continues to take.

systems.name: Ethone System
systems.desc: Ethone was the Mubothen Empire's designated research and magical development system before the blackout, records describe it as a place where the empire's most advanced magical investigation was conducted. Whether that research continued in isolation for fifty years, and what it might have produced, are questions that make several intelligence agencies deeply uncomfortable.

planets.name: Ethone
planets.atm_note: Believed standard, no current data
planets.grav_note: Believed standard
planets.tech_level: Unknown, but magical research conducted here before blackout was considered by Alliance intelligence to be the most advanced in any faction
planets.access_note: As Dicamia, no access, no return for those who try.
hazards: Fifty years of unobserved magical research, no characterisation of what may have been developed
Pre-blackout reports classified by Alliance intelligence, content unknown

notable_locations.name: Research Spires (Pre-Blackout)
notable_locations.desc: The research complex as described in pre-blackout records, multiple large installations for magical investigation and development. No current data exists on their state.

hooks: Technology appearing on open markets with properties consistent with magical integration at a level beyond any current faction's known capability is documented in intelligence records across the five decades of the Mubothen blackout, objects whose provenance cannot be established through normal investigation and whose properties suggest development that has continued in isolation. Analysts who track these appearances note that the frequency has increased in the past decade, which is itself considered significant.
planets.desc: Ethone is the part of the Mubothen blackout that intelligence agencies find most concerning. If the magical research programs operating here before the blackout continued in isolation for fifty years, without external observation, without the constraints of diplomatic visibility, without any need to limit development based on others' reactions, the resulting capability is not something that can be estimated from outside. It is simply unknown.

planets.name: Sephalos-Mir
planets.atm_note: Pre-blackout records are silent on this body, not considered significant enough to document in external-facing records
planets.access_note: Within Mubothen space.
hazards: Inside Mubothen space
Possible magical research activity, nature and extent unknown
planets.desc: A rocky body in the Ethone system whose pre-blackout documentation is minimal, the Empire's research focus was on the primary world, and this body was a resource for that research rather than a site of it. Whether any of the magical research operations that made Ethone significant before the blackout extend to this body is not known. The name Sephalos-Mir is reconstructed from fragmentary Imperial administrative records.

planets.name: Vareth-Salon
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant
planets.access_note: Within Mubothen space.
hazards: Inside Mubothen space
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Ethone system, designated Vareth-Salon in pre-blackout Imperial records. Its role in the Empire's research support infrastructure is not documented in accessible external records. That it is within Mubothen space, fifty years unobserved, is the only current fact about it.

systems.name: Astea System
systems.desc: Astea was the outermost system of the Mubothen Empire before the blackout, the frontier of their territory and the system closest to broader galactic routes. It is the system that ships approaching Mubothen space encounter first and the one from which any future contact, if it comes, is most likely to emerge.

planets.name: Astea
planets.atm_note: Believed standard, no current data
planets.access_note: As other Mubothen systems. Astea's frontier position means it is also the most likely location of any enforcement capability directed at the boundary.
hazards: Closest Mubothen system to standard transit routes, whatever enforcement mechanism the empire uses to maintain its blackout is most active here
Any appearance of Mubothen ships or capability would first be observed from this system

notable_locations.name: The Border
notable_locations.desc: The outer edge of Mubothen-claimed space. Several navigational beacons placed before the blackout still broadcast on old frequencies, though they carry only positioning data and no content. Whether they are maintained or simply still running on autonomous power is not known.

hooks: The Astea border beacons placed before the Mubothen blackout continue to broadcast positioning data and have done so without change for fifty years, a continuity that is itself informative, suggesting that either the beacons are operating autonomously without maintenance or that the Mubothen Empire is maintaining infrastructure on the outer boundary of its territory. The distinction matters to analysts who study the blackout, and neither explanation has been confirmed.

Ships that go missing near the Mubothen border and subsequently reappear are documented in Alliance records at a rate that exceeds what navigation hazards alone would predict, crews that return without being able to account for their absence in ways that satisfy any standard debriefing protocol. Alliance intelligence has classified the accounts of multiple returned crews, which is itself the most significant public fact about the pattern.
planets.desc: Astea marks the edge. Whatever the Mubothen Empire has become in fifty years of silence is behind that border. Astea is the closest point to finding out, and the most dangerous point to approach. The empire has maintained its blackout against every attempt at contact for half a century. Whether that changes, and what changes it, will begin here.

planets.name: Telath-Verin
planets.atm_note: Pre-blackout records indicate a thin atmosphere, no current data
planets.access_note: Within Mubothen space, likely within the enforcement range of whatever keeps the border closed.
hazards: Inside Mubothen space
Closest body to the border, any enforcement capacity is likely deployed from or near here
planets.desc: The inner rocky body of the Astea system, designated Telath-Verin in pre-blackout records. Its frontier position, and the Empire's practice of maintaining border enforcement, makes this body the most likely location of whatever physical infrastructure the Empire uses to enforce its silence. Whether that infrastructure is technological, magical, or both has not been established from outside the border.

planets.name: Doreth-Kaim
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant
planets.access_note: Within Mubothen space.
hazards: Inside Mubothen space
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Astea system, designated Doreth-Kaim. The border navigation beacons placed by the Empire before the blackout are positioned near this body, it serves as the outer reference point of Mubothen-claimed space. The beacons still broadcast. Whether they are autonomously maintained or actively serviced is not known. Both possibilities say something different about what is happening inside the silence.

systems.name: Yaevis System
systems.desc: Yaevis is the most developed system in the Solar Expanse, the first one the Alliance formally catalogued and the staging point for most organised exploration further into the region. It has the infrastructure that comes from being the gateway to a frontier: good fuel, decent repair facilities, and a community that has learned to deal with people who are either heading out or just came back.

planets.name: Yaevis
planets.atm_note: Standard, clean
planets.demographics: Mixed, pioneer families, Alliance support staff, exploration contractors
planets.economy: Frontier logistics, exploration support, fuel trade, basic manufacturing, agricultural development
planets.access_note: Open under Alliance affiliation. Alliance law applies but enforcement is light, the Alliance prioritises the gateway function over regulatory detail.
hazards: Frontier conditions, resource limitations, distance from emergency response
Alliance affiliation is nominal, legal protections are theoretical in many practical situations
Information security low, everything discussed here flows back to parties tracking frontier exploration

notable_locations.name: The Pioneer Depot
notable_locations.desc: The principal resupply facility for Solar Expanse exploration. Well-stocked by frontier standards, expensive by core world standards, and the only reliable source of certain supplies for significant distance.

notable_locations.name: The Survey Office
notable_locations.desc: Alliance exploratory survey headquarters for the Solar Expanse. Maintains charts of all catalogued systems, current hazard assessments, and records of all registered exploration missions. Also where you file a claim if you find something worth claiming.

hooks: Discovery claims filed through the Yaevis Survey Office that are classified by the Alliance within hours of filing have been documented on multiple occasions, a pattern that experienced frontier operators interpret as the Alliance having active monitoring of incoming survey data and a policy of suppressing specific categories of find before they enter public record. The teams whose claims have been classified have received no explanation and are not permitted to discuss the classifications under conditions they were not required to agree to before the classification occurred.

The Pioneer Depot at Yaevis has a documented history of receiving supply shipments that contain items not on filed manifests, a pattern sufficiently consistent that depot staff have developed their own informal inventory protocols for unmanifested cargo. The items are varied and do not consistently correspond to any obvious category. The Alliance supply chain office in the core has never successfully explained the discrepancies when asked.
planets.desc: Yaevis works because frontiers need a door. Exploration of the Solar Expanse flows through this system, out through it and back through it, and the community that built up around that function has become self-sustaining. It is not glamorous. It is remarkably functional. For players heading deeper into the Solar Expanse, Yaevis is the last place where anything is reliably available and the last place where a clear head about what they are going into is possible.

planets.name: YEV-B
planets.atm_note: Trace nitrogen atmosphere, unbreathable
planets.economy: None, mineral survey indicates marginal resource potential
planets.access_note: Pioneer Council survey claim. No development planned.
hazards: Thin toxic atmosphere
No infrastructure
planets.desc: The secondary rocky body of the Yaevis system, designated YEV-B in the Alliance Survey Office catalogue. The Pioneer Council filed a survey claim as part of standard frontier territory management. The mineral survey came back marginal. The Council has more pressing concerns than developing a marginal world.

planets.name: YEV-C
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant
planets.economy: None, fuel extraction has been proposed and not actioned
planets.access_note: No restrictions.
hazards: Gas giant approach
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Yaevis system, designated YEV-C. Ships using the system as a gateway stop use it as a navigation reference. The Survey Office has proposed a fuel extraction platform here twice; the Pioneer Council has noted the proposal and declined to act on it twice.

systems.name: Nausica System
systems.desc: Nausica contains one of the most spectacular naturally occurring garden worlds in the known galaxy, a planet of extraordinary biodiversity, dramatic landscapes, and a biosphere so complex that Alliance scientists have been studying it for decades and have not finished cataloguing what lives there. The system has become a destination in itself despite its frontier location.

planets.name: Nausica
planets.atm_note: Rich, warm, exceptionally high oxygen content, visitors often report feeling unusually energetic on first arrival
planets.grav_note: Noticeably below standard, combined with the rich atmosphere makes movement feel different from any other world
planets.faction: Nausica Preservation Council (joint Alliance and independent)
planets.population: ~200,000, researchers, support staff, small permanent settler community
planets.demographics: Mixed, heavily weighted toward scientific and research personnel
planets.economy: Scientific research, nature tourism (carefully regulated), biological study, University contracts
planets.access_note: Access permit required to protect ecosystem integrity. Permits are difficult but not impossible to obtain. Unrestricted entry would destroy what makes the system worth visiting.
hazards: Megafauna, some species are genuinely dangerous to unprepared visitors
Plant toxins, beautiful environment does not mean benign; contact with certain species causes immediate medical emergencies
Easy disorientation, the biodiversity and low gravity can lead to navigation errors
Preservation enforcement, illegal collection of biological samples is treated severely

notable_locations.name: The Great Canopy
notable_locations.desc: The continent-spanning rainforest that covers Nausica's equatorial zone, the most biodiverse square kilometre of surface in the known galaxy. Researchers describe the experience of entering it as humbling.

notable_locations.name: Research Station Alpha
notable_locations.desc: The primary scientific facility, built carefully to minimise environmental impact. Home to the longest-running continuous biological study in the Solar Expanse.

notable_locations.name: The Crystal Flats
notable_locations.desc: An expanse of mineral formations produced by Nausica's unusual geological history, simultaneously a stunning natural formation and a source of unique compounds being studied for applications in materials science.

hooks: Research teams at Nausica have documented species that do not fit any established evolutionary framework derived from the known biosphere, organisms whose properties suggest either convergent evolution from a radically different origin point or something that was not present in early surveys and has appeared since. The Preservation Council manages the publication of this data carefully, recognising that certain findings attract attention that complicates the protection mandate.

Illegal bio-harvesting from Nausica is documented in Alliance enforcement records going back decades, protected species appearing in collector and pharmaceutical markets in quantities that require an ongoing supply operation rather than isolated poaching incidents. The sophistication of the operation, which has bypassed Preservation Council access controls repeatedly, is considered by enforcement analysts to require inside knowledge of the control systems.

The pressure on the Preservation Council to permit commercial development of sections of Nausica has been sustained for years by offers and political approaches through structures designed to be difficult to attribute. Observers who have tracked the pattern over multiple governance cycles consider it coordinated rather than coincidental, the same pressure applied through different vehicles by what they believe is the same underlying party.
planets.desc: Nausica is the kind of world that makes the Solar Expanse's difficult distance seem worth it. The garden world's biodiversity defies easy summary, every survey reveals new species, new interactions, new complexity in a biosphere that appears to be functioning at a level of integration not seen elsewhere. Researchers who come here tend not to leave easily. The Preservation Council's strict access controls are the only reason it remains what it is, the pressure to exploit what is here commercially is constant and not diminishing.

planets.name: NAU-B
planets.atm_note: Airless
planets.economy: None, monitoring and early warning function
planets.access_note: Preservation Council monitoring station, access requires Council clearance.
hazards: Airless, full suit required
planets.desc: The inner rocky body of the Nausica system, used by the Preservation Council as a monitoring station location. Sensors positioned here provide early warning of unauthorised approach to the garden world system. The Council installed the station after the second documented illegal bio-harvesting operation, the approach vector had come from the inner system.

planets.name: NAU-C
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant
planets.access_note: No restrictions, the Preservation Council has no claim to this body.
hazards: Gas giant approach
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Nausica system, unmarked and unremarkable. Ships approaching the system use it as a navigational reference. Commercial interest parties who have studied the system for exploitation opportunities have noted that the distance from this body to the garden world would make it a useful staging point for any operation the Preservation Council would not sanction. The Council has noted this too.

systems.name: Rautis System
systems.desc: Rautis was identified by early Solar Expanse surveys as one of the most mineral-rich systems in the region and has attracted independent mining operations accordingly. The lack of corporate control means that conditions vary widely, some operations are well-run and profitable; others are chaotic. The system has developed a rough-and-ready culture shaped by extraction work done at distance from any oversight.

planets.name: Rautis
planets.atm_note: Thin but breathable at ground level, respirators recommended for extended outdoor activity
planets.demographics: Mixed, predominantly Human and Hakari mining workers
planets.government: Loose collective governance (disputes resolved by whoever controls the most viable operations)
planets.economy: Mineral extraction, ore processing, equipment maintenance, frontier services
planets.access_note: Open, the Collective has no formal entry controls. Bring your own equipment.
hazards: Mining environment, shaft collapses, gas pockets, heavy equipment accidents are routine
Collective disputes can become violent
No medical infrastructure beyond basic field medicine
Equipment failures at this distance from resupply can be immediately life-threatening

notable_locations.name: Main Shaft Settlement
