notable_locations.desc: The largest community in the system, a mining town that has grown organically around the most productive extraction site. Functional, dense, and offering every service that a mining workforce needs including several that are only available because oversight is far away.

hooks: Simultaneous competing claims over newly discovered deposits in Rautis are a recurring feature of the system's history, the informal collective governance structure has never developed binding dispute resolution mechanisms, which means that richness of a find correlates directly with intensity of conflict around it. Workers on Rautis treat the discovery of a significant new deposit as the beginning of a dangerous period rather than good news.

Finds in Rautis mine shafts that are clearly manufactured and predate any known human operation in the system have been documented across multiple independent discoveries over the years, objects whose origin cannot be attributed to any surveyed civilisation and whose purpose has not been established. The finds are discussed openly in the mining community and treated with the practical interest of people who assess unfamiliar objects primarily by whether they can be sold.
planets.desc: Rautis runs on ore and stubbornness. The independent mining culture here has produced a community with its own norms, its own dispute resolution methods (imperfect), and its own relationship to risk (accepting). It is not comfortable by core world standards and does not aspire to be. What it produces is real value at frontier cost, and the people who do that work have a practical competence that sophisticated core-world visitors tend to underestimate.

planets.name: RAU-B
planets.atm_note: Airless
planets.access_note: No restrictions, same claim culture as the primary world.
hazards: Airless, full suit required
Claim disputes
planets.desc: The secondary rocky body of the Rautis system, attracting the overflow of claim activity from the primary world. The mineral deposits here are less productive but the lower competition makes them viable for smaller operators. The same dispute culture from the primary world applies, scaled down to proportionate stakes.

planets.name: Rautis Outer Belt
planets.atm_note: Void
planets.access_note: No restrictions. Belt operators maintain informal coordination about traffic and hazards.
hazards: Navigation hazard, irregular asteroid field
No organised rescue capacity
Claim overlaps in the belt are even harder to adjudicate than on the planetary surface
planets.desc: The outer asteroid belt of the Rautis system extends the mining operations beyond the planets. Belt operations here are smaller-scale than the primary world's shaft mines but attract independent operators who prefer the autonomy of working a claim without neighbours on all sides. The belt community has developed its own informal norms that supplement the Collective's loose governance with practical field rules.

planets.name: RAU-C
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant
planets.access_note: Frontier fuel available at competitive rates.
hazards: Aging platform equipment
Gas giant operations
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Rautis system, where the Mining Collective operates a cooperative fuel platform. The fuel pricing is competitive because the Collective votes on it, and everyone who votes uses the fuel. The platform is old and maintained by the community rather than a corporate contractor, which means it is well-maintained in the things that matter and improvised in the things that don't.

systems.name: Strides System
systems.desc: Strides functions as the mid-point between the Solar Expanse gateway systems and the deeper far frontier. Its location makes it a natural transit stop and its community has built itself entirely around that function. Ships heading deeper into the expanse typically stop here. Ships coming back from the deep expanse definitely stop here.

planets.name: Strides Station
planets.atm_note: Station-maintained throughout
planets.demographics: Heavily transient, permanent staff are a minority of any given population census
planets.government: Station Authority (practical governance, keeps the life support running and the fuel available)
planets.economy: Fuel, resupply, ship servicing, crew rest, information trade
planets.access_note: Open to all, the station needs the trade.
hazards: Deep frontier conditions, rescue and emergency response capability is limited
Information flow in both directions, what you share on Strides Station reaches audiences in both directions
Cargo disputes from deep frontier operations concentrate here

notable_locations.name: The Forward Depot
notable_locations.desc: The deepest-stocked resupply facility in the Solar Expanse outside Yaevis. Regularly restocked by trade runs and guarded carefully because it is the only one.

notable_locations.name: The Return Bar
notable_locations.desc: Where crews coming back from the deep expanse stop first. The stories told here range from routine to extraordinary. The station staff have heard enough extraordinary ones to take them seriously.

hooks: Empty ships that arrive at Strides Station registered as arrived but with no crew aboard are documented often enough that the Station Authority has a specific protocol for them, a protocol that includes a waiting period, a search procedure, and a disposition process for the vessel. The crews are never found. The ships are sold. The pattern has continued long enough that experienced transit crews treat the empty ship accounts from Strides as established fact about the deep expanse rather than rumour.

The supply chain from Yaevis to Strides Station has experienced documented delays across its operational history, delays whose frequency increases during periods when something in the Solar Expanse has attracted Alliance attention. The Station Authority manages the timing carefully and does not publicly discuss the correlation between Alliance activity in the expanse and gaps in the supply schedule.
planets.desc: Strides is the middle distance, far enough in to be genuine frontier, close enough to the gateway to feel like a border. The community is defined by its transit function in the same way as Cetune, but with the specific character of deep frontier transit: the people here are either going very far or coming back from it. Both groups have things the other finds useful. The information flow between them is the most valuable product the station produces.

planets.name: STR-A
planets.atm_note: Airless, the station uses the body for gravitational reference and material extraction
planets.economy: Station material supply, ice and mineral extraction for station consumables
planets.access_note: Station Authority operational area. The body provides water ice and basic minerals for station life support.
hazards: Airless
Station proximity, approach must be cleared with station traffic control
planets.desc: The rocky body that Strides Station orbits, not settled itself but essential to the station's function. The Station Authority mines water ice and basic minerals from its surface for station life support. Without it, the station would be entirely dependent on supply runs for consumables. The Station Authority considers it the operational foundation of their independence.

planets.name: STR-C
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant
planets.economy: Hydrogen fuel for station operations and sale to transit ships
planets.access_note: Station Authority fuel operations, available to all transit ships at posted rates.
hazards: Gas giant operations with minimal platform infrastructure
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Strides system, where the Station Authority operates a minimal fuel collection platform. The fuel collected here supplies the station's own operations and forms the primary commercial offering to transit ships. The platform is small and the collection rate is calibrated to the station's needs, deep frontier fuel operations are not a large-scale industrial concern here.

systems.name: Ongora System
systems.desc: Ongora is a frontier system that has attracted disproportionate scientific attention because of a consistently anomalous set of readings that multiple independent surveys have confirmed and none have explained. The system functions normally in every measurable way except for a set of gravitational and electromagnetic patterns that do not correspond to any known natural phenomenon.

planets.name: Ongora
planets.atm_note: Standard breathable, anomalous readings do not affect atmospheric chemistry
planets.grav_note: Standard at surface, anomalous readings are system-wide in certain electromagnetic bands, not local gravitational
planets.faction: Independent with Alliance Science Authority presence
planets.population: ~50,000, small permanent settlement and rotating research teams
planets.government: Settlement Council with Science Authority observer status
planets.economy: Research support, small-scale agriculture, frontier services
planets.access_note: Open entry, Science Authority research activity ongoing. Visitors are logged with unusual thoroughness.
hazards: Unknown nature of anomalous readings, their effects on biological systems or technology over extended exposure are undetermined
Science Authority presence has a surveillance component that extends to all system visitors
The unknown factor

notable_locations.name: The Observation Array
notable_locations.desc: Science Authority installation, a significant sensor and monitoring system deployed to study the anomalous readings. The data collected here has been flowing to Alliance research institutions for years. What conclusions have been reached have not been published.

hooks: The Alliance Science Authority's response to the Ongora anomalous readings has been tracked by independent researchers through personnel deployment records, the size of the research team stationed at the Observation Array has grown steadily over the years, which specialists interpret as the Authority finding increasingly significant results rather than reaching conclusions. The data produced by this growing team is classified at increasingly restricted levels as the team grows.

Researchers who have left the Alliance Science Authority after working at the Ongora Observation Array have a documented and consistent pattern: they do not publish independent analyses of the data they worked with. The one known attempt produced a paper that was simultaneously challenged by a legal action from the institution that funded the array and by a public statement from the Science Authority disputing the paper's methodology. The paper was not published. The researcher has not commented publicly since.
planets.desc: Ongora is the kind of system where the question matters more than the current answer. Something is producing readings that don't fit the models. The Science Authority has been studying it long enough that their continued silence on conclusions is itself informative. Whatever Ongora is, it is interesting enough to justify sustained scientific investment and sensitive enough to keep the conclusions classified.

planets.name: ONG-B
planets.atm_note: Airless, also produces anomalous readings on specific instrument types consistent with the system-wide pattern
planets.access_note: Science Authority survey territory. The anomalous instrument readings are documented here as well as throughout the system.
hazards: Anomalous instrument behaviour, same pattern as system-wide
Airless
planets.desc: The secondary rocky body of the Ongora system, included in the Science Authority's monitoring scope because it also produces the anomalous readings that define the system. Whether the readings originate from this body, pass through it, or simply affect instruments near it is one of the unresolved questions. The Authority logs data from this body and does not publish what the logs contain.

planets.name: ONG-C
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant composition, but instrument anomalies affect readings of this body in specific electromagnetic bands
planets.access_note: No formal restrictions, the Science Authority monitors it but has not claimed it.
hazards: Instrument anomalies affecting navigation near the body
Gas giant approach
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Ongora system. The anomalous readings that affect the entire system also affect instruments used to approach and survey this body, making it difficult to study accurately with standard equipment. The Science Authority has dedicated specific observation runs to this body because the pattern of how the anomaly interacts with gas giant atmospheric dynamics differs from the rest of the system, which is itself considered significant data.

systems.name: Thars System
systems.desc: Thars is in the early stages of industrial development, a frontier system that has attracted investment attention because of its resource profile and is in the process of being built up. The tension between those developing it and those who were already there is active and unresolved.

planets.name: Thars
planets.atm_note: Standard, not yet degraded by industrial output
planets.faction: Contested, Development Consortium vs established independent community
planets.demographics: Mixed, original independent community and incoming development workforce
planets.government: Contested, Development Consortium holds contracts, independent community holds cultural claim
planets.economy: Developing industrial extraction, agriculture, services for incoming development workforce
planets.access_note: Open entry but Development Consortium and independent community each monitor arrivals for different reasons.
hazards: Active political tension between Consortium and community
Development operations creating environmental changes that the original community was not consulted about
Consortium security force operating outside any accountability framework

notable_locations.name: Pioneer Town
notable_locations.desc: The original independent settlement, the community that was here before the Consortium arrived. Well-established, self-sufficient, and increasingly concerned about what the development operations mean for the land they have worked for two generations.

hooks: The pattern of Development Consortia establishing operations on land that original settler communities have farmed for generations is documented across multiple frontier systems in the Solar Expanse, always following the same sequence of contract assertions, legal ambiguity, and security force presence that creates a confrontation the original community is structurally unable to win without outside support. Frontier advocates who document these situations consider Thars a textbook case of a process they have observed many times.
planets.desc: Thars is a story playing out in slow motion that picks up pace when outside parties arrive. The development Consortium is backed by serious capital and has contracts. The people who built their lives here before the Consortium arrived have moral claim and the specific determination of people who came a long way to be left alone. Neither of those things is a legal argument in the current framework. How this resolves depends on what resources both sides can bring to bear.

planets.name: TH-B
planets.atm_note: Thin CO2 atmosphere, unbreathable
planets.access_note: Consortium survey claim filed. The independent community contests the claim but lacks the legal resources to challenge it effectively.
hazards: Consortium security patrols in system extend here
Thin toxic atmosphere
planets.desc: The secondary rocky body of the Thars system, claimed by the Development Consortium as part of their system-wide resource assertion. The independent community that predates the Consortium's arrival did not file claims on this body because they had no interest in it. The Consortium did, and the claim is now filed. The pattern mirrors what happened on the primary world.

planets.name: TH-C
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant
planets.demographics: Mixed, Consortium and independent operators in dispute
planets.economy: Fuel extraction, contested between Consortium and independent operators
planets.access_note: Both parties claim the platform. The current situation is an uneasy shared use that both sides describe as temporary.
hazards: Jurisdiction dispute, security personnel from both sides present
Gas giant operations
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Thars system, home to a fuel extraction platform that the original independent community built and that the Development Consortium has asserted a claim over as part of their system-wide resource operations. Both sides are currently using it simultaneously under an arrangement that neither is satisfied with. The platform's future is part of the larger dispute about who Thars belongs to.

systems.name: Pholla System
systems.desc: Pholla is the most remote catalogued system in the Solar Expanse, the edge of what has been mapped and documented. Beyond Pholla, the deep expanse continues, but the systems out there have no names yet and the routes to them are not in standard navigation databases. Pholla is where the known ends.

planets.name: Pholla
planets.atm_note: Thin but breathable, high altitude environments require supplemental oxygen
planets.demographics: A specific kind of person comes to Pholla and stays, frontier hardened, self-sufficient, deliberately far from others
planets.economy: Frontier survival services, deep exploration support, what comes back from beyond
planets.access: Open, no one comes here accidentally
planets.access_note: No controls, no one passes through Pholla unless they mean to.
hazards: Extreme distance from all support
Cold environment year-round
The deep expanse beyond, what is out there is not in the navigation charts

notable_locations.name: The Last Station
notable_locations.desc: Pholla's only significant structure, a community facility that functions as bar, resupply point, information exchange, and memorial wall for expeditions that went beyond and didn't come back. The memorial wall is substantial.

hooks: Objects of unclear provenance brought back from beyond Pholla are a periodic feature of the Last Station's informal economy, items that arrived with someone who went further than the charts extend and returned without explaining where they went. The objects are generally sold rather than studied, and the buyers are rarely academics. The proprietor of the Last Station is believed to have declined to purchase several that they could not identify and did not want to own.

Deep expanse expedition leaders who have made the trip beyond Pholla previously are a small and identifiable group in the frontier community, and their subsequent departure on further expeditions is tracked informally by the community in the way that all significant departures from this outpost are tracked, with attention and without questions, because the culture of the place holds that asking where someone went last time is an imposition they are not obliged to answer.
planets.desc: Pholla is the last full stop before the sentence ends. The community here is small, self-selected, and shaped by the knowledge that they are at the edge of what anyone knows. People come here for specific reasons, to launch deep expeditions, to be as far from the rest of the galaxy as possible while still having breathable air, or because they were heading deeper and ran out of capacity to go further. The deep expanse beyond is real, large, and almost entirely uncharted. What is out there is not known.

systems.name: Grulania System
systems.proximity: Extreme north, the furthest known system in the Solar Expanse, well beyond Pholla. No human settlement confirmed. Entirely outside the range of any organised resupply or rescue capability. Nearest catalogued system is Pholla, itself an extreme frontier outpost.
systems.desc: Grulania is a system designation derived from long-range survey data, a handful of readings that confirmed a stellar body and at least one orbiting mass of sufficient size to register on instruments at the distances involved. Whether the system is habitable, inhabited, or relevant to human interests in any way has not been determined by direct observation. No expedition has returned from an attempt to reach it. Three expeditions are confirmed to have departed toward Grulania's coordinates over the past century. None returned. Their fate is unknown.

planets.name: Grulania (Survey Designation)
planets.atm_note: Long-range spectroscopic data suggests atmospheric composition unlike any world in the known catalogue, the readings have been challenged on instrument error grounds, but three independent surveys produced similar results
planets.population: No evidence of humanoid habitation, spectroscopic data contains anomalies that do not correspond to known natural processes and have not been attributed to instrument error
planets.access_note: No known safe route. The three expedition attempts that headed for Grulania's coordinates did not return. Whether the obstacle is navigational, environmental, or something else is not known.
hazards: Unknown, three expeditions failed without returning data on what they encountered
Extreme distance from any support or rescue capability, a ship in distress here is a ship lost
Deep Solar Expanse navigation in this region relies on charts derived from long-range survey, not direct observation
The spectroscopic anomalies, if genuine, suggest conditions unlike anything in the accessible catalogue

notable_locations.name: Survey Reference Point (Grulania)
notable_locations.desc: The navigational coordinates derived from long-range survey, the only reliable data that exists. The system's actual nature is unknown. What the spectroscopic anomalies indicate has never been verified at close range. The coordinates are filed with the Alliance Survey Office with a Do Not Approach designation that carries no legal force this far out.

hooks: Among the frontier community, accounts of navigators who claim to have reached Grulania's coordinates and returned are treated with the specific scepticism reserved for claims that are simultaneously impossible and unverifiable. The accounts that persist are those whose claimants show physical evidence of extreme transit stress, demonstrate knowledge of conditions that predates the claim, and consistently refuse to discuss what they found, a combination that the frontier community considers more credible than any amount of testimony.

The spectroscopic anomaly data from Grulania has been re-analysed by multiple independent groups using successively more capable equipment across successive decades, and the consistent finding is that the readings are genuine instrument outputs rather than error, genuine outputs that nonetheless cannot be explained by any natural phenomenon that the current scientific framework would predict at those coordinates. The accumulation of confirmations without explanation is itself the most significant scientific fact about Grulania currently available.

Deep frontier expeditions to Grulania's coordinates are funded through structures that obscure the funding source, a pattern consistent across the three known attempts and the persistent rumours of planned fourth and fifth attempts. Who considers Grulania worth funding an expedition toward, and why, is not publicly known. The exceptional terms offered to crew are consistently noted by people who were approached and declined.
planets.desc: Grulania exists at the edge of what any instrument can reliably read at distance, which is the only way it has been observed. Three expeditions went toward it. None came back. The spectroscopic data is anomalous in ways that scientists have not agreed on an interpretation for. It could be instrument artefact. It could be a world with atmospheric and surface chemistry unlike anything in the catalogue. It could be something else entirely. The only way to know requires going there, and the record on going there is not encouraging.

planets.name: Grulania Survey Companion (Unverified)
planets.type: Unknown Body, Long-Range Survey Data Only
planets.atm_note: Possible secondary body detected in the same long-range survey data as the primary body, confidence in this detection is rated very low by the survey teams that produced the data
planets.access_note: Same access situation as the primary body, three expeditions departed toward Grulania, none returned.
hazards: Same as primary, unknown and unsurvived
planets.desc: A possible secondary body detected in the same long-range survey passes that identified Grulania. The detection confidence is low and the data has been challenged on instrument error grounds. Whether this represents a second body in the system, a moon of the primary, or an artefact of the same instrument anomalies that characterise the Grulania readings is not established. It appears in the survey catalogue as an unverified notation.

systems.name: Basagoth Station
systems.desc: Basagoth is not a system, it is a space station that has been in pirate hands for so long that its origins as something else have been completely buried. It sits at the border between Alliance Space and the Gravemist Nebula, a position that makes it the only practical staging point for anyone entering the nebula. The pirates who hold it have built an economy around being the last stop before the impossible navigation begins.

planets.name: Basagoth Station
planets.atm_note: Maintained, life support is the one thing the pirates maintain meticulously because the alternative is dying
planets.grav_note: Artificial gravity throughout, some sections have maintenance issues
planets.population: ~15,000, pirates, support staff, temporary visitors, people waiting
planets.demographics: Mixed, anyone who needs to go into or come out of the Gravemist passes through here
planets.government: Pirate Council (rule by intimidation and mutual interest)
planets.tech_level: Mixed (whatever was on the station plus what has been brought in over the decades)
planets.economy: Navigation information (expensive), fuel (more expensive), nebula guide services (extremely expensive), seized goods trade
planets.access_note: Anyone can dock at Basagoth. Everything costs money. Violence is controlled because it is bad for business but the definition of "controlled" is loose.
hazards: Everything is for sale here including information about you
Pirate operations use Basagoth as a base, ships entering or leaving are assessed as potential targets
Navigation into the nebula from here requires guide services, without them, probability of return is low
The station's structural integrity in older sections is not certified by anyone

notable_locations.name: The Guide's Hall
notable_locations.desc: Where Basagoth's navigation guides operate, the only people who can reliably plot courses through the Gravemist. The Guild (such as it is) controls access to this knowledge jealously. No guide speaks for another, and none of them explain how they know what they know.

notable_locations.name: The Waiting Room
notable_locations.desc: The common area where everyone heading into or out of the nebula ends up waiting at some point. The information density in this room at any given time is extraordinary. So is the number of listening devices.

hooks: The Basagoth guides' pricing structure for deep nebula transits is understood in the broader community to include non-credit payment demands, specific services, information, or access that the guide considers more valuable than the credit equivalent. The pattern of what guides ask for non-monetarily has been tracked informally by traders who use the station and is considered informative about what the guides need that money cannot buy in the Gravemist.

Ships that enter the Gravemist with full crews and return with partial crews, or return with a single surviving member, are documented in Basagoth Station records going back to the station's earliest period in pirate hands. The survivors consistently share one characteristic: they do not explain what happened to the rest of the crew, and the medical examinations that follow show no physical reason why they could not speak. The Basagoth Council's standard response to these situations is not in any written record.
planets.desc: Basagoth is the door to the impossible. The Gravemist Nebula is nearly unnavigable, the few known paths are guarded knowledge belonging to the guides who work out of this station. Without them, entering the nebula is almost certainly fatal. The pirates who hold Basagoth understand their position perfectly and price their services accordingly. For players, Basagoth is a place where everything costs more than it should and the people you need to hire have their own agendas.

planets.name: Basagoth Anchor Rock
planets.atm_note: Airless, the station orbits this body
planets.economy: Station material extraction, mining for station consumables
planets.access_note: Pirate territory. The Council extracts material from this body for station operations.
hazards: Pirate territory, approach requires station clearance
Airless
planets.desc: The rocky body that Basagoth Station orbits, unnamed except as the "Anchor Rock" by station residents. The pirates have been extracting water ice and basic minerals from its surface for the station's life support since before anyone currently on the council can remember. The rock has no strategic value and no other use; its value is entirely as the thing that the station is tied to.

systems.name: Illora System
systems.desc: Illora is one of only two systems officially catalogued inside the Gravemist Nebula. Getting there requires a guide from Basagoth and a route that even most guides do not know. What is there is a community that came in through the nebula decades ago and never left, either by choice or because leaving became complicated.

planets.name: Illora
planets.atm_note: Standard breathable, the nebula's interference with stellar radiation produces unusual lighting but no atmospheric effect
planets.demographics: Mixed, the original community was diverse and has maintained that diversity in isolation
planets.government: Community Council (long-established, well-functioning given the circumstances)
planets.economy: Agricultural (internal), limited technology maintenance, guide services for the outward path
planets.access_note: No route to Illora that does not pass through Basagoth and require guide knowledge. The Illoran community maintains their own path knowledge and will not share it.
hazards: Nebula isolation, supply difficulty, technology degradation over time
Navigation back out requires either Basagoth guides or Illoran path knowledge
The nebula itself creates sensor and navigation anomalies throughout the system
The community has been isolated long enough to develop its own social dynamics that outsiders find difficult to read quickly

notable_locations.name: The Arrival Settlement
notable_locations.desc: The original settlement point, named for the moment the community arrived. Still the administrative and cultural centre of Illoran society. The records of the original journey in are kept here.

notable_locations.name: The Signal Array
notable_locations.desc: The communication system the Illorans use to maintain the path connection with Basagoth. Maintained carefully. The only reliable contact with the outside galaxy.

hooks: The Illoran community's relationship with Basagoth is one of mutual dependency without trust, the Illorans need Basagoth for the communication link to the outside galaxy, and Basagoth needs the Illorans' path knowledge for the deeper nebula routes that the guides do not independently know. The community manages its requests to the outside world with awareness that anything passing through Basagoth is known to Basagoth, and structures its communications accordingly.

The Arrival Settlement records that document the original journey into the Gravemist are maintained carefully by the community but are not shared with outside researchers, a consistent policy that the community describes as cultural but that scholars who have studied the fragments of the records that have emerged through indirect routes describe as consistent with a community that knows why it came here and does not want that reason known outside.
planets.desc: Illora exists in the nebula's quiet. The community here has been cut off from the main galaxy for longer than most of its current residents have been alive, and has made something functional from that separation. It is not paradise, resupply is difficult, technology degrades without replacement parts, and the social pressures of a closed community are real. It is, however, a community: people who have built their lives in an extraordinary context and are reasonably good at it by now.

planets.name: Illora Inner Rocky Body
planets.atm_note: Airless, the nebula's electromagnetic interference produces unusual optical effects when observing this body from the surface of Illora
planets.economy: Limited mineral extraction for community use
planets.access_note: Illoran Community maintains informal use rights. No external access controls, no external visitors reach this system anyway.
hazards: Nebula navigation to reach the system
Airless
planets.desc: The inner rocky body of the Illora system, mined by the Illoran community on an as-needed basis for materials the primary world cannot provide. The nebula's electromagnetic interference creates unusual visual effects when this body is observed from Illora's surface, the community describes it as one of the stranger and more beautiful features of living in the Gravemist.

planets.name: Illora Outer Gas Body
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant, but nebula particulates in the upper atmosphere create visible colour banding different from what gas giants display in open space
planets.economy: None, the community has discussed fuel extraction but lacks the equipment
planets.access_note: No restrictions.
hazards: Nebula navigation
Gas giant approach
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Illora system, visually distinctive due to the Gravemist Nebula's particulate content mixing with its upper atmosphere. The Illoran community uses it as a navigation reference and has periodically discussed fuel extraction operations to reduce dependence on fuel transported through Basagoth, a dependence they consider a vulnerability. The equipment required has been on the community's wishlist for years.

systems.name: Bother System
systems.desc: Bother is the second and deeper of the officially catalogued Gravemist Nebula systems, a designation based on two independent verified survey entries that reached it, made records, and returned. The most recent entry was forty years ago. Current conditions are entirely unknown. Whether the system is inhabited, what it contains, and whether it is navigable from Illora or only from the outer path, are all open questions.

planets.name: Bother (Unverified)
planets.atm_note: Last survey 40 years ago, atmospheric data from that survey suggests breathable conditions but the data quality was rated as low-confidence
planets.population: Unknown, original surveys found no evidence of habitation; current status unknown
planets.access_note: No known current navigable route. The guides at Basagoth who claim knowledge of the path to Bother are a minority and disagree about the route.
hazards: No current intelligence, unknown hazards
Navigation to Bother from any approach is not verified for safety
The nebula in the region of Bother is classified as "Dense Interference", even with guide knowledge, instrument reliability is severely degraded
Forty years of whatever has been happening without observation

notable_locations.name: Survey Point (Historical)
notable_locations.desc: The location where both historical surveys established contact and made their records. Whether anything is there now is unknown. The forty-year-old coordinates are the only reference point.

hooks: Among the Basagoth guides, claims of recent visits to Bother are treated with the same scepticism given to all claims about the deep nebula, but the subset of guides who make the claim without seeking commercial advantage from it, and who subsequently change their behaviour in ways consistent with having been somewhere genuinely unusual, are considered credible by those who know the guide community well. The specific nature of what disturbs guides who claim recent Bother visits has never been publicly stated by any of them.

The older of the two historical surveys of Bother contained a section in its original filed report that was redacted before the report entered any accessible record, a section that the expedition log refers to as "evidence of prior presence" without elaboration. The full original data from both surveys has never been released by the organisations that commissioned them. The redaction is the most significant public fact about what those surveys found.
planets.desc: Bother is catalogued and effectively unknown. Two ships went there across forty years, both returned, neither stayed long enough to produce comprehensive data. What is in the system, whether natural, inhabited, or something else, has not been established. The name is apocryphal: supposedly from the first survey crew's logged reaction when they got back to Basagoth. The cataloguing is technically complete. The understanding of what was catalogued is not.

planets.name: Bother Survey Body (Unverified)
planets.atm_note: One of the two historical surveys noted a possible secondary body in the system, the data quality was rated low-confidence and has not been confirmed
planets.access_note: As with the primary body, navigation to Bother from any approach is not verified for safety.
hazards: Same as primary body, unknown and uncharacterised
Dense nebula interference in this region is extreme
planets.desc: A possible secondary body noted in passing in one of the two historical survey entries for the Bother system. The notation is a data point, not a confirmation, the survey crew noted an instrument reading consistent with a secondary mass and did not have time to characterise it before departing. Whether it is a planet, an asteroid, or an instrument artefact has not been established.

systems.name: Phoxitis System
systems.desc: Phoxitis was identified by an Alliance survey mission as one of the more accessible systems inside the Erbrother Nebula, a smaller, more navigable nebula than the Gravemist but still challenging to transit without proper equipment. The system's unusual stellar characteristics have made it a subject of ongoing scientific interest.

planets.name: Phoxitis
planets.atm_note: Breathable but with elevated particulate content from nebula interaction, extended outdoor exposure requires filtration
planets.demographics: Almost entirely Science Authority personnel and contracted researchers
planets.access_note: Science Authority mission area. Academic credentials or Authority sponsorship required. Not commercially accessible.
hazards: Nebula navigation, access and egress require proper equipment and charted routes
Science Authority security enforces mission exclusivity
The nebula creates sensor interference affecting communication and navigation throughout
Unusual stellar radiation profile, some crew members on extended stays have reported health effects under investigation

notable_locations.name: Survey Base Phoxitis
notable_locations.desc: The Alliance Science Authority's installation, a well-equipped but temporary facility intended for extended research missions. The quality of the sensor equipment here is exceptionally high, directed at the nebula's properties and the system's stellar characteristics.

hooks: Internal dissent within Alliance Science Authority missions is suppressed through a consistent personnel management process, researchers who file formal disagreements with published conclusions are transferred to postings that remove them from the subject matter and from contact with other researchers who might amplify their concerns. The pattern is well-documented by science policy researchers who track Authority personnel movements. The content of suppressed dissents is, by definition, not accessible through any public record.

The Peavis community's passive observation of the Phoxitis survey base has produced a body of documented emission readings that the community shares among themselves and does not report to the Authority, readings that experienced members of the community describe as inconsistent with the instrumentation profile of a standard research installation. Whether this represents equipment used for purposes not included in the mission's published scope or an interaction between the equipment and the nebula environment has not been established from outside.
planets.desc: Phoxitis is a working science mission in an unusual location. The Erbrother Nebula is not the Gravemist, it is challenging to navigate but not effectively impossible, and the system's accessibility has made it a legitimate research destination. Whether the published research from this mission accurately represents what has been found is a question some people inside the Science Authority have started asking.

planets.name: PHX-B
planets.atm_note: Airless, nebula particulates create a faint glow around the body visible from the survey base
planets.population: Uninhabited, sensor array positioned on surface
planets.access_note: Science Authority territory, sensor array on surface monitors nebula properties from this vantage.
hazards: Science Authority restricted zone
Airless
Nebula electromagnetic interference
planets.desc: The inner rocky body of the Phoxitis system, used by the Alliance Science Authority as a sensor array placement site. The surface position provides a clean line of sight for certain nebula measurements that the survey base cannot achieve from orbit. The array is automated and checked during regular surface visits from the survey base.

planets.name: PHX-C
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant, nebula particulates give the upper atmosphere an unusual visual haze
planets.access_note: No formal restrictions, the Science Authority monitors it as part of the system survey.
hazards: Nebula electromagnetic interference affects navigation instruments
Gas giant approach
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Phoxitis system. The Science Authority has included it in their monitoring scope because the nebula interaction with gas giant atmospheric dynamics produces data relevant to understanding the Erbrother Nebula's properties. The survey base has conducted several dedicated observation runs on this body. The published data is a subset of what has been collected.

systems.name: Peavis System
systems.desc: Peavis is the second known system inside the Erbrother Nebula and the one that has developed without institutional presence. Where Phoxitis has the Science Authority, Peavis has whoever found it useful, independent operators who valued the nebula's natural navigation deterrent as a form of privacy protection. It has become a small but established independent community.

planets.name: Peavis
planets.atm_note: Standard breathable, the nebula filtering of stellar radiation produces a distinctive sky colouration but no atmospheric chemistry effect
planets.demographics: Mixed, people who came here for the privacy it offers
planets.economy: Small-scale agriculture, technical services, privacy-valued activities, observation of Phoxitis mission
planets.access_note: The nebula navigation is the access control, getting here without the right equipment and charts is difficult. Once here, the community is open.
hazards: Nebula navigation for entry and egress
Isolation, the community is self-sufficient but limits apply
The residents who chose Peavis for privacy reasons may react badly to parties perceived as representing institutional interests

notable_locations.name: The Settlement
notable_locations.desc: The primary community on Peavis, built informally over time by people who came here in small groups and stayed. Functional, somewhat improvised in its infrastructure, and with the social texture of a community that has been through things together.

notable_locations.name: The Observation Point
notable_locations.desc: The community maintains a passive observation array directed at the Phoxitis system, they watch the Science Authority mission with the interest of neighbours who have strong feelings about institutional proximity.

hooks: The Peavis community's concern about Alliance Science Authority expansion is based on a pattern they have observed in other independent communities adjacent to Authority research interests, a consistent progression from observation to formal inquiry to proposed presence to established presence that the communities involved rarely successfully interrupt. Peavis residents who have researched the pattern consider resistance most effective in the earliest stages, which is why the community tracks Authority communications carefully and responds to perceived approach signals before they become formal proposals.

Peavis's policy toward inquiries about its residents is the community's most consistent and non-negotiable characteristic, no information is shared with any external party about any person present on the planet, regardless of who asks or what justification is offered. This policy is the reason the community has the residents it does, and is maintained with the understanding that any exception would undermine the reason people come here.
planets.desc: Peavis is a community of people who came to the Erbrother Nebula because they wanted the world to have some difficulty finding them. The nebula navigation is not completely deterrent but it is deterrent enough to make it selective. The Science Authority's presence in Phoxitis is a source of sustained unease, not because the Authority has done anything to Peavis, but because the residents understand that institutional presence tends to expand and that their privacy has a specific value they would prefer to maintain.

planets.name: Peavis Inner Body
planets.atm_note: Thin nitrogen atmosphere, unbreathable but the nebula creates a distinctive visual diffusion around this body when observed from the surface of Peavis
planets.access_note: Community nominal claim. No restrictions, no outsiders reach this system without navigating the nebula first.
hazards: Thin unbreathable atmosphere
Nebula electromagnetic interference
planets.desc: The inner rocky body of the Peavis system, claimed nominally by the Community Council to prevent the Science Authority from positioning monitoring equipment on it without consultation. The community has not formally objected to the Authority's presence in Phoxitis, but they have taken precautionary steps. This body is one of them.

planets.name: Peavis Outer Gas Body
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant, nebula interaction produces observable atmospheric colouring
planets.economy: None, community has discussed fuel extraction as an independence measure
planets.access_note: No restrictions.
hazards: Gas giant approach
Nebula electromagnetic interference
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Peavis system. The community's Observation Point, directed at the Phoxitis Science Authority base, has also collected data on this body as a secondary function of the array. The nebula-modified gas giant dynamics are considered by the community as one of the more interesting features of their location. They share this data with each other and do not report it to the Authority.

systems.name: Asteroid Eater
systems.desc: The Asteroid Eater is the large black hole at the centre of Dark Space, named by the first navigators who plotted its position after observing it consume a dense asteroid field in its accretion disc. It sits at the gravitational heart of the region, and its influence shapes the orbital mechanics of everything in Dark Space. Navigation around it is essential knowledge for anyone operating in the region.

planets.name: Asteroid Eater Exclusion Zone
planets.atm_note: Hard void, extreme radiation throughout exclusion zone
planets.grav_note: Tidal forces detectable at extraordinary range, the largest known black hole in accessible galactic space
planets.population: Uninhabited, no stable structure possible within exclusion zone
planets.access_note: No approach designation, Alliance and independent navigators maintain wide exclusion by convention. The event horizon is visible from several Dark Space systems on clear instrument readings.
hazards: Extreme tidal forces, larger and more powerful than B.I.G. or Garson
Accretion disc activity, the active consumption of material creates unpredictable energy events
Gravitational influence measurable throughout Dark Space, all orbital calculations in the region account for it
Electromagnetic interference from accretion disc activity affects communications at significant range

notable_locations.name: The Feeding Zone
notable_locations.desc: The accretion disc of the Asteroid Eater, the active consumption zone from which the black hole takes its name. Material entering this zone is consumed within hours. The spectacle of the consumption is visible from multiple Dark Space systems and is one of the few things about Dark Space that tourists have been known to travel to see.

hooks: Navigation crews transiting past the Asteroid Eater's exclusion zone have filed reports across several decades of objects entering the accretion disc whose trajectory profiles are inconsistent with natural orbital delivery, entry angles and approach vectors that would require active positioning rather than passive infall. The reports have been acknowledged by the navigational authority and have not been included in any updated model of the black hole's consumption patterns.

The navigation anomaly at the Asteroid Eater's exclusion zone outer boundary has been reported by enough independent navigators across enough years that it appears in informal navigation advisories circulated among Dark Space pilots, not in the official charts, which have not been updated to reflect it, but in the captain-to-captain knowledge base that experienced Dark Space operators maintain in parallel to official documentation.
planets.desc: The Asteroid Eater is Dark Space's defining feature, the gravitational anchor of the entire region and a constant presence in every navigation calculation made here. Its name came from the observation that prompted its cataloguing: a ship that transited the region noticed an asteroid field entering the accretion disc and timed the consumption. The name stuck. The phenomenon has not stopped. It is the largest known black hole in accessible galactic space and the reason Dark Space's orbital mechanics are as complex as they are.

planets.name: Asteroid Eater Debris Field
planets.atm_note: Void, extreme radiation throughout
planets.grav_note: Tidal forces from the black hole create irregular gravitational conditions throughout the debris field
planets.access_note: Within the navigation exclusion zone. Material in this field is being consumed by the accretion disc on a geological timescale.
hazards: Tidal disruption forces
Extreme radiation from accretion disc
Gravitational anomalies throughout field
Any ship entering risks trajectory alteration toward the exclusion zone
planets.desc: The diffuse debris field surrounding the Asteroid Eater, the material that will eventually be consumed by the accretion disc. The field is the remnant of asteroid populations disrupted by the black hole's gravity over billions of years. Navigation reports citing unusual approach vectors for material entering the accretion disc have flagged sections of this field as a potential source of anomalous activity.

systems.name: New Oshana System
systems.desc: New Oshana was founded by colonists who believed the frontier would offer freedom that the Alliance could not provide. They were correct about the Alliance not being present. The freedom they found included freedom from infrastructure, emergency response, and legal protection. The colony has survived through a combination of determination and necessity that has produced a community unlike anything in organised space.

planets.name: New Oshana
planets.atm_note: Breathable, thin at altitude
planets.demographics: Mixed, original diverse colonial population and descendants
planets.government: Settler Council (direct democracy with significant community cultural enforcement)
planets.economy: Agriculture, small-scale mining, frontier services, trade with passing vessels
planets.access_note: Open entry, the community is cautious about outsiders based on hard historical experience but maintains trade relationships.
hazards: Dark Space proximity, the Black Angel's influence via the Nerulian Emperor's control extends to attitude about independent systems nearby
Periodic raiding from Dark Space frontier pirates
Resource limitations, the colony has never had enough of everything
Distance from any organised support

notable_locations.name: Founder's Settlement
notable_locations.desc: The original landing site of the colonial mission, maintained as a historical marker and administrative centre. The records here document two generations of survival that most academics consider extraordinary given the circumstances.

hooks: The Nerulian Emperor's historical territory claims in Dark Space, issued as declarations rather than military actions, are understood by Dark Space political analysts to be a consistent pressure technique that rarely precedes immediate action and almost always precedes eventual action. New Oshana's Settler Council has studied the historical record of previous declarations and the timelines between declaration and consequence. The study has not produced reassurance.

Intelligence collection operations in independent Dark Space colonies are sufficiently common that experienced community members in systems like New Oshana have developed the ability to identify them, visitors whose questions are too specific, whose interest is too broad, and whose stated commercial purpose cannot be verified. The communities share information about identified operations among themselves through networks that operate entirely outside any formal channel.
planets.desc: New Oshana is a colony that survived when it shouldn't have. The original colonists arrived under-supplied and over-optimistic. What they built over two generations is functional, self-sufficient at a basic level, and deeply aware of the fact that nobody is coming to help them. The community has a toughness that comes from that awareness, not aggressive, but entirely without illusions about what the galaxy provides.

planets.name: Oshana Prospect
planets.atm_note: Thin nitrogen-CO2 atmosphere, unbreathable without equipment
planets.economy: Small-scale mineral extraction, supplies the colony with materials unavailable on the primary world
planets.access_note: Settler Council territory. No external restrictions, Dark Space isolation is its own deterrent.
hazards: Thin atmosphere, equipment required
Dark Space frontier conditions
No rescue capability
planets.desc: The second rocky body of the New Oshana system, mined by the colonial community for materials not available on the primary world. The operation is small and run on a rotating basis, when the colony needs specific materials, a crew goes out. The practice has been established since the colony's early years when the colonists discovered the primary world lacked specific mineral types they needed.

planets.name: Oshana Deep Gas Body
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant
planets.economy: Fuel extraction, essential for colony's ship operations
planets.access_note: Colony fuel operations. Passing ships have been allowed to purchase fuel in exchange for goods or information.
hazards: Minimal platform infrastructure, improvised and maintained by the colonists
Gas giant operations
Dark Space frontier conditions
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the New Oshana system, where the colony maintains a minimal fuel extraction operation. The platform was built by the colonists themselves from salvaged equipment over several years, necessity being the driver rather than available resources. It functions because it has to. Passing ships have occasionally been allowed to purchase fuel, which is one of the colony's few external economic connections.

systems.name: Manola System
systems.desc: Manola is one of the Dark Space systems settled by Nerulian survivors after the Kraven invasion, far enough from the Kraven border to be considered relatively safe, close enough to San Tien's cultural orbit to maintain Nerulian identity. It is a quieter system than San Tien, with a smaller population and a stronger desire to simply be left alone to rebuild.

planets.name: Manola
planets.atm_note: Standard breathable
planets.economy: Agriculture, manufacturing, Nerulian technology maintenance, limited external trade
planets.access_note: Visitors accepted but monitored carefully. Nerulian cultural norms apply, ignorance of them is not an excuse.
hazards: Cultural sensitivity, Nerulian survivor communities have reasons for their wariness
Dark Space proximity, general frontier risks apply
Nerulian technology is old and different in ways that create unexpected interaction with modern systems

notable_locations.name: The Rebuild Quarter
notable_locations.desc: The section of Manola's primary settlement dedicated to cultural reconstruction, art, language preservation, craft traditions that were nearly lost in the invasion. The people working here are doing something that they consider important enough to have dedicated their lives to it.

hooks: Messages received by Nerulian diaspora communities on old encrypted communication protocols whose source cannot be attributed to any known San Tien or diaspora transmitter are documented in the private records of several communities including Manola, messages that the communities have not reported to the Alliance and have not responded to, because the first question the Council faces in each case is the same one it cannot answer: whether the message is genuine, a test, or a trap.
planets.desc: Manola exists in the quiet space between survival and rebuilding. The Nerulian community here is past the immediate crisis of the diaspora and working on the longer project of being a culture rather than just survivors. It is slow work, valued work, and work that outside interference tends to complicate. Players who come here with urgency will find that Manola moves at its own pace and for its own reasons.

planets.name: Manola-Oseth
planets.atm_note: Airless
planets.economy: Limited mineral extraction for community use
planets.access_note: Nerulian Council claim. Visitors acknowledged, Nerulian cultural protocols apply even here.
hazards: Airless
Dark Space frontier conditions
planets.desc: The inner rocky body of the Manola system, named Manola-Oseth in the Nerulian tradition, "Oseth" meaning secondary or companion in old Nerulian. The community mines it occasionally for materials. The act of naming it in the Nerulian tradition rather than a survey catalogue number is deliberate: the community names the things around it because naming is part of what it means to be here as Nerulians rather than refugees.

planets.name: Manola-Keth
planets.atm_note: Standard gas giant
planets.access_note: Council fuel operations. Open to respectful visitors.
hazards: Gas giant operations
Dark Space conditions
planets.desc: The outer gas giant of the Manola system, named Manola-Keth in the Nerulian tradition. The community maintains a fuel extraction platform here as part of their self-sufficiency programme. The platform crew observe Nerulian working traditions, there are certain days when the platform is shut down entirely for community observances. The practice is maintained even when it is operationally inconvenient, because the point of the observances is precisely that they are not subordinated to convenience.

systems.name: Cish System
systems.desc: Cish sits at a strategic junction in Dark Space navigation, the system's position makes it relevant to anyone trying to move through the region efficiently. This has made it a target for every faction with an interest in controlling Dark Space movement. The resulting conflict has been ongoing for years with no clear resolution.

planets.name: Cish
planets.atm_note: Breathable, combat operations have created localised atmospheric contamination in contested zones
planets.demographics: Mixed, original civilian population caught between competing military presences
planets.government: Contested, different factions claim authority over different zones
planets.economy: Strategic goods movement, military logistics, what civilian commerce survives between the fronts
planets.access_note: No safe entry without faction identification. Unidentified vessels from any approach vector are treated as hostile by at least one party.
hazards: Active multi-faction conflict throughout
Civilian population caught between competing forces, collateral damage is ongoing
No consistent rule of law, depends entirely on which faction controls a given area
Strategic value means this conflict has outside interest funding both sides

notable_locations.name: The Junction Point
notable_locations.desc: The navigational feature that makes Cish strategically valuable, a transit corridor used by Dark Space traffic. Currently effectively closed due to the conflict. Whoever controls the Junction Point controls the most important navigational feature in this part of Dark Space.

hooks: Transit through the Cish Junction Point is known among Dark Space operators to be negotiable, the faction controlling it at any given time is willing to grant passage in exchange for services that vary with the operational situation. The services requested tend to be things that the controlling faction cannot conduct itself without worsening its political situation, which is why outside parties with no affiliation to any Cish faction are specifically sought for these arrangements.

The civilian population of Cish has developed extensive expertise in moving through active multi-front conflicts, knowledge accumulated over years of living between fronts that has become one of the system's most significant informal exports. Communities in adjacent systems have hired Cish civilians as guides for difficult transit operations, and the knowledge is considered more reliable than any intelligence briefing by operators who have used both.
planets.desc: Cish is what happens when a geographic feature is worth more than the cost of conflict. The Junction Point's navigational value has sustained a multi-faction war for years because no party is willing to let another control it and none is capable of holding it decisively. The civilian population continues to live in the gaps between fronts. Dark Space players will find Cish a place where everything is negotiable and nothing is safe.

systems.name: Haran System
systems.desc: Haran was a corporate extraction operation that was abandoned when the economics deteriorated and the Dark Space security situation became too costly to maintain. The corporate withdrawal was rapid and incomplete, infrastructure was left in place, some equipment is still running, and the small resident workforce that was not evacuated in time has been managing on its own for years.

planets.name: Haran
planets.atm_note: Standard breathable, maintained without corporate oversight by remaining population
planets.population: ~8,000, people who didn't make it out
planets.demographics: Mixed, the accident of who was in the evacuation zone and who wasn't
planets.economy: Subsistence, maintaining what the corporation left running, limited salvage for trade
planets.access_note: Open, the survivor community welcomes contact from outside. They need resupply and have things to trade.
hazards: Corporate infrastructure not maintained to specification, failure risk is ongoing and unpredictable
Dark Space frontier risks apply fully, no corporate security presence
Resource depletion, the survivors have been living on finite supplies for years
Corporate legal status uncertain, who owns what is still technically contested

notable_locations.name: The Left-Behind Quarter
notable_locations.desc: Where the survivors have made their community, in the housing and facilities the corporation built for workers, maintained by the workers after the corporation left. The ingenuity of the maintenance is remarkable and occasionally alarming.

hooks: The legal status of Haran's infrastructure, corporate assets formally owned by a company whose withdrawal was incomplete and whose successor liability is contested across three jurisdictions, is a situation that corporate legal departments have been monitoring without resolving since the withdrawal occurred. The survivor community has been living in and maintaining the assets throughout, which has not clarified the ownership question and has produced a community with strong views about the answer.

Autonomous industrial equipment running on Haran without oversight or maintenance to specification has been producing outputs that the survivor community has documented without being able to identify, byproducts of the automated processes that do not match the equipment's intended output profile. The community's assessment of whether these byproducts are valuable or hazardous has changed several times as their understanding of the equipment has improved.
planets.desc: Haran is what the frontier looks like when the corporate model fails completely. The survivors who were left behind did not have a plan for the scenario, they had to make one. Three years in, the plan is working at a basic level. What they need is resupply, outside contact, and either a legal resolution of the ownership question or someone powerful enough to make the corporate claim go away. What they do not need is another party arriving with their own agenda for what Haran's infrastructure should be used for.

systems.name: Cassidir System
systems.classification: Dark Space System, Black Angel Proximity
systems.desc: Cassidir sits in the shadow of the Nerulian Emperor's reach, close enough to the Dark Space region under his influence that the Black Angel's presence is felt here, not directly but as an absence of the opposition that would otherwise organise against him. The systems near Cassidir have learned not to challenge the Emperor's interests. The systems that forgot this lesson are not discussed in polite company.

planets.name: Cassidir
planets.atm_note: Standard breathable, permanently overcast from dust storms
planets.government: Local Council (operating under implicit Imperial permission)
planets.economy: Trade, agriculture in protected lowlands, services for traffic moving through the region
planets.access_note: Nominally open, the implicit requirement is not attracting the Emperor's attention by doing anything he would object to.
hazards: Imperial interest, being noticed by the Nerulian Emperor's intelligence apparatus is dangerous
The Black Angel's influence: anything that challenges Imperial interests in this region tends to encounter problems that are difficult to attribute to any specific cause
Local governance operates under constraints that are not written anywhere but are understood by everyone
Alliance law has limited practical force here, enforcement would require the Alliance to confront Imperial interests, which it has declined to do

notable_locations.name: The Trading Quarter
notable_locations.desc: The economic heart of Cassidir, where goods moving through the Imperial periphery change hands. Some of those goods are things that would not change hands in Alliance Space. Nobody asks.

notable_locations.name: The Quiet District
notable_locations.desc: Where the population that remembers the last time someone in Cassidir challenged Imperial interests lives. The community here is extremely careful about what it says and who it says it to.

hooks: The existence of Alliance intelligence assets operating in Cassidir and similar Imperial periphery systems is an open secret in the intelligence community, both the Alliance and the Nerulian Emperor's apparatus know that the other maintains assets there, and both manage their exposure carefully. The practical consequence is that Imperial periphery systems see consistent intelligence counter-operations from both sides running simultaneously, with the civilian population as the medium through which both sides work.

Merchants who carry goods of interest to the Nerulian Emperor through Cassidir without knowing the significance of what they carry are a well-documented category of intelligence problem, the Emperor's intelligence apparatus is systematic enough to identify objects of interest in transit through its periphery, and patient enough to wait for the right moment rather than acting immediately. The pattern of how this plays out has been observed often enough that experienced traders in the region have developed a form of informal screening for what they accept as cargo.

The Black Angel's operational patterns in Dark Space have been studied continuously by every intelligence service in the galaxy, and the consistent finding is that changes in the pattern are more informative than the pattern itself, anomalies in how the Black Angel operates in a given system correlate with changes in the Emperor's strategic priorities that become visible through other means weeks or months later. Analysts who track both treat the anomalies as leading indicators.
planets.desc: Cassidir exists in the Emperor's penumbra. It is not under direct Imperial control, it has its own government and its own nominal independence. But the Black Angel's presence in the wider region has produced a consistent behavioural pattern in systems like Cassidir: accommodation of Imperial interests, avoidance of anything that might attract Imperial attention, and a collective understanding that certain topics are not discussed. It is a functional system operating under constraints that are never stated and always present.

systems.name: Puthea System
systems.desc: Puthea was documented by the Nuzonia expedition, the only credible account of the deep Dream region. Expedition records describe a system of unusual orbital geometry and multiple habitable bodies in apparent long-term ecological stasis. Whether the stasis is natural or intervention-maintained is one of many questions the expedition's brief visit could not resolve.

planets.name: Puthea Survey Data
planets.atm_note: Expedition records indicate breathable conditions, stasis-maintained ecosystems suggest atmospheric stability
planets.grav_note: Expedition records note consistent below-standard gravity across all surveyed bodies
planets.population: Unknown, expedition found no evidence of current habitation but found evidence of previous habitation
planets.access_note: No reliable route, only the Nuzonia expedition has navigated this region. Expedition charts are incomplete.
hazards: Navigation, the Dream region is not reliably chartable with current technology
Unknown conditions, expedition records are the only data source and were collected under time pressure
The evidence of previous habitation raises unanswered questions about what happened to that population

notable_locations.name: The Still Worlds
notable_locations.desc: What the expedition called the multiple habitable bodies of Puthea, worlds with active ecosystems that appear to have been in the same state for an indeterminate time. Flora, fauna, no apparent succession process. Ecologists who reviewed the expedition data described it as one of the most puzzling natural observations they had encountered.

hooks: The Nuzonia expedition's data on Puthea exists in two distinct bodies, the published summaries, and the complete internal records that have been seen by a small number of researchers under access conditions that precluded taking notes. Researchers who have seen the complete records consistently decline to discuss sections of them that correspond to the expedition's time on the surface of the Still Worlds, which is the section the published summary treats most briefly and least specifically.
planets.desc: Puthea is what the Nuzonia expedition found when it went somewhere no one else had gone. The ecological stasis, if that is what it is, has no known analogue anywhere in catalogued space. The previous habitation evidence has no identified population. The expedition was there for days. What they did not understand could fill a library, and might be worth filling one about.

systems.name: Betravir System
systems.desc: Betravir was the most anomalous system the Nuzonia expedition encountered, a system where physical laws appeared to operate normally on large scales but produced consistent small-scale deviations that the expedition's instruments recorded but could not explain. The expedition spent longer here than planned because the anomalies kept producing new data that the team felt they needed to document.

planets.name: Betravir Survey Data
planets.atm_note: Expedition records indicate breathable atmosphere, particulate effects from anomalous physics produced visible light diffraction
planets.grav_note: Gravitational anomalies at small scale, the expedition described it as "physics thinking about it differently in here"
planets.access_note: Dream region navigation required.
hazards: Physics anomalies, effects on biological systems over extended exposure unknown
Navigation anomalies in the system complicate transit and departure
The specific effect that delayed the expedition suggests the anomalies may interact with decision-making in some way

notable_locations.name: The Anomaly Field
notable_locations.desc: The region of the system where the expedition's instruments produced the most consistent anomalous readings. The team lead's personal log describes three attempts to leave the system, each of which produced a reason to stay and investigate more. Whether that reflects the anomalies' properties or human scientific curiosity is recorded as an open question.

hooks: Academic papers proposing that the Betravir anomalies indicate something artificial rather than natural as their producing cause have been published twice since the expedition returned, and both have been subject to legal challenges from the institution that funded the Nuzonia expedition, challenges whose basis has never been satisfactorily explained on scientific grounds and whose existence has prompted more discussion among physicists than the papers themselves would have generated without the challenge.
planets.desc: Betravir is the part of the Nuzonia expedition that its scientists found hardest to leave and hardest to explain. The anomalies they documented do not fit any current theoretical framework for naturally occurring physics. Whether that means the current frameworks are incomplete or that the anomalies have a non-natural origin is the question that has been generating academic debate ever since the expedition returned.

systems.name: Lumia System
systems.desc: Lumia was where the Nuzonia expedition found the clearest evidence that the Dream region has or had intelligent inhabitants, structures of clearly non-natural origin, distributed across the system in a pattern that suggested intentional placement. The expedition did not encounter anyone. The structures were empty. Whether they are abandoned or simply unoccupied is one of the galaxy's significant open questions.

planets.name: Lumia Survey Data
planets.atm_note: Breathable, the expedition spent surface time here without environmental hazard
planets.population: Unknown, structures found, no current inhabitants encountered
planets.tech_level: Unknown, structures are of unknown technological basis
planets.access_note: Dream region navigation required.
hazards: Unknown purpose of the structures, no assessment of whether they are passive or active
First contact protocols apply if inhabitants are present, mishandling could have consequences
The structures' material properties are unknown, what they are made of was not determined during the brief expedition visit

notable_locations.name: The Formation Array
notable_locations.desc: The largest grouping of structures found by the expedition, fourteen structures arranged in a geometric pattern across a mountain plateau. The expedition photographed them extensively. What they are for is not known. They did not respond to any contact attempt the expedition tried.

hooks: The section of the Nuzonia expedition report covering contact attempts at Lumia is the classified portion, confirmed to exist by expedition personnel who have been asked about it and confirmed to be classified by the funding institution which has never explained why contact attempt documentation requires classification. The scientific community's consensus is that the contact attempts produced results, and that the results were classified because of what they were rather than how they were obtained.

Dream region navigational data from sources other than the Nuzonia expedition has appeared on specialist markets on multiple documented occasions, data that includes detail about Lumia and surrounding systems that could not have been derived from the expedition's published records. The source of this independent data has not been established, and its existence is considered by scholars of the region to be the second most significant fact about the Dream, after the existence of the Lumia structures themselves.
planets.desc: Lumia is the piece of the Nuzonia expedition's findings that has generated the most speculation and the least public information. Structures of non-natural origin, clearly intentionally placed, empty on arrival. The expedition's official position is that the structures are most likely ancient and their builders long gone. The classified sections of the expedition report, whose existence has been confirmed but whose contents remain restricted, are widely believed to tell a different story.

systems.name: Nypsos F47 System
systems.desc: Nypsos F47 is positioned at the edge of the Dream region closest to Dark Space, a location that places it in the overlap between two poorly understood regions of space. The designation reflects its survey status: F for frontier, 47 for position in the grid of the survey that briefly catalogued this sector. Almost nothing is known about it.

planets.name: Nypsos F47
planets.atm_note: No survey data
planets.access_note: No known route, the border position between Dream region and Dark Space makes approach from either direction difficult.
hazards: Total intelligence blackout, no data
Dark Space proximity brings unknown risks associated with that region
Dream region navigation hazards apply from one direction
Potentially subject to Imperial periphery dynamics from Dark Space side

notable_locations.name: Survey Grid Reference F47
notable_locations.desc: A navigational coordinate in a distant survey grid. That is the entirety of what exists in the official record for Nypsos F47.
