hooks: Crews claiming to have come from the direction of Nypsos F47 have appeared at navigable systems on a handful of documented occasions, crews whose accounts of their origin are inconsistent in ways that experienced frontier operators attribute to either genuine disorientation from a transit that exceeded normal experience or to deliberate vagueness about something they have chosen not to share. The two explanations are not mutually exclusive, and neither produces a satisfying account of how they navigated from there to where they arrived.
planets.desc: Nypsos F47 is close to nothing and not close to anything known to be good. Its position between Dream region uncertainty and Dark Space danger makes it theoretically accessible from both directions and reliably reached from neither. It is the kind of system that appears in navigation databases as a coordinate and a question mark.

systems.name: Zelmolla System
systems.desc: Zelmolla shares Nypsos F47's border position between the Dream region and Dark Space, but has one additional piece of documentation: a brief long-range scan from a Dark Space survey vessel that recorded what appears to be electromagnetic activity inconsistent with a dead system. The scan was not followed up. Whether the activity represents technology, unusual natural phenomena, or something else was not determined.

planets.name: Zelmolla
planets.atm_note: No direct survey data
planets.tech_level: Unknown, electromagnetic pattern suggests possible technological activity
planets.access_note: No established route from either Dream region or Dark Space.
hazards: Unknown, electromagnetic activity of unknown origin
Dark Space proximity with all associated risks
Dream region navigation challenges
If the electromagnetic activity is technological in origin, unknown party of unknown capability and disposition

notable_locations.name: Signal Source (Estimated Position)
notable_locations.desc: The estimated origin point of the electromagnetic activity detected in the Dark Space survey scan. The confidence interval on the position is significant, the survey was at long range.

hooks: The electromagnetic activity from Zelmolla has been detected by multiple independent instruments at different positions over the years, producing triangulation data that places the source consistently at the same coordinates. The signal is periodic rather than continuous, consistent with a transmission schedule rather than continuous operation, and does not match any known beacon or navigation format. Among the small community of researchers who track anomalous signals at the Dark Space / Dream region border, Zelmolla is considered the most significant unresolved active signal in the catalogue.
planets.desc: Zelmolla is the Dream region system with the one additional datum: something appears to be happening there. What that something is, natural, artificial, inhabited, automated, is not known. The one piece of evidence that distinguishes it from Nypsos F47 is either significant or a navigational anomaly. Resolving that question requires going there, which the border position makes difficult and the unknown nature of the signal makes risky. Both of those things also describe it as exactly the kind of place that certain parties find compelling.

systems.name: DR345-0 System
systems.desc: DR345-0 is named with the designation system used for Tronik Network systems, the alphanumeric codes assigned during the post-Tronik War survey that catalogued the systems between Freeland and System 5. The Tronik Network was the site of the war's most intense fighting and these systems bear the evidence of it. DR345-0 is on the Freeland border and has developed the most normal community of any Network system.

planets.name: DR345-0
planets.atm_note: Breathable but with trace contamination from the war period, acceptable and declining year on year
planets.demographics: Mixed, settlement drawn from both Freeland and Alliance populations
planets.economy: Post-war reconstruction, agriculture, frontier trade, historical site management
planets.access_note: Open under nominal Alliance affiliation.
hazards: Unexploded Tronik War ordnance, still being cleared from rural areas
Post-war trauma in the older population has produced cultural patterns that visitors should understand before engaging
Some areas remain physically unsafe from war damage that hasn't been cleared

notable_locations.name: The Clearing Ground
notable_locations.desc: The ongoing ordnance clearance operation, a permanent team working through the rural zones. The war produced an extraordinary volume of unexploded material. The team is professionally matter-of-fact about their work.

notable_locations.name: The War Memorial Network
notable_locations.desc: DR345-0 has more Tronik War memorials per square kilometre than any other system. The community has processed the war through memorial practice rather than forgetting.

hooks: Ordnance clearance teams working DR345-0's rural zones have documented finds that predate the Tronik War by centuries, objects in the soil that were not placed there by any force involved in the war and that do not correspond to any known historical activity in the system before it was settled. The finds are reported to the Community Council and handled through a process that has been established precisely because the finds have occurred before, and whose outcome is not disclosed publicly.
planets.desc: DR345-0 is the Tronik Network system that has made the most progress toward normalcy. The war ended here a long time ago and the community has had generations to build something from the aftermath. The memorials are thick on the ground because the fighting was thick on the ground. But the community is not defined by what happened, it has used what happened to build a culture of remembrance that coexists with active life. It is the best case scenario for a Tronik Network system.

systems.name: L.I.F.T.N System
systems.desc: L.I.F.T.N., the name is an acronym from the industrial consortium that operated the system before the Tronik War, now defunct, is the most industrially developed Tronik Network system. The war damaged the infrastructure but did not destroy it, and successive corporate interests have operated here continuously since, attracted by the existing investment and the system's position as the Network's manufacturing centre.

planets.name: L.I.F.T.N.
planets.atm_note: Heavy industrial atmosphere, visible air quality issues in manufacturing districts, managed in residential zones
planets.climate: Industrial (Temperate base with significant thermal output)
planets.economy: Heavy manufacturing, industrial processing, Tronik Network logistics, component production
planets.access_note: Consortium industrial zone, worker or contractor credentials required.
hazards: Industrial environment, standard hazards at scale
Corporate governance with limited external accountability
War-era infrastructure, some of the original installations are centuries old and the maintenance history is complicated
Labour conditions that are legally acceptable and practically difficult

notable_locations.name: The Original Installation
notable_locations.desc: The pre-Tronik War industrial complex, repaired, expanded, and continuously operated since the war ended. Parts of it date to the industrial consortium that gave the system its name. The engineering here is genuinely impressive in a purely utilitarian way.

hooks: The L.I.F.T.N. Industrial Consortium's acquisition of previously heritage-designated sections of the system is documented in public records, each acquisition legally clean in form and preceded by the revocation of heritage designations at a speed that heritage preservation advocates consider inconsistent with any ordinary administrative process. The pattern has recurred across three separate acquisitions, producing a well-documented sequence that advocates describe as a template and that the Consortium describes as coincidence.
planets.desc: L.I.F.T.N. works in the uncomplicated way that industrial centres work, it produces things, the things are sold, the profit funds continued production. The Tronik War is part of the system's history in the specific sense that the industrial infrastructure survived it and someone kept the furnaces running. The consortium that runs it now is the fourth to hold it. The furnaces are the continuity.

planets.name: L.I.F.T.N. Dyson Construct
planets.atm_note: Structure surrounds the system star. No atmosphere on the construct surface. Interior habitation sections are sealed and pressurised.
planets.grav_note: Artificial gravity systems installed on internal habitation and maintenance sections only. The construct surface itself is microgravity.
planets.demographics: Industrial engineers, maintenance specialists, consortium technical staff
planets.economy: Power generation and energy export. Captures a fraction of stellar output and supplies L.I.F.T.N. Prime entirely, with surplus sold to Tronik Network grids.
planets.access_note: Consortium operational zone. Engineering clearance required for approach. Unauthorised vessels are warned off by automated systems before any crew response.
hazards: Proximity to stellar body — radiation shielding critical at all times
Incomplete sections sealed but structurally uncertain, avoid unmarked approach vectors
Scale of the construct means maintenance hazards are distributed across enormous distances with long response times
Energy output from active collection arrays creates electromagnetic hazard zones along equatorial approach corridors

notable_locations.name: The Capture Array
notable_locations.desc: The functional ring of energy collection panels at close stellar orbit. Engineering that predates the Tronik War, substantially expanded and repaired by successive operators. The output figures are genuinely impressive. The original design documents are in the consortium archives and are studied by megascale engineering teams who want to understand how it was built with the tools available at the time.

notable_locations.name: The Sealed Sections
notable_locations.desc: Approximately 30% of the Dyson construct was never completed or was damaged beyond economic repair after the Tronik War. These sections have been sealed and are listed on approach charts as exclusion zones. The consortium's official position is that they are stable and pose no hazard. Survey teams who have approached the sealed sections describe structural states that do not match the official documentation.

hooks: The L.I.F.T.N. Dyson construct's incomplete sections are documented in consortium records as sealed and stable. An independent engineering survey commissioned by a Tronik Network trade authority and then abruptly cancelled produced a partial report, not officially released, that described structural deterioration in three sealed sections inconsistent with the maintenance logs. The trade authority says the survey was cancelled due to budget constraints. The engineering firm that conducted it has since dissolved.

The construct's original construction records, pre-Tronik War, reference a fourth ring section that does not appear on any current chart of the structure and is not accounted for in the sealed-section documentation. Whether it was never built, destroyed in the war, or is simply uncharted is not established.
planets.desc: A partial Dyson sphere — a ring section and associated collection arrays encircling the L.I.F.T.N. system star at close orbital distance. Begun by the original industrial consortium that named the system, damaged in the Tronik War, and partially repaired by successors. The functioning sections produce more power than current industrial operations require. The incomplete sections have been sealed and are not discussed in consortium public communications. The construct is one of the few megascale engineering structures in the Tronik Network that remained operational through the war, and the consortium considers it the centrepiece of the system's industrial identity.

systems.name: Niezh System
systems.desc: Niezh is the Tronik Network system with the most active post-war political dispute, multiple parties claim the system based on pre-war ownership, wartime alliance, and post-war settlement rights. The legal status has been contested for decades and has produced a community that lives under permanently ambiguous governance while various parties argue about who is in charge.

planets.name: Niezh
planets.atm_note: Standard breathable
planets.demographics: Mixed, the population reflects the overlapping claims, with communities identifying with different claimant factions
planets.government: Provisional Administration Council (compromise body, contested legitimacy)
planets.economy: Agriculture, services, moderate industry, all operations conducted under uncertain legal framework
planets.access_note: Open entry, but all operations in the system require navigating the competing legal frameworks, each of which has different implications for contracts, ownership, and liability.
hazards: Three overlapping legal systems, what is legal under one may be illegal under another
Community tensions between populations identifying with different claimants
All economic activity operates under the risk that the jurisdiction question resolves against the party you dealt with
Outside parties who get involved in the dispute tend to find it more complicated than initially presented

notable_locations.name: The Provisional Hall
notable_locations.desc: The Provisional Administration Council's seat, a compromise building on neutral ground that neither of the major claimant factions will admit to accepting. The administration it houses functions, somewhat. The question of what authority it rests on remains unanswered.

hooks: Observers of the Niezh jurisdiction dispute have documented multiple occasions where one claimant appeared to have made a legally decisive move, each time producing the same response from the other two claimants, who independently seek outside help to contest it from different directions simultaneously. The pattern has produced a situation where the dispute's resolution appears imminent at regular intervals and has never actually arrived, suggesting that the equilibrium serves all three claimants more than any resolution would.

The legal situation on Niezh has produced documented cases where the same physical asset is simultaneously owned by two different parties under two different claim frameworks, situations that cannot be resolved within any single jurisdiction and that produce a class of problems specific to Niezh which has attracted legal specialists from across the galaxy who treat the system as the most advanced available laboratory for multi-jurisdictional property law.
planets.desc: Niezh is governed by whoever is winning the current legal argument, which changes. The population has adapted to this by developing an exceptional facility for operating under ambiguous authority, Niezh's citizens are among the most legally sophisticated in the Network because they have had to be. The dispute will resolve eventually. Whether the resolution will be based on law, political force, or simple exhaustion is not clear.

systems.name: Monda System
systems.desc: Monda is the Tronik Network system that avoided the worst of the war by virtue of not being strategically significant. The fighting largely passed it by. What it has instead of war history is a long quiet, generations of ordinary life conducted in a region defined by extraordinary events that did not quite reach it. This has produced a community that is notably stable compared to its neighbours.

planets.name: Monda
planets.atm_note: Clean, the lack of war damage and industrial development has left Monda's atmosphere in good condition
planets.demographics: Mixed, stable community with low transient population relative to Network neighbours
planets.economy: Agriculture, small-scale manufacturing, services, trade with Network neighbours
planets.access_note: Open entry, Monda has no particular reason to restrict visitors and moderate commercial reasons to welcome them.
hazards: The quiet here attracts parties who want to conduct operations away from scrutiny
Stability is relative, the Network's instability is not far away
Resource limitations compared to systems with more industrial development

notable_locations.name: The Market Town
notable_locations.desc: Monda's primary commercial centre, the agricultural and trade hub of a system that built its economy on what grows in good soil. Nothing remarkable here by galactic standards. Entirely pleasant by local ones.

hooks: Monda's documented history of outside parties using its relative stability as a base for operations conducted elsewhere in the Tronik Network, and the community's consistent pattern of eventually identifying and removing these presences, is considered by political analysts who study the Network to be one of the clearest illustrations of how stability functions as both an asset and a liability for a system in an unstable region.

Monda's position as the swing vote in Network-wide political decisions is established and recurring, the system's lack of strong factional alignment means that parties seeking Network-wide consensus or opposition come to Monda, and the Council's practice of taking its time before committing is understood in the Network as a deliberate negotiating posture rather than genuine indecision.
planets.desc: Monda's stability in the Tronik Network is both its defining characteristic and its most valuable asset. A system that had the fortune not to be significant during the war and the subsequent good sense to stay uncontested is rare in this part of space. The community is aware of how unusual their situation is and is careful about it without being paranoid. It is, by the standards available in the Tronik Network, a good place to live.

systems.name: Conso System
systems.desc: Conso sits at the junction between the Tronik Network and System 5, the most strategically significant position in the Network and the reason the Alliance maintains a permanent garrison here. The Tronik War ended in part because of what happened at Conso, and the Alliance has never stopped treating its control of this system as non-negotiable.

planets.name: Conso
planets.atm_note: Standard, maintained to military specification in garrison zones
planets.demographics: Mixed, significant military population, civilian community supporting military presence
planets.economy: Military operations, strategic logistics, civilian support services, trade goods movement through the junction
planets.access_note: Civilian entry open with Alliance ID. Military zones restricted. All arrivals logged and assessed, the junction position means intelligence interest is high.
hazards: Alliance military presence is significant and permanently alert, mistakes are handled quickly
Intelligence operations from multiple parties active in the system due to strategic position
History of the war site produces periodic destabilisation events, veterans, revisionist groups, investigators
The junction position means what happens on Conso affects everything on both sides of it

notable_locations.name: Garrison Command
notable_locations.desc: The Alliance military headquarters for Tronik Network operations. Maintains permanent readiness posture. The strategic lessons of the Tronik War are institutionally embedded here.

notable_locations.name: The Junction Memorial
notable_locations.desc: The memorial to the Tronik War action at Conso, the engagement that effectively ended the war. Both sides have memorials. They are positioned at opposite ends of the city. Both are maintained carefully.

hooks: Veterans of the battle at Conso who maintain that the official account of the engagement is materially wrong are a persistent presence in the community on the station and in the Network more broadly, accounts that agree with each other in the specific ways they diverge from the official record, suggesting not confusion or memory failure but a specific set of events that the official account omits. The Alliance military's consistent position is that the official account is accurate and complete.

Transit log discrepancies at the Conso junction, cargo and vessels passing through that do not appear in official records, or that appear differently than what was actually transited, are documented in the records of independent operators who compare their own logs against filed records and have noted the gaps for years. The discrepancies are small enough individually to be attributed to clerical error and consistent enough collectively to require another explanation.
planets.desc: Conso is where the Tronik War ended and where the Alliance decided it would not start again. The garrison here is not symbolic, it is substantial, well-equipped, and maintains the readiness posture of a command that takes its strategic position seriously. Civilian life coexists with the military presence in the practical way that it does in systems where the military has been there for generations and the economy has built around it. The junction between the Network and System 5 has been Alliance-controlled since the war ended. The Alliance has shown no indication it intends to change this.
